headline_en: Fake job offers rife in the UAE: the country's 5 warnings to avoid fraud
perpetrator_type: brokers and fraud rings issuing fake job offers (general pattern)
trust_devices: fake job offer / appointment letter
verification_mentioned: UAE Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation (MOHRE): every genuine job offer issued through its system has a serial number and barcode; check it on the ministry's official website, the 'MOHRE UAE' mobile app, or by calling 600590000.
advice_or_warning_in_article: MOHRE's five warning signs (via Gulf News): (1) being asked to open a new bank account in your name as part of recruitment; (2) an unverified person or firm asking for confidential bank details; (3) being asked to pay a fee to secure the job or complete recruitment; (4) being asked to receive money into your account or transfer it onward; (5) insistence on contact only through WhatsApp or another messaging app with no official phone number or address. If any appears, stop and verify; make no payment and share no personal data until the offer is confirmed. Use only government and legal channels.
other_practical_details: No individual case. More than 2.6 million people contacted MOHRE channels for services and verification in July-September 2026.
key_quote_bn: নিয়োগপত্রের সত্যতা নিশ্চিত না হয়ে কোনো আর্থিক লেনদেন বা ব্যক্তিগত তথ্য দেওয়া যাবে না।

headline_en: They send people to Serbia for BDT 6 lakh and even give a visa; the fraud is caught at the airport
destination_promised: Serbia (also other European countries 'for little money'); job not specified
route_and_actual_destination: Stopped at the airport in Bangladesh; several were turned back
visa_type_claimed: Serbia visa (forged)
amount_total: Not stated. One middleman says he paid BDT 900,000 to a Dhaka agency for four relatives.
perpetrator_type: fraud ring with members across the country, a local intermediary and an unnamed Dhaka agency
perpetrator_names: Abdul Mabud of Satkania, Chattogram (arrested); Mamun Sheikh of Munshiganj (local man through whom passports and money were given; says he himself paid an unnamed Dhaka agency)
how_victim_met_them: Through a man from the victim's own area (Mamun Sheikh, Munshiganj)
trust_devices: a Serbia visa handed over after the passport was collected; when the visa failed at immigration, the ring blamed some other problem with the traveller
timeline: Money was taken before the visa was handed over; one victim was due to travel to Dhaka the day after the arrest
how_it_was_discovered: Airport immigration police check found the visa was forged
victims_count: 17 passports recovered; total not stated
harm: Money lost; turned back from the airport; passports held by the ring
official_response: Kotwali police (Chattogram) arrested Abdul Mabud at a hotel on Sunday 22 November 2026 and seized 17 passports and 5,000 forged Serbia visas; raids continue for other members (OC Zahedul Kabir).
money_recovered: None mentioned
verification_mentioned: Immigration police at the airport detect the forged visa; no earlier check is described.
advice_or_warning_in_article: OC Zahedul Kabir: the ring has members in Dhaka, Mymensingh, Munshiganj, Chattogram and across the country, taking money by promising Serbia and other European countries cheaply.
other_practical_details: The visa is given as a trust device after payment, so holding a visa sticker or printout proves nothing. A victim whose passport was among those seized had not heard of the arrest and was still preparing to travel. Being told after an airport offload that 'you had some other problem' is part of the script.
key_quote_bn: জাল ভিসা বিমানবন্দরে পুলিশের অভিবাসন শাখায় ধরা পড়লে চক্রের সদস্যরা ভুক্তভোগীর অন্য কোনো সমস্যা আছে বলে দাবি করেন।

headline_en: Flight in 10 days: quit his job, went on a trip to the Sundarbans, then learned the agency had vanished
destination_promised: Azerbaijan (jobs with a construction company; surveyor engineer post for some)
route_and_actual_destination: Never left Bangladesh
promised_job_and_wage: Surveyor engineer and other posts at 'Colin Construction' [কোলিন কনস্ট্রাকশন], Azerbaijan; wage not stated
visa_type_claimed: Azerbaijan work visa with appointment letter (both fake)
amount_per_person: BDT 80,000 to 350,000 (victims' accounts). Suman Reza paid BDT 130,000; Md Shimul was quoted BDT 250,000 and paid BDT 125,000. Plus BDT 5,000 each for the medical test.
amount_total: BDT 3,06,10,000 (about 3.06 crore) from 200 people, per the case filing
payment_method: Four instalments
how_money_was_raised: Loans and sale of cows and goats; one student borrowed BDT 200,000 from an NGO and now pays BDT 20,000 a month
perpetrator_type: agency office in a rented flat (called a recruiting agency in the article; no licence number given)
perpetrator_names: S Alam Overseas [এস আলম ওভারসিজ], 2nd floor, House 17 (Ma Nibash), Road 4, Sector 12, Uttara, Dhaka. Director Shafiqul Islam; manager Mehedi Hasan; assistant manager Mosharraf Hossain; marketing manager Masud Rana; receptionist Mili Akter.
trust_devices: office premises in Uttara; fake appointment letter from an Azerbaijan construction company; visa shown; online interviews conducted by foreigners; medical test at Sunmoon Medical Center Ltd, Banani; passport collection; staged payment in four steps; a flight date ('in 10 days', end of October)
timeline: Flat rented 4-5 months before it vanished; flights promised for end of October; receptionist phoned everyone on 23 October to say the firm had closed; case filed 24 October
how_it_was_discovered: On 23 October the receptionist phoned victims to say the company had closed and passports would be returned; victims went to the office and found only her there. They then learned the appointment letters and visas were fake.
victims_count: About 200 (Prothom Alo spoke to 23)
harm: Money lost, debt, jobs given up (Suman Reza resigned as a surveyor engineer on the agency's word and is now unemployed)
official_response: Case at Uttara West police station on 24 October listing 200 victims' passport numbers and amounts. Victims handed receptionist Mili Akter to police. Investigating officer SI Zillur Rahman: the director's NID was fake; efforts to arrest the others continue.
money_recovered: None mentioned; passports were to be returned
verification_mentioned: None described. Police found the director used a fake NID; the flat owner says they rented it with false statements.
other_practical_details: The medical centre's MD says S Alam sent 70-80 people and it charged BDT 2,500 each, while victims paid the agency BDT 5,000; the centre denies collusion and says it is owed about BDT 150,000. An office, a medical test, a foreigner on a video interview and a visa printout were all staged within a few months from a short-let flat. Victims were educated professionals (engineer, project workers, a master's student). Victims vandalised the office afterwards.
key_quote_bn: তারা ভিসা দেখিয়েছিল। এক পর্যায়ে তাদের বিশ্বাস করেছি। যার খেসারত এখন দিতে হচ্ছে।

headline_en: BDT 5 lakh paid to bring back son held hostage in Libya, still no trace; another 42 lakh demanded
destination_promised: Libya (purpose stated only as improving the family's finances)
route_and_actual_destination: Libya; held hostage by a trafficking ring
perpetrator_type: village broker and trafficking ring with Bangladeshis in Libya
perpetrator_names: Broker Sohel; arrested: Md Monowar Hossain (40) and Md Sohel Rana (45) of Chandpur village, Singra upazila, Natore; named as holding the victim in Libya: Mokarram and Anwar
how_victim_met_them: Went to Libya through Bangladeshi broker Sohel about two years ago
timeline: Went about two years ago; ransom call 5 August last year around noon; BDT 5 lakh sent 10-25 August; case filed 5 September last year; arrests Thursday 12 November 2026. Victim still untraced.
how_it_was_discovered: Phone call from a Libyan number to the victim's wife saying he was in their custody and would be killed unless BDT 30 lakh was paid
what_happened_abroad: Md Saiful (39) was taken hostage by a trafficking ring in Libya; the family has not been allowed to speak to him and his whereabouts are unknown.
harm: Victim missing in captivity; BDT 500,000 lost
ransom_details: BDT 30 lakh first demanded by phone from a Libyan number, with no contact allowed until half was paid. Family sent BDT 5 lakh in several transfers between 10 and 25 August from a bKash shop at Bamandanga Hall Mor, Sundarganj, to several mobile numbers supplied by the accused; no call with the son followed. A man named Sohel then promised to rescue him, called the wife to Kadamtali in Dhaka and switched off his phone. Then a further BDT 42 lakh was demanded from the 70-year-old father from another number. The father refused to pay more without speaking to his son directly; the calls stopped.
official_response: Father Abdus Samad filed a case at Sundarganj police station under the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act; transferred to CID, which arrested Monowar Hossain and Sohel Rana at Singra Bazar, Natore. CID is trying to locate the victim and identify other members.
money_recovered: None mentioned
advice_or_warning_in_article: CID: before going abroad, verify the legitimacy of the person, the agency, the visa and the employer.
other_practical_details: Ransom was collected inside Bangladesh through mobile banking numbers, and paying did not produce even a phone call. A second set of callers posing as rescuers demanded more. The family's leverage was refusing further payment without proof of life.
key_quote_bn: কথা ছিল, টাকা পেলেই ছেলের সঙ্গে কথা বলিয়ে দেওয়া হবে। কিন্তু টাকা নিয়েও কথা রাখেনি দালালেরা।

headline_en: AB Party's seven demands, including ending the syndicate for sending workers to Malaysia
amount_per_person: Government-set cost about BDT 79,000; workers going to Malaysia in 2022-2024 paid BDT 500,000-600,000 or more above that, according to published information cited by AB Party
perpetrator_type: syndicate of a limited number of recruiting agencies (not named)
harm: Excess migration cost and debt
official_response: None; AB Party (press conference, Monday 9 November 2026, Bijoynagar, Dhaka) demanded no syndicate when the Malaysia market reopens, full disclosure of recruitment costs, verification of employer, contract and nature of work for Russia and other risky markets, and fast, transparent BMET clearance for workers with legal European jobs and visas.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Raja Golam Rabbani, AB Party expatriate welfare secretary: all qualified licensed agencies should get equal opportunity; a syndicate of a few agencies must not be allowed.
other_practical_details: Political press conference; the only concrete migrant-relevant figures are the BDT 79,000 official Malaysia cost versus the 5-6 lakh or more actually charged in 2022-2024.
key_quote_bn: অথচ নির্ধারিত ব্যয় ছিল প্রায় ৭৯ হাজার টাকা।

headline_en: No clearance without ministry permission to send workers to 12 countries including Russia
destination_promised: Serbia, Moldova, Belarus, Congo, Russia, Japan, Iraq, Laos, Vietnam, Cambodia, Ukraine and Libya (the 12 countries covered)
perpetrator_type: recruiting agencies using fake appointment letters (allegation, not a named case)
trust_devices: fake appointment / demand letters; a visa; a job offer through a recruiting agency
what_happened_abroad: Pattern cited: in Cambodia, Laos, Vietnam and some other countries people lured by jobs were confined in scam compounds and forced into online fraud; in Russia many have ended up in the war.
official_response: On Wednesday 4 November 2026 the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare instructed the BMET Director General not to issue emigration clearance for the 12 countries without the ministry's recruitment permission or approval. BAIRA passed the instruction to all member agencies the same day.
verification_mentioned: Ministry recruitment permission plus BMET emigration clearance. Previously demand letters for up to seven workers needed no ministry permission, a gap allegedly used to send workers on fake appointment letters; now every demand letter needs prior approval.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Sector people: for these 12 countries, make no payment and no final decision until the appointment letter, ministry approval and emigration clearance are confirmed. Volunteers from migration organisations: a visa or a job offer through a recruiting agency is not proof of safe, legal migration; check the real job opportunity in the country, the employer's identity, the contract, pay, visa type and Bangladesh government approval.
other_practical_details: The 12-country list is a practical red-flag list for would-be migrants.
key_quote_bn: আগে সাতটি পর্যন্ত নিয়োগের চাহিদাপত্রের জন্য মন্ত্রণালয়ের অনুমতি লাগত না। এ সুযোগ কাজে লাগিয়ে নকল নিয়োগপত্র এনে কর্মী পাঠানোর নামে অভিযোগ আছে।

headline_en: UN finds evidence Bangladeshis were forced into Russia's war; brokers involved
destination_promised: Russia: civilian jobs such as security guard, driver, mechanic, electrician, construction worker, welder, repair worker, transport worker, technician; some offers in IT, medical, sports or agriculture
route_and_actual_destination: Russia, then front lines in Ukraine. Transit countries named in the UN report (all nationalities): Bahrain, Brazil, Ethiopia, France, Kenya, Mexico, Morocco, Oman, Panama, Spain, Turkey, UAE.
promised_job_and_wage: High salary, Russian citizenship, comfortable housing, pension after leaving the job (no figures)
visa_type_claimed: Business visas for the Bangladeshis (copies seen by the UN commission, citing an invitation from a Russian civilian company); for others short-term tourist visas or no visa needed
payment_method: Some paid in advance; others were told it would be deducted from wages later
perpetrator_type: recruitment agents and firms (local, regional or Russian nationals, often operating as travel or tourism businesses) coordinating with Russian authorities
how_victim_met_them: Social media advertisements, recruitment agents and firms; in some cases an acquaintance
trust_devices: photos or catalogues of housing; recruiters' assurances; reports from others who said they got the same job; the recruiting firm's government approval documents or local licence; a written guarantee that they would not be sent to the war (one group of 30); visas issued by the Russian embassy through the agents
timeline: Pressed to travel within days of agreeing; military contract signed within hours or days of arrival; training from 20 minutes to a few days, sometimes up to a month
how_it_was_discovered: At the airport in Russia: loss of free movement, temporary housing, then handover to the armed forces and a one-year military contract in Russian
what_happened_abroad: Made to sign one-year contracts with the Russian defence ministry written in Russian, which most could not read and could not translate because their phones had been taken. Refusal met with pressure, threats or torture (one recruit said four men were shot in front of him). Sent to dig trenches, guard, carry food and water, collect bodies, and assault forward positions. Many got no pay or little; bank cards taken by agents or military staff; accounts emptied or frozen. One group of 30 given a no-war guarantee: 17 killed, 5 missing, 1 returned wounded (nationality not given in the report).
victims_count: Citizens of 29 countries including Bangladesh; number of Bangladeshis not given in the report
harm: Death, injury, capture, disappearance, unpaid wages
official_response: Draft report of the UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on Ukraine published on the OHCHR site 26 October 2026; recommends Russia stop such recruitment, discharge trafficked persons and prosecute those involved. Russia rejects the commission's mandate. Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury: appointment letters for Russia are now checked much more closely and action against involved agencies has begun.
verification_mentioned: None that would have exposed it: the report notes some recruiting firms held local licences and showed government approval documents.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Selim Reza, coordinator, Centre for Migration Studies, North South University: the government keeps issuing clearances for Russia despite knowing of forced recruitment; it must act so that not one worker is deceived or forced into the war, and recover compensation and rescue those stuck.
other_practical_details: Warning signs from the UN findings: a 'job' on a business or tourist visa; pressure to fly within days; being told the work is under the military but civilian; being told to cross by road to a neighbouring country and fly from there to avoid being caught at the airport; a contract in Russian presented on arrival. A trafficked person who signed is legally a member of the Russian armed forces, not a mercenary, and is entitled to prisoner-of-war protection if captured.
key_quote_bn: চুক্তিগুলো রুশ ভাষায় লেখা ছিল। অধিকাংশ নিয়োগপ্রাপ্ত রুশ ভাষা জানতেন না।

headline_en: Death penalty for migrants in Saudi Arabia: 'they don't understand the language, get no lawyer, and the body doesn't come back'
destination_promised: Saudi Arabia (migrant work; no specific job)
route_and_actual_destination: Saudi Arabia; prisons named: Khamis Mushait, Najran, Tabuk
perpetrator_type: recruitment brokers and employers under the kafala system; people who coerced migrants into carrying drugs (pattern, per Amnesty)
timeline: Families may get at most 24 hours' notice by a phone call from the prisoner; some learn days later from other prisoners or the media
what_happened_abroad: Explainer based on Amnesty International and ESOHR reports. In 25 documented drug cases (Egyptians, Ethiopians, Jordanians, Pakistanis, Somalis) migrants went through the Saudi courts alone: they did not understand or receive the charges and court papers, had no professional interpreter, lawyer or consular help, and risked confessions taken without them. In two cases the accused said they had been forced to carry banned drugs, but the court did not examine or accept this. Amnesty also documents migrants in Saudi Arabia cheated by recruitment brokers, forced to work excess hours and robbed of wages. Bodies were not returned and grave locations not disclosed. Two Bangladeshis were recently executed for an 'immoral act' in a mosque in Mecca.
victims_count: 59 foreigners among 108 executed in Jan-Jun 2026 (ESOHR), Bangladeshis among them (number unknown); 597 executed for drug offences Jan 2014-Jun 2025, about 75% foreigners (Amnesty); two Bangladeshis executed recently in Mecca
harm: Execution after trials without interpreter, lawyer or consular access; bodies withheld from families; families lose their main earner
official_response: UN human rights experts and the UN Committee on the Elimination of Racial Discrimination (Dec 2024) raised concerns and called for a moratorium; Amnesty demands an independent, transparent investigation. No Bangladeshi government action is described.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Amnesty: migrants' vulnerability starts at home with deceptive recruitment and continues under kafala; lack of money, education and Arabic makes effective defence nearly impossible. IOM risk factors for Saudi-bound migrants: irregular migration; hidden work such as domestic work, work at sea or the informal sector; undue employer control; recruitment corruption; dependence on third-party brokers; gaps in state protection. IOM guidance: being forced into illegal activity through deception or coercion counts as human trafficking.
other_practical_details: Drug offences carry the death penalty in Saudi Arabia: 49 of 71 drug executions in Jan-Jun 2026 were of foreigners. Saudi Arabia's 2013 criminal procedure law gives the right to legal help at investigation and trial and bans torture, but ESOHR found prisoners without interpreters or lawyers, and many did not know when their sentence was upheld or their pardon plea rejected. Saudi law has no clear rule to notify the prisoner or family before execution and does not guarantee return of the body. About 2.5 million Bangladeshis work in Saudi Arabia, the largest foreign group. ESOHR could document nothing before execution in 91 of the 108 cases, so nothing is known about Bangladeshi prisoners' numbers, charges or access to lawyers, interpreters and consular help.

headline_en: Went to Cambodia hoping for a good job; passport seized and 'sold' for USD 5,000
route_and_actual_destination: Cambodia; sold to a scam centre
amount_per_person: About BDT 600,000 each
perpetrator_type: human trafficking ring (Bangladeshi members arrested in Dhaka)
perpetrator_names: Md Shaon Molla (23) and Md Sakib Sarkar (26), both from Pubail, Gazipur; arrested in Paltan, Dhaka
timeline: After release they stayed about two months in a local hotel in Cambodia; returned to Bangladesh 3 September; case filed 26 October; arrests 27 October 2026
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Cambodia their passports were taken and they were sold to a scam centre
what_happened_abroad: Passports seized on arrival; 'sold' for USD 5,000 to a scam centre; forced to do online fraud; physical and mental torture for refusing or for small mistakes; no way to leave. After ransom was paid the traffickers still kept them under control and took more money for the air ticket home.
harm: About BDT 600,000 each lost, plus ransom and ticket money; confinement, torture, forced crime
ransom_details: After being sold, a further USD 5,000 ransom was demanded from their families for release, and the families paid; ransom was taken in several rounds, and money was collected again for the return air ticket. Payment method not stated.
official_response: Case at Paltan police station on 26 October naming Shaon Molla and Sakib Sarkar; CID arrested both on 27 October; investigation continuing.
money_recovered: None mentioned
other_practical_details: They got home with online help from BRAC Migration Centre. Bangladeshis are taken to Cambodia in the name of call-centre jobs and then made to run online scams. BMET: 12,263 Bangladeshis took clearance for Cambodia in 2025 (8th largest destination); 646 returned in June after Cambodian raids closed scam centres. Sector people quoted: Cambodia's economy is no better than Bangladesh's and jobs are few, yet workers are sent for the scam centres.
key_quote_bn: এরপর পাঁচ হাজার মার্কিন ডলারে ‘বিক্রি’ করে দেওয়া হয় একটি স্ক্যাম সেন্টারে।

headline_en: Tough diplomatic and legal steps are needed (editorial)
route_and_actual_destination: Russia; Russia-Ukraine front line
how_money_was_raised: High-interest loans and sale of homestead land
perpetrator_type: recruiting agencies and broker rings
what_happened_abroad: Instead of promised jobs, young Bangladeshis pushed to the front and used as 'bait'; 54 deaths in three years per Prothom Alo's reporting; some maimed in hospital.
victims_count: 54 deaths in three years (Prothom Alo count cited)
harm: Deaths, disability, bodies not returned, families pressed by lenders
official_response: Editorial says no exemplary legal action against the agencies or brokers has been visible; calls for punishment under the human trafficking law (not just licence cancellation), compensation for families, full attestation of job letters and clearance for Russia, and tighter airport monitoring.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Prothom Alo editorial: unlicensed or accused agencies repeatedly change names and routes to send workers to uncertain destinations; traffickers now also use AI, deepfakes, social media and cryptocurrency to trap people.
other_practical_details: Editorial, no new case facts.
key_quote_bn: কিন্তু প্রতিশ্রুত চাকরির বদলে তাঁদের ঠেলে দেওয়া হয়েছে রাশিয়া-ইউক্রেন যুদ্ধের ময়দানে।

headline_en: 'If we don't meet in this world, we'll meet on Judgment Day': bodies of Bangladeshis killed in Russia never come home
destination_promised: Russia; work in a construction company (high-paid job)
route_and_actual_destination: Flew Dhaka to Russia on 7 May 2026; kept four days in a hotel, made to sign a paper, sent to an army camp, 21 days of training, then to the front line of the Russia-Ukraine war
promised_job_and_wage: Construction company job with high pay; exact wage not stated
visa_type_claimed: Valid visa, job contract and required papers (per BRAC research on the pattern); BMET clearance taken in the name of TS Overseas
amount_per_person: about BDT 1,000,000 on average
how_money_was_raised: Not specified; Mamun's family is described as debt-ridden
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency working through brokers
perpetrator_names: Jabale Noor International (জাবালে নূর; Khilkhet, Dhaka), founder Mizanur Rahman; Abu Taher alias Lentu; RS International (Ashulia); TS Overseas / TS Group (clearances were taken in its name). Separately named: Bonna Bijoy Overseas (বন্যা বিজয় ওভারসিজ), managing director Barun Debnath, took the most Russia clearances.
how_victim_met_them: Through brokers (families' letters to the ministry say they went 'through a broker'; Rajon paid a broker)
trust_devices: valid visa; job contract; BMET clearance; licensed agencies; group departure of 30 from Dhaka; agency promised families it would take responsibility when they called before deployment
timeline: 7 May 2026 departure; 4 days in hotel; 21 days training; sent to the front in groups of 16, 8 and 6 in June; many died around 12-13 June; families lost contact from the first week of June; Adnan spent two months in hospital and returned 15 Sep 2026; arrests 13 Oct 2026. Mamun's family had had no proof of death five months on.
how_it_was_discovered: After four days in a hotel in Russia the men were made to sign a paper and taken to an army camp. On 18 May a worker's family phoned the embassy to say the 30 were being sent to war. Workers pleaded with their families by phone before being deployed.
what_happened_abroad: No promised job; handed to the Russian army ('sold', per families' letters). After 21 days of training they were sent to the front, where, according to SRB, intelligence and others, untrained Bangladeshis are pushed forward as bait so that Ukrainian drone strikes reveal enemy positions. SRB has information that at least 20 of the 30 died. Dead foreigners' bodies are left on the field. Abdullah Al Mamun (Lalmonirhat) phoned his brother the day before deployment and is reported dead by fellow recruit Al Amin. Adnan Hossain (Narayanganj) took shrapnel in the stomach, had three operations in a Moscow hospital, escaped to the embassy after two months and came home on a travel pass. Rajon Hossain (21, Jhenaidah) was sent to the front with five other Bangladeshis; four died in a drone strike; he was injured, escaped from hospital and returned. Md Palash Sheikh was injured, sent back to fight, lost a hand and is under army guard in a Moscow hospital, unable to leave.
victims_count: 30 in this group (at least 20 reported dead by SRB); Prothom Alo has reports of at least 54 deaths in three years; Russia has informed the embassy about 40 dead or missing Bangladeshis
harm: At least 20 deaths reported, no bodies returned, no death proof so no compensation; serious injuries (lost hand, abdominal shrapnel); about BDT 1,000,000 each lost; families in debt
official_response: SRB (Special Response Battalion) arrested Mizanur Rahman and Abu Taher alias Lentu on 13 Oct 2026 and held a press conference on 14 Oct. The Expatriates' Welfare Ministry cancelled the licences of Jabale Noor, TS Overseas and RS International and locked Bonna Bijoy's server so it can take no new clearances. CID sources say at least six cases have been filed over trafficking to Russia. The embassy's labour wing wrote to the ministry on 25 May saying it had not attested Jabale Noor's 5 May request for 70 workers, had suspended RS International's 10 workers on suspicion, and that the two agencies sent the workers under TS Overseas' name; it was writing to Russia's foreign ministry to return the men to the contracted work. Ambassador Md Nazrul Islam says Russia claims the 30 went to war voluntarily with written proof and is not handing over bodies. Families submitted 28 separate letters to the ministry in July asking for rescue and financial help.
money_recovered: None; Palash Sheikh's family received no money at all after spending BDT 1,000,000
verification_mentioned: Embassy attestation of the job demand: the embassy in Russia refused or suspended attestation for these agencies, and the workers were sent anyway under another agency's clearance. Two of the three agencies' names were not found in the BMET database. Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury: no clearance is now given without verification and attestation of a confirmed job.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury: the government discourages going this way; no clearance without verified, attested job information; many go via other countries; all embassies have been alerted. Shariful Hasan (head of BRAC Migration Programme): agencies accused of trafficking are sending the most workers to Russia; nobody knows how many got jobs or where the rest are; families get neither body nor compensation; he advises opening a hotline and listing the missing. Adnan (survivor): Russia does not publish Bangladeshi deaths or return bodies; anyone who does not come back from the front is declared missing, and missing means dead. Ambassador Nazrul Islam: over 90% of workers go to war of their own accord.
other_practical_details: The paper signed in the hotel preceded transfer to the army camp; Russia says it holds written proof of voluntary enlistment. Lure for those who enlist knowingly: Russian citizenship after six months at war and BDT 300,000-400,000 a month. Compensation from Russia is possible if someone dies or is missing over six months, but the heir must prove inheritance and stay in Russia at least six months; bodies cannot be recovered. Wage Earners' Welfare Board: brings a dead worker's body home at its cost if the worker had BMET clearance or embassy membership registration (otherwise the family can still apply and the ministry pays); BDT 35,000 cash for burial, BDT 300,000 grant, plus life insurance; no application has come from Russia because there is no proof of death. BMET clearances for Russia: 37 (2023), 1,395 (2024), 4,725 (2025), 3,105 to 15 Oct 2026; 93 agencies took Russia clearances in four years; Bonna Bijoy Overseas alone took 27% (about 2,500) and faces trafficking allegations and a case over Algeria; TS Overseas took 266; state agency BOESL took 771 (second highest) for three Russian companies, two of which stopped hiring after one worker fled with a vehicle and one joined the war. BRAC research (Nov 2025): the deception starts in Bangladesh; the men left with valid visas, contracts and papers.

headline_en: The family's last hope: Pabitra may still be alive
route_and_actual_destination: Russia on 7 May; hotel for some days, then handed to the Russian army and sent to the Russia-Ukraine front
promised_job_and_wage: Construction company job (wage not stated)
amount_per_person: About BDT 1,000,000 (10 lakh) on average. Pabitra Chandra raised BDT 130,000 plus BDT 950,000.
how_money_was_raised: Pabitra: wife's gold jewellery sold for BDT 130,000 and BDT 950,000 borrowed from an NGO and local moneylenders. Robin Mir: sold village land and livestock and took loans.
perpetrator_type: recruiting agencies
perpetrator_names: Jabale Noor, RS International and TS Group (as named by SRB)
trust_devices: told in the hotel that work would be given once papers were sorted; good food and sightseeing for the first 3-4 days
timeline: Arrived 7 May; in contact for a few days from a hotel; Robin Mir said on 15 May they were being taken to work; seen in an army camp video on 17 May; on 29 May both men phoned to say they were being forced to war. 21 days' training; 17 died in a drone strike on the first day at the front.
how_it_was_discovered: Phone calls on 29 May from the men themselves; a 17 May video showing Robin Mir in an army camp
what_happened_abroad: Passports and mobile phones taken; handed to the Russian army; 21 days of military training; sent to the front. Of 30: 17 killed by drone on the first day, 3 more later, 2 wounded in Russian hospitals (Palash Sheikh, Ali Hasan Sohel), 2 returned (Rajon Hossain, Adnan Hossain), 6 still at the front digging bunkers and carrying food, water and weapons. Sourav Molla tried to escape twice and failed.
victims_count: 30 (20 reported dead)
victim_home_districts: Tangail (Gopalpur), Narayanganj (Siddhirganj), Gopalganj, Lalmonirhat, Madaripur, Kishoreganj
harm: 20 deaths reported, none officially confirmed to families; families hounded by lenders; Pabitra's wife has had a mental breakdown; family considering selling its last 3 decimals of land, which still would not clear the debt
official_response: SRB press conference on 14 October. Pabitra had asked the Bangladesh embassy to bring them home. Families held a human chain in Dhaka. No official confirmation of deaths from the embassy or government.
money_recovered: None mentioned
other_practical_details: Victims were a carpenter and an auto-rickshaw driver from low-income families. The pattern: a few comfortable days in a hotel, 'papers being processed', then loss of phone and passport and transfer to a camp. The six still at the front keep contact through the imo app. The article names 18 of the dead.

headline_en: 1,800 workers cheated in Cambodia; government help sought to bring them back
route_and_actual_destination: Cambodia; ended up in online scam compounds
visa_type_claimed: Many went with valid passport, visa and government (BMET) clearance, per the NGO's press release
perpetrator_type: not specified (recruiters / trafficking ring; scam compound operators)
trust_devices: valid passport and visa; government emigration clearance
what_happened_abroad: Instead of the promised job, forced to work in online scam compounds. Victims and families allege deceptive recruitment, coercion, intimidation, restricted movement, passports withheld, physical and mental torture, and money demanded for release.
victims_count: More than 1,800 stranded; Cambodian authorities accepted a list of 1,797 for fine-waived return; over 400 more missed the application deadline
harm: Forced scam work, confinement, passport confiscation, torture, ransom demands; stranded with overstay fines
ransom_details: Money demanded in exchange for release (amount not stated)
official_response: Anirban Survivor Voice Foundation (survivor-led anti-trafficking group) filed an application with the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare on Sunday 18 Oct 2026, copied to the Foreign and Home ministries and the Wage Earners' Welfare Board, asking for special flights, help with travel documents, prosecution of traffickers and rehabilitation. Cambodia has announced closure of all scam centres and set a general-amnesty deadline of 31 October to leave.
verification_mentioned: The NGO says cases of people who went with valid government clearance should be reviewed to find gaps in employer verification, workplace inspection, job contract, wage, housing and destination-risk assessment.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Al Amin, president of Anirban Survivor Voice Foundation: sending citizens abroad legally is not enough; their safety, rights and dignity must also be ensured.
other_practical_details: Going with a valid visa and BMET clearance did not protect people from ending up in Cambodian scam compounds. Cambodia's amnesty waives overstay fines for those on the list accepted via the Bangladesh embassy notice.

trust_devices: real news twisted: Australia's 17 September announcement of faster processing for farm-sector visas; half-true claim that anyone aged 18 to 30 can apply
verification_mentioned: A granted Australian visa has a grant number that can be checked on the Australian government's VEVO service (author says check further even if it shows there). Anyone giving Australian immigration advice must be registered and should be able to show a registered migration agent number
advice_or_warning_in_article: Author (Kawsar Khan, registered Australian migration consultant): there is no direct agriculture visa for Bangladeshis; the whole trade is fraud. End the conversation if someone cannot show a registered migration professional number, cannot state the visa subclass and details, or promises a 'visa in ten days'. BMET and the Bangladesh High Commission in Canberra should issue clear warnings
other_practical_details: Farm workers reach Australia mainly through the Pacific Australia Labour Mobility (PALM) scheme, open only to nine Pacific island countries and Timor-Leste (Fiji, Kiribati, Nauru, Papua New Guinea, Samoa, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, Vanuatu); its official website says no money or gift is needed to join and the employer pays the airfare up front. India joined the working holiday list in 2024 through a trade deal, by lottery. Legal routes for Bangladeshis: student visa, skilled migration, employer-nominated work visa (Skills in Demand, subclass 482, since December 2024), needing a listed occupation, proof of skill, experience, English and an eligible sponsor. No route exists for fruit picking or field clearing from Bangladesh
key_quote_bn: বাংলাদেশিদের জন্য অস্ট্রেলিয়ায় সরাসরি কোনো কৃষি ভিসা নেই।

headline_en: Up to BDT 4 million taken from jobless youths and women who were never sent to Europe, and tortured
route_and_actual_destination: Told they would go via Serbia and Belarus to Italy. In practice sent first to countries in Asia and the Middle East, then via Nepal or Sri Lanka to Egypt or Libya, with the promise of a risky sea crossing to Europe. Some stranded abroad; several women still stuck in Egypt
promised_job_and_wage: High-paid jobs in Europe; no figure
visa_type_claimed: Visas were shown or supplied; SRB also alleges forged visas and documents
amount_per_person: BDT 2,000,000 to 2,500,000, in some cases up to BDT 4,000,000
amount_total: About BDT 8,500,000 from one group (two women plus Parvez, Firoz and Mehedi Hasan). One bank account of the accused showed BDT 17,075,450 in transactions over the past year
payment_method: Bank account transactions found; otherwise not stated
perpetrator_type: unlicensed agency or travel office
perpetrator_names: Mohammad Arzur Rahman (47), arrested in Banani C Block, Dhaka; firms named: 'Arzu Immigration Limited' and 'Nafis Air Immigration Limited' (unlicensed, per SRB)
trust_devices: visas shown or supplied; company names styled as immigration firms; forged visas and documents
timeline: Accused said to have operated for about 12 years. A victim, Kamrun Nahar, contacted NSI on 16 July; arrest on a Monday in late September
how_it_was_discovered: Victims found themselves stranded or confined in transit countries; one victim's request for help to NSI started the investigation
what_happened_abroad: Some women were forced into 'immoral work'; those who refused were held hostage, beaten and burned with cigarettes. Victims in Egypt escaped and sent video messages describing torture
victims_count: More than 2,000 by SRB's preliminary estimate; 30 to 35 contacted SRB after the arrest; about 300 more in contact with NSI
harm: Large sums lost, confinement, physical and sexual abuse, women still stranded in Egypt
official_response: Arrested by Special Response Battalion (SRB-4 and SRB-1) on NSI information and handed to the police station concerned; investigation continues to identify associates. Ministry working to bring back women stuck in Egypt. SRB says 223 people were arrested for trafficking from 2025 to date
verification_mentioned: SRB says the firms he used were unlicensed
other_practical_details: Targets were unemployed young men across the country and women from remote areas. The stated route kept changing after departure. Same case as the two women's account published the same day
key_quote_bn: ইউরোপে পাঠানোর কথা বলে জনপ্রতি ২০ থেকে ২৫ লাখ টাকা এবং কোনো কোনো ক্ষেত্রে ৪০ লাখ টাকা পর্যন্ত নেওয়া হতো

headline_en: Burned with cigarettes, filmed and threatened: account of two women trafficked abroad
route_and_actual_destination: Bangladesh to Egypt, where they were told the Italian embassy process would be completed; they never left Egypt
visa_type_claimed: Italian visa to be arranged through the Italian embassy in Egypt; never issued
amount_per_person: First woman per the account: BDT 600,000 then USD 1,000 (about BDT 700,000 in all). Other woman: BDT 1,100,000 then USD 3,000
payment_method: Not stated; the dollars were taken from them in Egypt
how_money_was_raised: Not stated; they describe themselves as poor and say the money was hard to gather
perpetrator_type: agency or travel office (licence status not stated in article)
perpetrator_names: Mohammad Arzu Rahman (47), arrested in Banani, Dhaka
trust_devices: good behaviour at first; claim that the route was legal; claim that paperwork would be done at the Italian embassy in Egypt; promise that the visa would come within a week of paying the dollars
timeline: Held about one and a half years in Egypt
how_it_was_discovered: After arrival in Egypt: passports and phones taken, locked in a room; no visa came after the extra dollars were paid; when they asked to be taken to the embassy they were beaten
what_happened_abroad: Locked in a house for months. Outside men were brought in to assault them; pressure to do 'immoral work'; beaten and burned with cigarettes when they refused. The abuse was filmed and they were threatened that the videos would be posted on social media. They overheard that they would be sold elsewhere. They escaped one night when the house was empty, leaving passports and phones, took shelter in another house and contacted family and the Bangladesh embassy
victims_count: 2 in this account; they say many more women are held in Egypt
harm: About BDT 700,000 and BDT 1,100,000 plus USD 3,000 lost; about 18 months' confinement; torture; passports still with the traffickers; continuing threats to them and their families using photos and videos
official_response: Arzu Rahman arrested by SRB on NSI information and handed to police; families filed complaints in Bangladesh; the women contacted the Bangladesh embassy and are waiting to return
money_recovered: None; they are asking the government to recover their money
other_practical_details: Pattern stated by the article: Italy is the bait, money is taken for visa and papers, and the destination changes once the person is out of Bangladesh. Fear for family honour kept them silent for a long time. The women sent their account by video to NSI from a hidden shelter in Egypt
key_quote_bn: আমরা বলছি, আমাদের এম্বাসিতে দাঁড় করান। এই কথা বলার পর আবার মারা শুরু করছে।

headline_en: Chances to stay in Australia are narrowing: what should Bangladeshis do now?
destination_promised: Australia (study, then stay on and work)
visa_type_claimed: Visitor visa to be converted to a student visa onshore; student visa renewed by enrolling in a cheap private college
how_money_was_raised: Families sell land or break savings to send students
perpetrator_type: unlicensed agency or travel office (education/visa agencies in Dhaka and other cities; none named)
trust_devices: flashy advertising
harm: Risk described: tuition and living costs with no route to stay; about 77,000 visa overstayers to be identified and removed
official_response: Australian immigration and home affairs minister Tony Burke announced: new international students and graduate visa holders can no longer bring spouses or children (PhD researchers exempt; families already there are not split); 'visa hopping' to a lower-level course is banned; a mandatory 'no further stay' condition on visitor visas; 100 new border force officers to remove overstayers
advice_or_warning_in_article: Author (Kawsar Khan, Prothom Alo Sydney correspondent and immigration lawyer): stop trusting agents who say 'get to Australia any way first, sort it out later'; the days of buying years through visa changes or appeals are over. Those whose real aim is only to work or to live with family should not come under the current rules. Aim for in-demand fields: construction engineering, nursing, health care, specialised teaching, technical trades
other_practical_details: Opinion column, no individual victim. Agency claims now false: 'you can go on a visit visa and become a student', and 'once in, you can enrol in some private college and keep renewing the visa'
key_quote_bn: ভ্রমণ ভিসায় গিয়ে শিক্ষার্থী হওয়া যায়

headline_en: Laos stops new work permits and labour visas for Bangladeshis
destination_promised: Laos (workers mainly in construction and manufacturing)
visa_type_claimed: Labour visa LA-B2 (approvals for Bangladeshis stopped until the end of 2026)
perpetrator_type: unauthorised labour suppliers; employers who bring workers and evade responsibility (as described by the Lao ministry)
harm: Article notes allegations that Bangladeshis in Laos have been drawn into crime and tortured; no case detail
official_response: Lao Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare directive of 9 September: new work permits, labour import plans and labour project approvals for Bangladeshis suspended from 1 September to the end of 2026, citing illegal entry, human trafficking, unauthorised labour suppliers and employers evading responsibility. Bangladesh's expatriates' welfare minister said he had no formal information yet
other_practical_details: Source: The Laotian Times, 14 September. No person, company, employer or labour supplier may on its own bring Bangladeshis into Laos or hire them. Large government-approved priority projects with contract work schedules are exempt. Fines: employer LAK 2.5 million (USD 110) per worker brought or hired without approval; LAK 2 million (USD 89) for using a worker assigned to another unit; worker LAK 1 million (USD 44) for working outside the assigned workplace and sent home within 30 days at the employer's or violator's cost; triple for repeat offences. About 3,000 BMET clearances for Laos in the first eight months of this year and 3,835 last year. Any new Laos work visa offer in this period falls under the suspension
key_quote_bn: লাওসে বাংলাদেশিদের নিয়ে অপরাধে যুক্ত করাসহ নির্যাতনের অভিযোগ আছে।

headline_en: Call to cut migration costs in the Malaysia labour market
perpetrator_type: syndicate of recruiting agencies (alleged by speakers; none named)
harm: Speakers: a ring extracts extra money through the whole sending process; because of excessive migration cost many workers cannot recover their loan money even after several years abroad
advice_or_warning_in_article: AB Party demands: no money beyond the government-set migration cost; all payments through banks or approved digital channels; register and monitor brokers, sub-agents and digital intermediaries; publish how many workers each agency sends and how much it charges; cancel licences and blacklist agencies where fraud or harassment is proven
other_practical_details: Open discussion at Dhaka Reporters Unity organised by AB Party; speakers included ICB chairman Abu Ahmed and BNP vice chairman Asaduzzaman Ripon. No individual case or amount given
key_quote_bn: অতিরিক্ত অভিবাসন ব্যয়ের কারণে অনেক শ্রমিক বিদেশে গিয়ে কয়েক বছরেও ঋণের টাকা তুলতে পারেন না।

headline_en: Taken to Russia for an electrician's job, sent to the battlefield, and then...
route_and_actual_destination: Flew to Russia 7 May, arrived 8 May; taken to an army camp, then to the front line near the Ukraine border
promised_job_and_wage: Electrician; BDT 150,000 a month (claim of a relative, for all 30)
visa_type_claimed: Work visa (all 30 had visas, BMET cards and police clearance, per a survivor)
amount_per_person: About BDT 850,000
how_money_was_raised: BDT 50,000 NGO loan; about BDT 400,000 advance (dadon) against the paddy crop; the rest borrowed from relatives and from selling cattle
perpetrator_type: recruiting agency (licence status not stated); brokers
perpetrator_names: Jabal-e-Noor International Limited (‘জাবাল-এ নূর ইন্টারন্যাশনাল লিমিটেড’)
how_victim_met_them: Not stated; his wife's aunt, Mosammat Kobila Akter, was involved in arranging it
trust_devices: visa issued through an agency; BMET card; police clearance; group of 30 travelling on the same flight
timeline: Papers submitted about two years before; visa came after a long wait; left 7 May; contract signed 12 May; sent to the front 12 June; 17 killed on 14 June; last audio message from Mamun 19 August; family told of his death in September
how_it_was_discovered: On 12 May in Russia they were made to sign a contract in Russian, told it was for a bank card, SIM card and work permit. They could not read it and later learned it was a contract to join the Russian army
what_happened_abroad: Taken to an army camp, trained, sent to the front on 12 June. On 14 June a drone attack and mine blasts killed 17 of the 30, per survivor Rajon Hossain. Al Mamun was killed by a Ukrainian drone about two weeks before the family was told; the news came via a Russian-speaking commander who had acted as interpreter. Rajon was injured, fled hospital, reached the Bangladesh embassy on 18 August and came home on 23 August
victims_count: 30 on the same flight; at least 17 killed, several missing
victim_home_districts: Mymensingh (Nandail upazila, Kharua village); Jhenaidah (Kaliganj upazila, Goyeshpur village)
harm: Death of Al Mamun (24) and at least 16 others; survivor injured; family left with about BDT 850,000 of debt; body not returned and place of death unknown
official_response: Family contacted the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry after learning of the Russian contract and were assured Bangladeshis would not be sent to war; repeated visits to the ministry and a police station brought only assurances. Nandail UNO told the family to submit a written application, to be sent through the Deputy Commissioner's expatriate welfare branch to the ministry. No case or arrest reported
verification_mentioned: None that worked: the survivor says all 30 held visas, BMET cards and police clearance
other_practical_details: The trick was a Russian-language document presented as paperwork for a bank card, SIM and work permit. Survivor Rajon Hossain returned with the help of the Bangladesh ambassador in Russia after going to the embassy himself
key_quote_bn: আমার ছেলেকে যে দালাল বেইচা দিছে, এই দালালের বিচার চাই।

headline_en: A recruiting agency's office sealed and fined
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency
perpetrator_names: Triple A Overseas (‘ত্রিপল এ ওভারসিজ’), RL-2630
trust_devices: licensed agency office
how_it_was_discovered: Special mobile court run by the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry, led by a BMET executive magistrate
harm: Workers' passports held by the agency (three boxes), collected against the rules for Malaysia while that market was not yet open
official_response: Office sealed, fined BDT 50,000, three boxes of passports seized into BMET custody; further legal action against the agency under way. Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury promised zero tolerance
money_recovered: Passports to be returned to their owners through a legal process; no mention of money
advice_or_warning_in_article: Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury: no dishonest or illegal recruiting agency will be allowed to cheat ordinary people
other_practical_details: Having an RL number did not stop the agency collecting passports for Malaysia before any official recruitment had opened. Number of workers and any money taken not stated

headline_en: Who will stop the fraud of digital brokers in the name of going abroad?
destination_promised: Saudi Arabia ('free visa' jobs advertised on Facebook); also Malaysia factory jobs, Europe/Italy
promised_job_and_wage: Ads typically promise 'free visa', 'guaranteed job', 'salary of BDT 1 lakh a month'
visa_type_claimed: 'Free visa' for Saudi Arabia; many later learned their visa was not a work permit at all
amount_per_person: About BDT 400,000 to 600,000 each (several hundred aspirants from Munshiganj and Cumilla, Saudi 'free visa')
payment_method: Mobile financial services (pattern described: contact on Facebook, bargaining on WhatsApp, money sent by mobile banking)
how_money_was_raised: General pattern: land sale, pawning jewellery, high-interest loans
perpetrator_type: online contact (Facebook pages, WhatsApp numbers, self-styled 'recruitment consultant', 'visa processing expert', 'overseas job solution', 'official representative' of a foreign firm); sub-agents
how_victim_met_them: Facebook ads and pages, WhatsApp and imo groups, YouTube videos
trust_devices: employer's logo in the ad; forged signatures; fake appointment letters; photos and videos of 'successful' workers abroad; testimonials; pages with thousands of followers; YouTube videos showing an easy route to Europe
how_it_was_discovered: Many found out later that the visa they held was not a work permit
victims_count: Several hundred from Munshiganj and Cumilla (Saudi 'free visa'); thousands cheated over Malaysia jobs in the past five years, per the author
victim_home_districts: Munshiganj, Cumilla; Brahmanbaria (Nabinagar upazila, Kamrul Hasan)
harm: Money lost; in the Russia case, forced signing of a contract to fight in Ukraine
official_response: 2024 amendment to the Overseas Employment and Migrants Act brought sub-agents and intermediaries under the law; a 2025 code of conduct also covers sub-agents; over 2,000 recruiting agencies are on the Recruitment Agents Information System (RAIMS)
verification_mentioned: No public check exists for an online job ad. Author proposes a unique government ID for every overseas job ad, checkable on a government platform (employer, wage, visa type, total cost, responsible agency)
advice_or_warning_in_article: Author (Dr Selim Reza, North South University): digital brokers charge under new labels such as 'registration', 'visa processing' and 'document verification'. Evidence is hard to keep: chats get deleted, payment numbers are switched off, pages vanish overnight. IOM warning cited: fake online job ads can be the first door to trafficking and forced criminality
other_practical_details: Opinion column summarising reported cases. Other case: Kamrul Hasan of Nabinagar, Brahmanbaria was cheated by one broker after reaching Russia; a second broker took BDT 500,000 promising to send him on to Italy, then handed him to the Russian army where he was made to sign a contract to fight in Ukraine (family's allegation). The digital broker has no signboard, no visible trade licence, sometimes not even a real name
key_quote_bn: পরে অনেকেই জানতে পারেন, তাঁদের ভিসা আসলে কাজের অনুমতিই নয়।

headline_en: Big Middle East labour markets have shrunk; fraud in the name of new markets
destination_promised: Russia; cook's job in a cantonment (army base)
route_and_actual_destination: Sent to Russia, then directly to the front line of the war with Ukraine
promised_job_and_wage: Cook in a cantonment; wage not stated
trust_devices: job described as cooking, not fighting
timeline: Sent to Russia in 2025 ('last year'); returned to Bangladesh after seven months, of which two months were in hospital
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival: instead of kitchen work he was handed a weapon without training and sent to the front
what_happened_abroad: Jahangir Alam of Lakshmipur was given a weapon with no training, then taught to use it for one day. 16 Bangladeshis were together in the war camp; four died. He fell ill, spent two months in hospital, escaped from there and returned home through the Bangladesh embassy.
victims_count: 16 Bangladeshis in his camp (4 of them died); article also cites 34 Bangladeshis killed out of 100+ who fought for Russia (Fortify Rights and Truth Hounds, March 2026)
harm: Forced into combat; four of his group of 16 killed; illness and two months in hospital
official_response: Returned through the Bangladesh embassy. General: CID anti-trafficking unit (THB) says 1,657 people were charged in 536 cases in 2018-2025 but only 353 arrested; Home Ministry says 94-95% of accused in 4,427 cases under the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act (2020-24) were acquitted. In July 2026 the government withdrew the licences of 49 recruiting agencies after a charge sheet in a Malaysia recruitment corruption case.
verification_mentioned: Migration expert Asif Munir: BMET clearance is the government's responsibility; workers should not be sent to countries (Russia, Cambodia) whose appointment letters cannot be verified. Article notes only 100 (2025) and 63 (2026) people took BMET clearance for Libya, so those reaching Libya go via the Middle East and other countries without clearance for Libya.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Ali Haider Chowdhury (former BAIRA secretary general): UAE and Qatar markets have shrunk and Malaysia is closed; people are cheated and trafficked trying to go by any means; he claims 70% of workers going to Saudi Arabia go on short terms and many find no work there. Asif Munir (migration expert): there is indifference to following the rules; why issue clearances for Russia and Cambodia when job letters cannot be verified. Sector people quoted: Cambodia's economy is no better than Bangladesh's and has few jobs, yet workers are sent there for scam centres. Article: there are complaints of not getting the contracted work in Saudi Arabia; there is not enough work there for the number of workers arriving.
other_practical_details: Cambodia: Bangladeshis are taken for 'call centre' jobs and then made to do online fraud; after raids on scam centres, 646 Bangladeshi workers returned in June 2026 alone and more return daily. BMET clearances in 2025: Cambodia 12,263 (8th largest destination), Russia 4,727 (13th). Markets: Malaysia closed since June 2024 for irregularities (reopening announced, not yet open); Oman effectively closed since 2024; UAE down from about 100,000 (2023) to 13,750 (2025); Bahrain closed for a long time. Saudi Arabia: about 755,000 went in 2025, about 215,000 in the first six months of 2026. Central Mediterranean: 14,194 reached Italy to June 2026, 32% (3,691) Bangladeshi; in 2025, 1,126 of all nationalities were dead or missing at sea. People returning on travel passes (after losing passports and being detained by police): 15,245 in Jan-Mar 2026 and 8,215 in April alone (airport sources). Licensed recruiting agencies: 2,646 (India 192, Pakistan 464, Nepal 416, Sri Lanka 248, per RMMRU).

headline_en: Went to Cambodia hoping for a job, held 17 days in a 'scam centre', recounts the ordeal
route_and_actual_destination: Dhaka to Phnom Penh by air; taken about 40 minutes by auto-rickshaw to a residential building, then driven overnight to a walled compound of three six-storey buildings near the Thai border; released near Siem Reap
promised_job_and_wage: Computer data entry; wage not stated
visa_type_claimed: Employment visa (he says Cambodian immigration changed it to a tourist visa at Phnom Penh airport)
amount_per_person: BDT 450,000 contract; a further USD 800 taken on arrival; USD 3,200 paid for release
payment_method: Contract written on a BDT 200 stamp paper; method of payment not stated
perpetrator_type: online contact acting as broker; Bangladeshis already abroad; foreign-run scam compound (Chinese owner, run by Pakistanis, per victim)
perpetrator_names: Md. Masud Mia (broker, had an office, now closed); Mostafa Mukul (Masud's associate in Cambodia); Arif (Mukul's associate who met him outside Phnom Penh airport)
how_victim_met_them: Met Masud Mia on Facebook, who then offered a job abroad
trust_devices: written contract on BDT 200 stamp paper; broker had an office; three-day BMET training at Probashi Kalyan Bhaban in Dhaka; BMET clearance / smart card issued; employment visa; learned basic computer work beforehand for the 'data entry' job
timeline: Contract 1 September last year; flight first set for 16 October, moved to 26 October; reached the compound 27 October; work began 28 October; refused after two days and was handcuffed; released 16 November; home 18 November. 22 days in Cambodia, 17 of them held
how_it_was_discovered: Stopped by Cambodian immigration at Phnom Penh airport and passport seized; then at the compound his phone and passport were taken, he was made to sign a paper in Chinese and given Hindi and English scripts to memorise
what_happened_abroad: Assigned to the second line of a 'calling room' that defrauds Indians (fake police video calls, fake bank). Refused after two days; handcuffed, beaten, given electric shocks, underfed, and repeatedly offered for sale. A fellow Bangladeshi, Ishtiaq Rabbi, was sold the same night. Released on 16 November, dropped in a deserted place in Siem Reap with passport and phone returned
victims_count: 1 (plus Ishtiaq Rabbi, sold on to another group)
harm: BDT 450,000 plus USD 800 lost, USD 3,200 paid for release, 17 days of confinement, beatings and electric shocks; returned empty-handed
ransom_details: USD 3,200 paid to the scam centre by the Bangladeshi community in Cambodia, after his younger brother asked them for help
official_response: None yet. He is preparing to file a case and wants government help; says he has received no compensation and no justice
money_recovered: None. Broker Masud promised compensation after his return, then disappeared; office closed
verification_mentioned: At Dhaka airport immigration police stopped him and sent him to the expatriates' desk to verify his smart card. He says the desk worker was scanning everyone's cards but let him through without checking after seeing his name on the passport. The reporter saw his passport, travel papers and some payment records but could not independently verify the detention account
other_practical_details: A BMET smart card and PDO training did not prevent this. How the scam centre works, per the victim: calling section has four lines (line 1 phones 500 numbers a day to confirm name and address, targeting Indians; line 2 checks Aadhaar details; line 3 is a room staged as a police station making threatening video calls; line 4 is a room staged as a bank demanding a 'fine' and PIN). Chatting section runs fake female profiles on Facebook, Instagram and dating apps, 11pm to 11am, targeting US citizens, with voice-changing software. Most workers were Pakistani, some Bangladeshi and Indian. The driver who dropped him bought him a bus ticket to Phnom Penh; he stayed two days with a community representative until a ticket was bought from Bangladesh
key_quote_bn: এটি মূলত ‘স্ক্যাম সেন্টার’। চীনা মালিক, চালান পাকিস্তানিরা।

headline_en: Will a syndicate move in as soon as Malaysia's labour market reopens?
destination_promised: Malaysia (worker recruitment; first batch of 10,000 workers planned at no cost through BOESL on special chartered flights)
amount_per_person: No figure fixed. Article says that in the past several times the government-set cost was allegedly charged, and some fear a worker may again have to pay several lakh taka
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency; brokers (feared, not a proven case)

perpetrator_type: Licensed recruiting agencies selected into a syndicate; alleged controllers in Malaysia and Bangladesh
perpetrator_names: Bestinet, owner of the FWCMS software 'Migrams', owned by Aminul Islam bin Abdul Nur (Amin Nur), a Malaysian citizen of Bangladeshi origin, alleged to control the whole trade; Ruhul Amin alias Swapan (former BAIRA secretary general), alleged to be his representative in Bangladesh, in hiding abroad since the 2024 uprising, licence withdrawn, cases ongoing, ACC investigating. 17 of the 25 selected agencies have no record of sending workers to Malaysia: Tania Trade, Satkhira International, A-Plus, Al Hayat Overseas, Valley Trade, Khan Jahan Ali Overseas, Bengal Human Resource, Earth Smart, At Taqwa, Motherland, Mangrove, Jewel Rinku Enterprise, Bangladesh One Overseas, Anwesha Air, Chandpur International, Goodness Services, Bhaluka Overseas (owner Md Abu Sohag Khan; licence 2022). trust_devices: official list of 25 approved agencies; licensed agencies; government announcement that the market is reopening
timeline: Market closed 2009; reopened end of 2016 (10 agencies); closed September 2018; reopened July/August 2022 (25, later 100 agencies); closed June 2024. Current MoU signed 18 December 2022 expires 31 December (2026). Article published 2 September 2026; a linked headline says workers start going from September.
harm: Expected higher cost for workers (BDT 600,000 to 700,000); earlier rounds ended in overcharging, cheated workers and repeated market closure
official_response: State minister Md Nurul Haque: the government sent a list of 423 agencies, Malaysia chose 25, and at the government's request allowed 338 more as associates; the ministry will set a cost ceiling; any agency accused of trafficking or corruption will be reported to Malaysia and its licence withdrawn. Ministry notice of 28 August: selection was done by a Malaysian high-level joint committee with no involvement of the Bangladesh government; under the 2022 MoU Malaysia alone selects agencies; the ministry says 312 agencies get 'associate recruiting agency' status. ACC wrote to BMET on 23 July asking for information on 57 agencies: a case was filed in June last year against 5 agencies for trafficking women abroad with forged papers in collusion with dishonest BMET officials, and 52 more were found in the investigation, including three on the new list. ACC is investigating the earlier syndicate fee; the ministry withdrew the licences of 49 agencies after a case was filed. Nepal has started an investigation into its own list of 25.
verification_mentioned: Ministry: the process for sending workers to Malaysia is not final and will be announced by ministry notice. Riazul Islam (immediate past senior vice-president, BAIRA): if there had been real vetting, these unknown agencies would not be on the list.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Expatriates' welfare ministry: beware of brokers and fraud rings; the Malaysia process is not finalised; do not make any payment before the ministry's notice. Shariful Hasan (associate director and head of migration programme, BRAC): choosing 25 agencies shows the syndicate is stronger than the two governments; recruitment is again running through Amin Nur's system; the agreement should have been amended, or workers sent from next year under a new agreement, otherwise there is no point reopening a market only for lakhs of workers to be cheated and the market closed again. Riazul Islam (BAIRA): it is a syndicate again with a new tactic and workers' costs will rise.
other_practical_details: Malaysia agreed in principle to take 10,000 workers free of cost, and the market is to restart with workers sent through the state agency BOESL. How 'associate' agencies work, according to four agency owners and BAIRA members: associates cannot send workers directly; demand comes in the name of the 25, so an agency with a demand letter contacts a listed agency and pays the syndicate fee; nobody applied to be an associate, they were simply made associates; each of the 25 has 10 associates and BOESL has 62; at least 817 agencies sent workers by paying the fee last time. Agencies approved without experience are unknown to Malaysian employers, so they will send through experienced agencies and collect the fee. Of the 25, eight have sent a combined 1,612 workers to Malaysia since January 2004. Malaysia set 10 conditions; 163 agencies qualified at first, conditions were relaxed, and 423 were sent. Nepal and Bangladesh got 25 agencies each; India, Pakistan and Myanmar 10 each; Sri Lanka and the Philippines had their whole lists approved; agency associations of four countries issued a joint protest. The article gives the number of associates as 338 in the minister's quote and 312 elsewhere.

route_and_actual_destination: Dhaka to Phnom Penh, Cambodia; three days in a restaurant, then a scam centre

DIG Dr Md Al-Mamunul Ansari (airport APBn): police take cases from victims, investigate, have rescued victims from Iran, Libya and Greece, and try to identify and arrest accused who are in Bangladesh.
verification_mentioned: DIG Al-Mamunul Ansari: at immigration, officers often recognise that someone on a tourist visa is really going to work and report or stop them; databases are checked for cases. advice_or_warning_in_article: Shariful Islam Hasan (BRAC): agencies are Dhaka-based, with none in Sylhet, Tangail, Munshiganj and other high-migration districts, so middlemen connect people to Dhaka and Bangladeshis pay the highest migration costs in the world; many go to Libya via Egypt or Dubai and are tortured there, paying BDT 2,500,000, 3,000,000 or even 6,500,000-6,700,000; traffickers use social media; BRAC's campaign slogan is 'no going abroad by sea'. perpetrator_names: Refers to the Nilphamari ring: Mariful Islam and Bachcha Bau alias Hasinur
how_victim_met_them: Social media; calls on WhatsApp or imo from numbers with the Canadian +1 country code
trust_devices: fake job offer letter with a well-known company's logo; forged LMIA or work permit copy; fake visa approval letter; fake website made to look like a government site; photos or identities of people living in Canada used on social media; calls from +1 numbers; pressure to decide quickly

perpetrator_names: Kafeel not named. Recovery scam: Md Rakib (20), Md Rakib Molla (29), Md Alauddin (26); 23 accused, most from Borhanuddin upazila, Bhola. Ad names: 'Habibullah Hujurer Darbar Sharif', 'Jainpuri Ma-Fatema Darbar Sharif', 'Tantrik.com Ghor' [তান্ত্রিককম.ঘর]
how_victim_met_them: Facebook and YouTube advertisements seen on 8 March 2022 promising recovery of owed money among other things; contact by phone
trust_devices: promise to recover the money within 72 hours by supernatural power; religious oaths on the Quran; edited frightening 'jinn' photos and distorted voice recordings; threats that her children would die if she told anyone
timeline: Contact from 8 March 2022; case filed 22 April 2024; charge sheet 13 July 2026
how_it_was_discovered: Kafeel: visa complications meant the 17 could not be sent and he did not refund. Recovery scam: the fraudsters kept giving new dates and then cut contact
victims_count: 1 family in this case (17 intending migrants behind the BDT 35 lakh)
harm: BDT 35 lakh not refunded by the kafeel; a further BDT 10.2 lakh lost; the wife became mentally ill and attempted suicide
official_response: Case at Tejgaon police station; PBI charge sheet against 23 under investigation by SI Md Sajibul Hasan; three arrested, confessed in court, now on bail; 20 absconding. Nothing reported on action against the kafeel.
money_recovered: None reported
other_practical_details: A secondary scam targeting a migrant family: people who lose visa money are approached by 'recovery' fraudsters. Accused said their ads also promised to get visas. One accused spent BDT 15,000 every five days on TV, Facebook and YouTube ads and admitted taking BDT 2-3 crore overall.
key_quote_bn: বাংলাদেশ থেকে ১৭ জনকে সৌদি আরবে নিতে নিজের কফিলকে ৩৫ লাখ টাকা দেন।

route_and_actual_destination: Nobody was sent anywhere
promised_job_and_wage: High-paid jobs and the chance to settle permanently (no figures)
visa_type_claimed: Work permit; fake visa approval letter and fake Canadian LMIA
amount_per_person: About BDT 480,000 (complainant Md Sayedul Haque)
payment_method: bKash / mobile banking, in stages (medical fee, visa processing fee, document charge, document verification, ticket)

perpetrator_names: Mariful Islam (21) and Bachcha Bau alias Hasinur (28), arrested in Kishoreganj thana area, Nilphamari
how_victim_met_them: Attractive job advertisements for Australia, Canada and other countries on social media; the ring then contacted job seekers

headline_en: Fraud and human trafficking in the trap of technology: what to do (roundtable, Dhaka, 22 July 2026)
route_and_actual_destination: Bangladesh to Cambodia on 5 Dec 2025; after a few days taken to a Chinese-run establishment (scam centre)
promised_job_and_wage: Restaurant job; wage not stated
perpetrator_type: relative or neighbour
how_victim_met_them: A relative from his own area offered the restaurant job
trust_devices: relative from his own area; training before departure
timeline: Went 5 Dec 2025 after training; taken to the scam centre a few days after arrival; date of rescue not stated
how_it_was_discovered: A few days after arrival he was taken to a Chinese establishment where thousands of people were working at computers and was told to pose as 'Maria' on Instagram
what_happened_abroad: Mannan Soyal (earlier three years in Saudi Arabia from 2022) was told to build relationships on Instagram under the name 'Maria' and extract money by fraud. When he objected, he was told to repay the money and take his passport back, which he could not do; his passport was held. He was forced to work, beaten for missing targets and locked in a small room. He was freed in a police raid. With no passport, return was complicated; BRAC arranged a travel pass and ticket.
victims_count: 1 (thousands of people were working in the centre); BRAC: 583 returned from Cambodia in June 2026 alone and 1,800 so far in 2026 as cyber-scam victims
harm: BDT 500,000 lost; passport confiscated; forced criminal work, beatings, confinement; now himself an accused in a counter-case and cannot afford to fight it
official_response: He filed a human trafficking case; the accused side filed a counter-case against him. Rebeka Khan (joint secretary, Home Ministry): the new 2026 law covers migrant smuggling and fraud through fake online job advertisements alongside trafficking; a national referral system and National Plan of Action 2026-30 are in progress; bilateral and regional cooperation against scam centres in Cambodia has been strengthened; officials involved in trafficking face legal action. Mahmudul Hasan (legal coordinator, RMMRU): a trafficking case takes two to three years to move from investigation to trial; the Dhaka human trafficking tribunal has had no judge for five months; there is no dedicated investigation agency for the tribunals.
verification_mentioned: Rebeka Khan: Passenger Name Record and Advance Passenger Information systems at airports are being expanded to detect fake travel documents. Dipta Rakshit (Winrock International): 80% of Cambodia returnees went through the legal migration process. Al-Amin Noyon (Anirban Survivors' Voice): BMET is responsible for checking that workers reached the workplace and that pay and housing are right; the state could identify how many people left on tourist visas and did not return.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Shariful Islam Hasan (BRAC), on Cambodia returnees: 98% did not get the promised job, 88% were confined, 87% had forged papers, 66% went through brokers, 38% suffered serious psychological trauma and 27% physical torture; people in Malaysia are also being cheated with promises of onward travel to Australia; social media is the traffickers' main tool. Al-Amin Noyon: in the last year and a half 56,000 Bangladeshis went with BMET clearance to 28 countries with no Bangladeshi embassy or consulate, and 16,000 went to Cambodia; many were shown an employment visa, then given a tourist visa and sold to scam rings although they had followed government rules; scam-centre returnees should be treated as survivors, not criminals. Ali Akbar Khan (acting additional IGP, CID): many go on tourist visas and are then defrauded; some victims later become traffickers; many victims settle or refuse to testify after returning. Dr B M Mainul Hossain (IIT, Dhaka University): traffickers use fake job advertisements, AI-generated videos, cryptocurrency, anonymising tools and secure messaging apps; even mainstream media are fooled by synthetic video. Tanvir Hassan Zoha (prosecutor, ICT): victims are often taken abroad, tortured and held for ransom. Dipta Rakshit: money channels (bKash, Nagad, hundi, cryptocurrency) need monitoring. Shakirul Islam (OKUP): a Madaripur deputy commissioner said he knows the traffickers but lacks power to act; workers leave with BMET clearance, so the state must own that process.
other_practical_details: Typical trick in the Malaysia case below: travel on a visit visa with coached answers for immigration, then confiscation of passport, ticket and papers on arrival and demands for more money. Cambodia pattern: employment visa shown in Bangladesh, tourist visa actually issued. Without a passport, returning requires a travel pass. Filing a trafficking case can bring a counter-case from the accused. Courts may push out-of-court settlement (OKUP's 2019 case ended in 2025 with a little over BDT 400,000 despite the victim asking for justice, not money). About 500 Rohingya deaths were reported in one week on the Bay of Bengal route to Malaysia (BRAC).
