headline_en: Fraud in the name of jobs abroad takes lakhs of taka
destination_promised: Russia, cook's job at a cantonment (main case); article also covers Cambodia call-centre jobs and Italy/Greece via Libya
route_and_actual_destination: Russia, sent straight to the Russia-Ukraine battlefield
promised_job_and_wage: Cook at a cantonment (wage not stated)
perpetrator_type: a ring sending Bangladeshi workers to the Russia-Ukraine war (not further identified); three agencies sending to Russia lost licences
how_victim_met_them: Article says a group uses social media to lure people with job offers
trust_devices: job advertisements on social media; BMET emigration clearance issued for Russia and Cambodia
timeline: Jahangir Alam went last year (2025) and returned after seven months
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival: sent directly to the battlefield instead of a cook's job
what_happened_abroad: Jahangir Alam of Lakshmipur was handed a weapon without training, then given one day of weapons training; 16 were together in the war camp and 4 died; he escaped and returned through the Bangladesh embassy
victims_count: Main case 1 (16 in his camp, 4 killed). Russia clearances: 4,727 last year, 2,125 in the first six months of this year
victim_home_districts: Lakshmipur (Jahangir Alam); Sunamganj (12 of at least 18 dead on the Libya-Greece route in March)
harm: Forced into combat, deaths of fellow recruits; in Libya, torture in camps and ransom; deaths at sea
ransom_details: In Libyan camps workers are held hostage and BDT 25 to 30 lakh is extracted (migration sector sources)
official_response: Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury: 49 agencies' licences withdrawn over Malaysia irregularities; licences of three agencies sending to Russia cancelled; BMET told to be more careful before giving clearance for Cambodia. Home Ministry: 1,126 new trafficking cases in 2025; 5,284 cases pending to May 2026; 94-95% of accused in 4,427 cases (2020-24) acquitted.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Shariful Hasan (BRAC associate director): trafficking now happens in the name of migration through job advertisements, driven by the urge to leave at any cost; traffickers are not punished.
other_practical_details: Cambodia: taken for 'call centre' jobs and made to do online fraud; 583 returned in June after scam centres were shut; BMET still cleared over 15,000 workers for Cambodia in a year and a half. BRAC on Cambodia returnees: 98% got no job, 90% forced into scam work, 88% had no freedom of movement, 86% had passport and papers taken, 27% severe physical torture. Mediterranean: 20,259 Bangladeshis entered Europe by sea in 2025 (Frontex via BRAC); 4,249 to Italy and 3,608 Libya-to-Greece in the first half of 2026. Oman and Malaysia markets closed for two years; UAE effectively closed.
key_quote_bn: প্রশিক্ষণ ছাড়াই অস্ত্র ধরিয়ে দেওয়া হয়। এরপর একদিন অস্ত্র চালানো শেখানো হয়। একসঙ্গে ১৬ জন ছিলেন যুদ্ধের ক্যাম্পে।

headline_en: Agencies will face ruin if they do not stop fraud: State Minister Nurul Haque
destination_promised: Singapore (main example); Malaysia and other countries in social media ads
amount_per_person: BDT 12 to 15 lakh taken from a worker going to Singapore, per the state minister
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agencies and a syndicate around six authorised training institutes; social media advertisers; officials (bribes at Probashi Kallyan Bank)
trust_devices: flashy and fake social media advertisements for Malaysia and other countries
official_response: BMET and RMMRU launched an Online Complaint Management Module on the Overseas Employment Platform linking all District Employment and Manpower Offices (DEMO) and BMET's central complaint system. State minister: fraud rings are under watch by DB police and intelligence agencies; BMET urged to run mobile courts against fake ads. BMET DG Jamil Ahmed: in 2025 BMET settled 500 complaints manually and recovered BDT 10 crore in compensation.
money_recovered: BMET says it obtained BDT 10 crore compensation for migrants from 500 complaints settled in 2025
verification_mentioned: State minister: advertising sending people abroad on social media without ministry permission is clearly illegal
advice_or_warning_in_article: State Minister Md Nurul Haque: of about 3,000 licensed agencies most are involved in irregularities; only 400-500 would survive if rules were followed. PM's special assistant Md Shakirul Islam: migrants must be aware so they do not step into a broker ring's trap. Ministry secretary Md Mokhtar Ahmed: most complaints prove true; the commonest are money taken for sending abroad, migrants' property grabbed at home, and migrants missing abroad.
other_practical_details: Through the new module migrants and families can file a complaint online from home, upload evidence, track progress and get notifications. RMMRU research (Tasneem Siddiqui): about 51% of migrants face some fraud, 19% paid and could not go, 32% were abused abroad. State minister alleged bribes of BDT 10,000-20,000 for Probashi Kallyan Bank loans.
key_quote_bn: এই টাকা কি সিঙ্গাপুর অথরিটি নেয়? নো। ছয়টা ট্রেনিং ইনস্টিটিউটকে অথরাইজেশন করেছে। তারা চার্জ দিচ্ছে, সিন্ডিকেট করে ব্যবসা করে তারা শতকোটি টাকার মালিক হয়ে যাচ্ছে।

headline_en: Coordinated action needed to prevent technology-driven human trafficking (roundtable report)
destination_promised: Cambodia and the Myanmar border (jobs in cyber scam centres presented as work)
route_and_actual_destination: Scam centres in Cambodia and on the Myanmar border
perpetrator_type: online contacts and recruiting agencies; earlier victims who later join the ring
how_victim_met_them: Fake job advertisements and posts about successful arrivals abroad on social media
trust_devices: fake job advertisements on social media; social media posts showing people who reached abroad successfully; regular migration process through a recruiting agency
victims_count: About 1,800 Bangladeshis returned after this kind of fraud up to June 2026 (BRAC concept paper); 473 returnees from Cambodian scam centres cited by Winrock
harm: Forced work in scam centres; some victims later become part of the same ring
official_response: Home Ministry joint secretary Rebeka Khan: national referral system, information sharing between agencies and modern technology at airport immigration. Survivor Mannan Soyal said that after he filed a case against those who cheated him, the accused filed a counter-case and are pressing him to take money and withdraw.
advice_or_warning_in_article: CID acting additional IGP Ali Akbar Khan: catching brokers at home is not enough because the drivers are abroad; expand legal migration and awareness. Dipta Rakshit (Winrock International): counter-campaigns must run on the same media where people are being deceived. Prof B M Mainul Hossain (Dhaka University IIT): AI, deepfakes, cryptocurrency, VPNs and encrypted apps make fraud hard for ordinary people to detect.
other_practical_details: Winrock: 80% of 473 people returned from Cambodian scam centres had gone through a recruiting agency in the regular migration process. Salma Ali: cases drag on for lack of skilled prosecutors and judges.
key_quote_bn: কম্বোডিয়ার স্ক্যাম সেন্টার থেকে ফেরত আসা ৪৭৩ জনের মধ্যে ৮০ শতাংশই রিক্রুটিং এজেন্সির মাধ্যমে নিয়মিত মাইগ্রেশন প্রক্রিয়ায় গিয়েছিলেন

headline_en: Woman trafficked to Cambodia and tortured in the name of a job; ringleader arrested
route_and_actual_destination: Sent to Cambodia in August 2025; moved between various establishments there
promised_job_and_wage: High-paid customer care service job (wage not stated)
amount_per_person: BDT 400,000 in total
payment_method: BDT 100,000 NGO loan taken by the accused directly; BDT 200,000 deposited to a bank account he gave; more taken at various times
how_money_was_raised: NGO loan of BDT 100,000 arranged with the accused's help, plus borrowing from others
perpetrator_type: village broker (an NGO employee who was her loan contact) with ring members in Cambodia
perpetrator_names: Md Rubel (29), home at Khagjana, Kalukhali upazila, Rajbari; arrested at Charbhadrasan, Faridpur. NGO not named.
how_victim_met_them: She had taken a loan from a local NGO; Rubel worked at that NGO and met her there
trust_devices: he worked at the NGO she borrowed from; he helped her get a BDT 100,000 NGO loan for the cost
timeline: Sent August 2025; returned to Bangladesh 1 July (2026); Rubel arrested the Tuesday before the 23 July 2026 report
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Cambodia other ring members forcibly took her passport and the money she carried
what_happened_abroad: Passport and cash seized; moved between establishments and made to do work against her will while her earnings were taken; attempts to involve her in illegal activities; physical and mental torture when she refused; threatened with death and with being sold to another broker when she asked to go home
harm: BDT 400,000 lost, NGO debt, forced labour, earnings taken, physical and mental torture
official_response: Victim filed a case after return; CID arrested Rubel, who gave a confessional statement in court; investigation continues into other members and possible other victims
other_practical_details: She returned with help from the BRAC Migration Welfare Centre (BRAC Migration Programme) and international and humanitarian organisations.

headline_en: Let there be no new 'Malaysia syndicate' (editorial)
amount_per_person: Government-set fee BDT 79,000; the syndicate took about BDT 550,000 from each worker
how_money_was_raised: Editorial says migrants generally sell assets or land or borrow at high interest
perpetrator_type: syndicate of licensed recruiting agencies with influential people in Bangladesh and Malaysia, including former Awami League ministers and MPs
timeline: Market closed September 2018 over a 10-agency syndicate; reopened 2022; closed again June 2024; reopening agreed after PM Tarique Rahman's visit to Malaysia the previous month
what_happened_abroad: Many Bangladeshi workers in Malaysia ended up in miserable, inhumane and undignified conditions; OHCHR issued a statement on their plight
harm: Overcharging of about BDT 550,000 per worker; poor conditions in Malaysia; market closure
official_response: Ministry cancelled licences of 49 syndicate agencies; editorial calls for legal action against all syndicate members
advice_or_warning_in_article: Prothom Alo editorial: the government must make sending workers to Malaysia transparent, fair and affordable and stop agencies forming a syndicate under political cover
other_practical_details: Of 14 countries sending workers to Malaysia, only Bangladesh had a syndicate system; 25 agencies at first, later 100.
key_quote_bn: সরকার নির্ধারিত ফি ছিল ৭৯ হাজার টাকা, সেখানে এই চক্র একেকজন কর্মীর কাছ থেকে হাতিয়ে নিত প্রায় সাড়ে ৫ লাখ টাকা।

headline_en: At the airport a woman learns someone else has already gone to Italy on her visa
destination_promised: Italy (woman joining her husband, who has long lived in Italy, with four children; not a job)
route_and_actual_destination: Victim never left Dhaka; another woman travelled to Italy on the victim's visa on 24 April
visa_type_claimed: Italy visa applied for through the Italian embassy (type not stated)
payment_method: Bank deposit to the accused's bank account in two instalments (19 April and 11 May)
perpetrator_type: agency or travel office (travel agency in Gulshan 1; tout met outside the embassy) (licence status not stated in article)
perpetrator_names: Belayet Hossain (40, head of the travel agency in Gulshan 1, described as ringleader), Nazmul Hasan (19), Mehedi Hasan (37), Solaiman Sumon (32), Fazle Rabbi (27), Touhidur Rahman (24), Kawsar Hossain (42). Agency name not printed.
how_victim_met_them: She met Nazmul Hasan when she went to collect her expired passport from the Italian embassy for renewal; he said he could get quick passport renewal and an Italy visa and took her to a travel agency in Gulshan 1, where he introduced her to Belayet Hossain
trust_devices: office premises (travel agency in Gulshan 1); written financial agreement saying full payment only after the visa is issued; a real Italy visa was actually issued in her passport; passport returned after payment
timeline: Paid on 19 April and 11 May; another woman flew on her visa on 24 April (before the second payment); arrests the day before the 21 July 2026 report
how_it_was_discovered: At Dhaka airport immigration on the day of travel with her children: officers told her another woman had already gone to Italy on 24 April using the Italy visa in her passport
victims_count: 1 complainant (plus four children); CID says Belayet has sent about 30 people to Italy by the same method since 2016
harm: BDT 440,000 lost; visa used by another person; could not travel; husband's air tickets wasted
official_response: Case filed at Gulshan police station under the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling Act; CID arrested seven in Gulshan 1; seized 56 passports in various names, 153 seals of government, private and foreign institutions, 3 CPUs, 1 laptop, 1 embossing seal and BDT 250,000. Belayet is on bail in a 2024 Airport police station case for a similar offence. Forensic examination under way.
verification_mentioned: Airport immigration records showed the visa had already been used (immigration officers)
advice_or_warning_in_article: Immigration authorities advised her to complain to CID's human trafficking unit
other_practical_details: The accused demanded the contract money when she collected her passport with the visa from the embassy, and took her passport when she did not pay; she paid to get it back. CID: the ring kept victims' passports in their custody and by forgery sent other people abroad in place of the real passport holder.
key_quote_bn: তাঁর পাসপোর্টে থাকা ইতালির ভিসা ব্যবহার করে ২৪ এপ্রিলই অন্য আরেক নারী ইতালি চলে গেছেন।

headline_en: Licences of 49 recruiting agencies cancelled, including 5 owned by former Awami League MPs
amount_per_person: Government-set maximum cost was BDT 78,990; workers paid BDT 544,000 on average
amount_total: About BDT 24,000 crore of business from about 450,000 workers sent in a year and a half
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agencies in the Malaysia syndicate (including agencies of former ministers and MPs)
perpetrator_names: Orbitals Enterprise and Orbital International (wife and daughter of former finance minister A H M Mustafa Kamal); Ahmed International (Benzir Ahmed, Dhaka-20 MP); Snigdha Overseas Limited (Nizam Uddin Hazari, former Feni-2 MP); Five M International (Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, former Feni-3 MP); Unique Eastern Private Limited (Noor Ali); Catharsis International (Ruhul Amin alias Swapan, described as a key syndicate member). Others named: Messrs Shahin Travels, Irving Enterprise, Hridoy Trade International, Rabbi International, Zahrat International, 4 Site International, Binimoy International, Akash Bhraman Limited, QK Quick Express Limited, United Export Limited, GMG Trading Private Limited, Sadia International, The Super Eastern Limited, Elegant Overseas Limited, Midway Overseas Limited, Madina Overseas, Al Khamis International, New Age International, Damasi Corporation Limited, Galaxy Corporation, Sultan Overseas, Provati International, Manispower Corporation, Amin Tours and Travels, ISMT Human Resource Development, Darbar Global Overseas, Natasha Overseas, Aparajita Overseas, Stanford Employment Private Limited, Jannat Overseas, BM Travels, BNS Overseas Limited, Rubel Bangladesh Limited, Trans Asia Integrate Services Limited, Al Farah Human Resources and Consultancy, Brothers International, Thanex International Limited, JG Alfalah Management, Imperial Resources Limited, PR Overseas Limited, MEF Global Bangladesh Limited, Ananya Apurba Recruiting Agency. No licence numbers printed.
timeline: Malaysia market reopened July 2022 after about four years closed; syndicate started with 25 agencies and grew in three steps to 100; sending stopped June 2024 (last entry date for approved workers 31 May 2024).
victims_count: About 450,000 workers sent in a year and a half (all paying the inflated cost, per the article)
harm: Workers paid on average about BDT 544,000 against a government ceiling of BDT 78,990; market closed since June 2024
official_response: Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment Ministry gazette (issued Sunday, the day before publication) withdrew 49 licences because a court had accepted charge sheets against the agencies under Penal Code 1860 sections 406, 420, 385, 386, 427 and 34. Ministry sources: a withdrawn licence may need a legal fight to get back.
other_practical_details: The 'Malaysia syndicate' is a system where only a small number of agencies are allowed to send workers to Malaysia; Malaysia chose them from a list of 1,520 agencies sent by the ministry. Agencies allegedly paid large sums to get into the syndicate. Ruling-party leaders, city councillors and many new firms sent large numbers of workers through it.
key_quote_bn: মালয়েশিয়ায় কর্মী পাঠাতে সরকার নির্ধারিত সর্বোচ্চ খরচ ছিল ৭৮ হাজার ৯৯০ টাকা। কিন্তু মালয়েশিয়া যেতে গড়ে একজন বাংলাদেশি কর্মী খরচ করেছেন ৫ লাখ ৪৪ হাজার টাকা।

headline_en: From Russia to a Ukrainian prison: will Kamrul be able to return to his wife and child?
destination_promised: Russia: construction work at Sinopec Engineering and Construction company [সিনোপ্যাক]
route_and_actual_destination: Arrived in Russia 17 July 2025; five to six months in a hilly area; went to Moscow looking for work; handed to the Russian army; fled the camp; captured by Ukrainian soldiers; now in a prison in Ukraine
promised_job_and_wage: USD 600-700 a month at the company named in the advertisement
visa_type_claimed: Work (not specified)
amount_per_person: BDT 850,000 in total to go to Russia (contract BDT 800,000); a second broker in Moscow later took BDT 500,000 for a promised move to Italy
how_money_was_raised: Loans: BDT 250,000 at interest from a local man, BDT 100,000 from a relative, BDT 100,000 from relatives in Dhaka
perpetrator_type: training centre linked to a recruiting agency; then brokers in Moscow
perpetrator_names: MSTC Technical Training Centre, Uttara, Dhaka (described as a sister concern of Munia Overseas), contact Toufayel Ahmed (marketing staff). He says Kamrul was sent through 'Bonna Bijoy Overseas-1214' travel agency [বন্যা বিজয় ওভারসিস-১২১৪]. Moscow brokers not named.
how_victim_met_them: Saw an advertisement for workers at a Russian company and contacted the training centre
trust_devices: job advertisement naming a company and a USD 600-700 wage; three months of training at the training centre; contract
timeline: Reached Russia 17 July 2025; 5-6 months at the first site; last call home 31 March 2026 ('you won't find me for six months'); wife's Facebook post 13 May 2026; contacted 16 May; video call from the prison 17 May
how_it_was_discovered: On 31 March 2026 he told his wife a broker had forced them to sign a contract and sent them into the Russian army; on a video call she saw Bangladeshis in military uniform
what_happened_abroad: In Moscow one broker's fraud left him sleeping in the open for two nights; a second took BDT 500,000 promising Italy, then he was handed to the Russian army and made to sign a one-year contract by force. After about a month of hunger and abuse he and another Bangladeshi (Sumon) fled the camp unarmed and were captured by Ukrainian soldiers; held in a Ukrainian prison without identity papers.
victims_count: 1 (plus another Bangladeshi, Sumon, captured with him)
harm: Forced military service, hunger and abuse, imprisonment in Ukraine; BDT 850,000 plus BDT 500,000 lost; family debt now BDT 300,000 with interest
official_response: None reported; wife appeals to the government to bring him home. The training centre's Toufayel Ahmed denies taking that much money, says leaving the workplace is against company rules and they are not responsible for anyone who left on his own.
money_recovered: None
other_practical_details: Kamrul had worked 12 years in Singapore before this. The danger came after he left the original job site and dealt with brokers in Moscow offering onward travel to Italy. His wife found him by posting in the Facebook group 'Russia Probashi (Russia Expatriate)'; a man identifying himself as Swiss journalist Kurt Pelda then contacted her on WhatsApp.
key_quote_bn: পরে আরেক দালাল ইতালিতে পাঠানোর প্রলোভন দেখিয়ে পাঁচ লাখ টাকা হাতিয়ে নেয়। এরপর প্রতারণার মাধ্যমে তাঁকে রাশিয়ার সেনাবাহিনীর কাছে হস্তান্তর করা হয়।

headline_en: Went to Russia lured by a company job; wounded on the battlefield, pleads to be brought home
route_and_actual_destination: Flew to Russia on 7 May 2026 with BMET clearance; handed to the Russian army; deployed in Russian-occupied areas of Ukraine; wounded and in a field medical camp in a town the article names as 'Krasnodo' [ক্রাসনদো], Ukraine
promised_job_and_wage: Construction work for a company at 60,000 roubles a month (about BDT 90,000), for two years
visa_type_claimed: Work (sent with BMET clearance); visa type not stated
amount_per_person: BDT 700,000 (first asked BDT 800,000)
amount_total: BDT 2,800,000 from four people
how_money_was_raised: Borrowing
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency, reached through a broker
perpetrator_names: Jabel-e-Noor International Limited [জাবেল-ই-নূর ইন্টারন্যাশনাল লিমিটেড], recruiting agency, Malibagh, Dhaka (no licence number given). Broker: Imran Hossain of Satair, Boalmari, Faridpur.
how_victim_met_them: About a year earlier, introduced to broker Imran Hossain through the victim's nephew/cousin
trust_devices: licensed recruiting agency office in Malibagh; medical test and formalities; BMET clearance (smart card); written contract for a company job; a woman representative met them at the airport in Russia
timeline: Introduced about a year before; flew 7 May 2026; three days in a hotel then handed to the army; families complained to the ministry 19 May; wounded 13 June; reached family 15 June, about a month and a half after leaving
how_it_was_discovered: Handed to the army right after landing in Russia; a few days later they told families by SMS and voice message that each had been sold to the Russian forces for BDT 3,075,000 through the agency
what_happened_abroad: A group of 30 was kept in a hotel for three days, then handed to the army, heads shaved, put in uniform, trained for a few days and given heavy weapons. Split into groups of 16 and 14 and sent ahead of Russian soldiers to check roads for mines and drones. Ali Hasan Sohel and Palash Sheikh were wounded on 13 June (hearing loss, hand injuries); 12 of his group are untraceable and feared dead; food is inedible; they are told they will be sent back to the front.
victims_count: 4 complainant families (Ali Hasan Sohel 42, Palash Sheikh, Roni, Sourav Molla) out of a group of 30; another wounded man, Rajon of Jhenaidah
harm: Forced into combat, wounded by drone/mine attacks, 12 companions missing; BDT 700,000 each lost; families in debt
official_response: Four families filed a written complaint with the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare on 19 May 2026. Goalanda UNO Sathi Das said she had not known and would help if the family takes legal action. No case or arrest reported in this article.
money_recovered: None; wife says not one taka of the BDT 700,000 has come back. The agency gave no help and threatened the families.
verification_mentioned: None; the men travelled with BMET clearance through a licensed agency and were still handed to the army
other_practical_details: BMET clearance and a licensed agency did not prevent this. Sohel's cousin and others from Boalmari were due to travel but did not go in the end.
key_quote_bn: কিন্তু রাশিয়া বিমানবন্দরে নামার পরই আমাদের সেনাবাহিনীর কাছে হস্তান্তর করা হয়।

headline_en: Going abroad by sea must be stopped now (roundtable)
destination_promised: Malaysia (Tarekur Rahman: told a Malaysian visa would be easy to get)
route_and_actual_destination: From Maheshkhali (Cox's Bazar) to Myanmar; held in a hidden location, moved to another, taken toward the border, caught and jailed in Myanmar; never reached Malaysia
visa_type_claimed: Easy Malaysian visa promised by the broker
amount_per_person: BDT 100,000 taken from the family first; then more under torture (amount not stated); then another large sum on a promise of onward travel to Malaysia (amount not stated)
how_money_was_raised: Selling the house
perpetrator_type: Broker and traffickers
trust_devices: promise of an easy Malaysian visa; repeated assurance of onward travel to Malaysia
timeline: About seven months in a Myanmar prison; other durations not stated
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Myanmar, where the torture began immediately
what_happened_abroad: Beaten on arrival; after BDT 100,000 was taken from the family they were moved to another hidden place, tortured and threatened with death; often fed only once in three or four days even after paying; taken toward the border on a false promise of Malaysia, caught and jailed in Myanmar for about seven months.
victims_count: Tarekur speaks of 'we' (number not stated). UNHCR (Astrid Castelein): about 5,787 people went missing on irregular sea journeys in 2023, half Rohingya and half Bangladeshi.
harm: Torture, starvation, death threats, about seven months in prison, house sold, money lost
ransom_details: BDT 100,000 from the family after the first beating; further payments under torture and another large sum for the false onward journey; to the traffickers; method not stated
official_response: Tarekur says they got little help from the Bangladesh embassy and came home on money sent by the family. Advocate Biswajit Bhowmik (Bangladesh National Women Lawyers' Association): about 465 human trafficking cases are pending in Cox's Bazar and the association handles cases for about 100 returnees. Captain Mohammad Mizanur Rahman (Coast Guard east zone commander): traffickers who are charged often get out of jail and return to the same work. District manpower office (Liton Kanti Chowdhury): about 30 complaints settled.
money_recovered: None mentioned; he returned on money sent by the family
verification_mentioned: Mobarak Hossain (assistant director, regional passport office, Cox's Bazar): since e-passports started in 2020 a passport cannot be issued without online verification of NID and birth registration, and multiple passports are now easily detected; under a February 2025 circular the NID data is the basis of the passport.
advice_or_warning_in_article: State minister Md Nurul Haque: brokers hold people hostage on the way and extract large sums from families; no food or water is given; many die; those who land are arrested. Coast Guard commander: traffickers bring people from around the country to the hills and send them out by sea at night; no food, clean water or toilet on the boats; bodies are thrown into the sea. SP A N M Sazedur Rahman: traffickers befriend people on social media, invite them for a visit, then abduct or traffic them; some fishermen think trafficking pays more than fishing. Deputy commissioner Md A Mannan: risk rises in winter when the sea is calm; families often will not admit what happened, which makes investigation hard. Shariful Islam Hasan (associate director, BRAC migration programme): brokers promise Malaysia or Australia but people are tortured and ransomed; most irregular migrants end in death, jail or return; BRAC's slogan is 'say no to going abroad by sea'. Biswajit Bhowmik: many leave by air with passport, visa and BMET card but on 90-day visas, get no right to stay or work, and come back empty-handed.
other_practical_details: Md Shah Jalal (principal, Ramu TTC, Cox's Bazar): pre-departure training and three-month courses (electrical, housekeeping, graphics design, IT support, air conditioning and refrigeration, automobile mechanics); a centre for the skill verification test needed for Saudi jobs now operates in Cox's Bazar, and passing makes a job easier to get and the pay higher. Liton Kanti Chowdhury: a pre-decision pilot programme for would-be migrants runs in Chakaria. Shariful Hasan: about 100,000 Bangladeshis detained crossing the Mediterranean in 16 years; about 650,000 Bangladeshis have asylum applications pending in various countries; legal migration is complex, costly and often broker-controlled. Hamida Yasmin is listed as a participant (victim returned from Saudi Arabia) but no statement from her is printed.

key_quote_bn: সহজে মালয়েশিয়ার ভিসা পাওয়া যাবে, এই প্রলোভন দেখিয়ে দালাল আমাদের মহেশখালী থেকে মিয়ানমারে পাচার করে দেয়

headline_en: Bangladeshi student killed in Cyprus after an argument on a bus; accused then staged a kidnapping
destination_promised: Cyprus (already there as a student); lured with a factory job at Kofinou
route_and_actual_destination: Larnaca, Cyprus
promised_job_and_wage: A job at a factory in Kofinou; 12 June was to be his first day
visa_type_claimed: Student (enrolled at a private university in Larnaca a few months earlier)
perpetrator_type: foreign national (22) met on a bus in Cyprus; nationality not stated
how_victim_met_them: Met on a bus five days before the killing; the accused was angered by a remark and then lured him with a job offer
trust_devices: job offer at a factory
timeline: Left home 12 June 2026 about 6:30 pm; body found after nine days of searching; accused arrested 21 June
how_it_was_discovered: Ransom demands reached the father (who lives in Greece) and on social media; the suspect confessed and led police to the body
what_happened_abroad: Shahriar Ahmed Emon (22) was lured from his flat in Oroklini to a secluded spot near the Kofinou migrant reception centre and stabbed and strangled the same evening; the accused hid the body, took his phone and staged a kidnapping to extract money
harm: Death
ransom_details: Messages demanded EUR 10,000 one day and EUR 25,000 the next, with a threat not to inform the authorities; article does not say any was paid
official_response: Larnaca CID arrested a 22-year-old foreign national, who confessed; to be produced at Larnaca District Court for remand. Motive still under investigation, with financial gain treated as primary.
other_practical_details: Student took up factory work alongside study; sent a location pin to a friend the night he disappeared, which the family gave to police.

headline_en: Lives in Bangladesh, poses on Facebook as an expatriate in Australia, and takes people's money
route_and_actual_destination: Never left; victim is a Bangladeshi worker in Oman
promised_job_and_wage: Job and permanent residence in Australia; no wage stated
visa_type_claimed: Work permit / work visa (as advertised on the fake page)
payment_method: bKash (mobile banking) in stages; a bank account number was then given to collect more
perpetrator_type: online contact posing as a Bangladeshi in Australia, introduced by an acquaintance
perpetrator_names: Md Roni Islam (19), Taraganj, Rangpur, posing as 'Khaja Mohammad Ali'; Md Rakibul Hossain (26), Saidpur, Nilphamari (handled the mobile-banking accounts)
how_victim_met_them: An earlier acquaintance contacted him in December 2025 offering to arrange work in Australia and connected him to 'Khaja Mohammad Ali'
trust_devices: fake Facebook page with attractive videos on Australian jobs, work permits and migration; imo account on an Australian phone number; contact by phone, imo, WhatsApp and Messenger; itemised fees for processing, online application, form filling and visa
timeline: First contact December 2025; case filed 2 June 2026; arrests 17 June 2026
how_it_was_discovered: After a long time with nothing arranged, the phone numbers were switched off and all contact stopped
victims_count: 1 in this case; CID says the two had long been taking money from people this way
harm: BDT 146,400 lost
official_response: Victim's nephew filed a case at Jatrabari police station, Dhaka on 2 June 2026 (law not stated). CID arrested both at Kamarpukur Bazar, Saidpur, Nilphamari and seized six phones and 12 SIMs.
advice_or_warning_in_article: CID: do not pay any money on an offer of a job or migration abroad without properly verifying the organisation, the recruiting agency and the visa process.
other_practical_details: Money was collected into several mobile-banking accounts and moved on by an accomplice. Target was a Bangladeshi already working abroad (Oman).
key_quote_bn: বিশ্বাসযোগ্যতা তৈরির জন্য অস্ট্রেলিয়ার নম্বর ব্যবহার করে ইমু অ্যাকাউন্টের মাধ্যমেও যোগাযোগ করা হতো।

headline_en: Biman official arrested on charge of trafficking people to Italy with fake Schengen visas
route_and_actual_destination: Given tickets for Nepal and Italy; flew on a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight on 26 May 2026; reached Rome Leonardo da Vinci airport, held two days, sent back to Bangladesh on 28 May
promised_job_and_wage: Job in Italy (unspecified)
visa_type_claimed: Italian Schengen visa (fake)
amount_per_person: Agreed BDT 3,000,000 each; BDT 2,000,000 each taken in advance
amount_total: BDT 4,000,000 advance from two people
perpetrator_type: trafficking ring including an airline ground-service official
perpetrator_names: Mohammad Akhlasur Rahman (40), Junior Officer (Ground Service, INS Gate), Biman Bangladesh Airlines; home Bakshiganj, Jamalpur; lived at Ashkona, Dakshinkhan, Dhaka. Ring leader and others not yet identified.
trust_devices: fake Italian Schengen visa in the passport; air tickets for Nepal and Italy; boarding passes
timeline: Departed 26 May; deported 28 May; case filed 30 May; arrest on a Tuesday night in mid-June 2026
how_it_was_discovered: Italian immigration at Rome Leonardo da Vinci airport identified the Schengen visa in their passports as fake on arrival
what_happened_abroad: Held in custody for two days at Rome airport, then returned to Bangladesh
harm: BDT 2 million each lost; two days' detention; deportation
official_response: Case filed 30 May 2026 at Airport police station, Dhaka (law not stated). CID arrested Akhlasur Rahman at Nilakhia Bazar, Bakshiganj, Jamalpur; investigation continues to identify the ring leader.
advice_or_warning_in_article: CID: follow only government-approved legal procedures for work, migration or travel abroad, and report any information on trafficking, fake visas or irregular migration to law enforcement.
other_practical_details: The victims got through departure from Dhaka on the fake visa and were stopped only at the destination. On return they were questioned by immigration police and CID.
key_quote_bn: রোমের লিওনার্দো দা ভিঞ্চি আন্তর্জাতিক বিমানবন্দরে পৌঁছানোর পর দেশটির ইমিগ্রেশন কর্তৃপক্ষ তাঁদের পাসপোর্টে থাকা শেনজেন ভিসাটি জাল বলে শনাক্ত করে।

headline_en: Four Patgram youths trafficked to Russia's 'battlefield'
destination_promised: Russia: jobs in a garment factory and IT firm (one victim says they were told a drone factory)
route_and_actual_destination: Dhaka to Bahrain to Moscow on 8 May 2026; ended up in an unidentified military camp in Russia
promised_job_and_wage: Well-paid job in a garment factory / IT firm; drone factory work per victim's video; wage not stated
amount_total: BDT 3,600,000 from four people
how_money_was_raised: Mortgaged farmland, loans, savings
perpetrator_type: local brokers (local political figures) working with a licensed recruiting agency
perpetrator_names: RS International, recruiting agency, Sector 15, Uttara, Dhaka (office found locked 7 June). Accused locally: Md Yunus Ali (president, Jamaat-e-Islami Patgram upazila youth wing), Md Sohel Rana (Jamaat ameer, Patgram municipal unit) and his employee Mahin. Ministry also named Jabal-e-Noor and TS Overseas Limited. No licence numbers given.
how_victim_met_them: Local men from their own area offered good jobs in Russia
trust_devices: licensed recruiting agency with an office in Uttara; local political figures as recruiters
timeline: Flew 8 May 2026; family applications to ministries 22-23 May; press conference 26 May; agency office locked since after the Eid holiday
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Moscow their passports, visas and phones were taken; they reached family using someone else's phone, and a video by one victim spread on social media
what_happened_abroad: Held in a camp; told they would be sent to fight after 15 days of training. Families allege they were sold to a Russian 'mercenary force' / the army.
victims_count: 4 (Nazmul Alam 21, Mehedi Hasan 21, Al Amin 20, Abdullah Al Mamun 22); RAMRU and the ministry say 30 more youths from various districts were sent before Eid and are held
harm: Confined in a military camp, documents and phones seized, risk to life; BDT 900,000 each lost; families in debt with land mortgaged
official_response: Four separate cases filed at Patgram police station naming Yunus Ali, Sohel Rana and Mahin; under investigation (law not stated). Ministry withdrew the licences and forfeited the security deposits of RS International, Jabal-e-Noor and TS Overseas Limited. Diplomatic contact started to bring the 30 back. Jamaat relieved the accused of their posts on 20 May and said any involvement was personal.
money_recovered: None reported
advice_or_warning_in_article: RAMRU acting executive director Tasneem Siddiqui: a ring lures youths with good pay and citizenship and is sending them to the Russia-Ukraine war; RAMRU had warned the interim government, which took no major step. RAMRU: 4,663 people went to Russia last year against 993 in 2024.
other_practical_details: Families applied to the Wage Earners' Welfare Board director general, the expatriates' welfare secretary and the foreign ministry's Consular and Welfare Wing director general. The agency was licensed, so a licence alone did not protect the victims.
key_quote_bn: সেখানে পৌঁছানোর পর তাঁদের পাসপোর্ট, ভিসা ও মুঠোফোন কেড়ে নেওয়া হয়।

headline_en: Way to send Bangladeshi workers to Malaysia will open very soon: expatriates' welfare minister in parliament
destination_promised: Various countries (shell companies abroad); Russia (jobs) for the 30 sent to war
route_and_actual_destination: Russia cases: many reached Russia through a third country (state minister)
visa_type_claimed: Work visas against demand letters from nominal (shell) companies
perpetrator_type: shell companies abroad opened by Bangladeshis, sometimes with local owners; licensed recruiting agencies (Russia cases)
trust_devices: demand letter attested by the Bangladesh embassy
what_happened_abroad: State Minister Nurul Haque: nominal companies bring 100 people where there is work for 10. At least 30 Bangladeshis taken to Russia on the promise of work were drawn into the war, according to their families.
victims_count: At least 30 (Russia war cases reported to the ministry)
official_response: Licences of three recruiting agencies suspended over the Russia cases; legal action in process. Ministry wants stricter embassy-level scrutiny of demand letters; 30 labour welfare wings in 27 countries, short of staff and money.
verification_mentioned: State minister: demand letters sent from abroad are attested by the Bangladesh embassy in that country, and that check needs to be stricter (i.e. attestation alone has not stopped fake demand)
other_practical_details: Toll-free hotline 16135 for expatriates, reachable from abroad. Two Bangladeshi safe homes in Saudi Arabia. Collateral-free loan for outbound workers up to BDT 300,000 at 8% interest (plan to raise to BDT 500,000; no interest-free loan planned). For workers who went with BMET clearance the government bears the full cost of bringing a body home; undocumented workers are helped on humanitarian grounds. Workers currently being sent to Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Qatar, Romania, Seychelles, Portugal; Malaysia, Oman, UAE, Bahrain closed or restricted.
key_quote_bn: নামমাত্র কোম্পানি খুলে এখান থেকে লোক নিয়ে যাচ্ছে। দেখা যায় ১০ জনের কাজের জায়গায় ১০০ জন নিয়ে যাচ্ছে।

headline_en: Rights of women migrant workers and safe migration (roundtable)
destination_promised: Middle East (women workers, mostly domestic work); Jordan garment sector through BOESL
amount_per_person: No fraud amount given. BOESL: women go to Jordan's garment sector at zero cost.
how_money_was_raised: High-interest loans or sale of assets (Badabon Sangho 2025 study)
perpetrator_type: Foreign employers; brokers and recruiting agents (pattern, no individual named)
trust_devices: false publicity by brokers and recruiting agents on digital media (S K Mojibul Haque, BNSK)
what_happened_abroad: Pattern described by speakers: 12 to 14 hours of work instead of 8; low pay; loss of control of the passport; physical, mental and sexual abuse; some women return with children after abuse.
victims_count: Jasiya Khatun (WARBE), citing the Wage Earners' Welfare Board: about 799 to 800 women migrants came home dead in the last 8 years
victim_home_districts: Study districts: Dhaka, Manikganj, Gopalganj, Sunamganj, Narsingdi, Cumilla, Pabna
harm: Deaths recorded mostly as heart attack, illness or sometimes suicide, with the real cause unknown; abuse; debt; no rehabilitation and social stigma on return
official_response: State minister Md Nurul Haque: agreements with some countries now allow cases and compensation claims; plans for law firms abroad, a one-stop service at district level, a 'Probashi Card', a standard migration cost, a grading system for recruiting agencies and a rehabilitation fund. Wage Earners' Welfare Board (Dr A T M Mahbub-ul Karim): legal help through labour wings; 22 law firms in 12 countries help recover dues.
verification_mentioned: Nu-Emong Marma Mong (deputy manager, overseas recruitment, BOESL): the labour wing at the Bangladesh embassy verifies each employer's demand before BOESL publishes a notice; the fixed migration cost for each country is announced in advance; he says those who go through BOESL have no chance of being cheated.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Farzana Shahnaz (IOM): for lack of reliable information villagers depend on brokers; people must work out the cost, the earnings, the length of stay and what is left, because loan-financed migration often ends with earnings going to repay the debt. Jasiya Khatun (WARBE): employer lists in the Middle East should be strictly monitored by the ministry and embassies and risky employers blacklisted. Rahnuma Salam Khan (ILO): the 2025 rules on the responsibilities of recruiting agencies and sub-agents are not yet being enforced. Marina Sultana (RMMRU): sub-agent registration exists in law but is not implemented. Sheikh Romana (general secretary, Bangladesh Obhibashi Mohila Sramik Association): of about 2,200 agencies 1,100 are legal, and ethical recruitment is still not real; embassies are short of staff. Mahmuda Sultana (general secretary, migrant women workers' federation): the three-day basic training at the district employment office does not cover the reality of the work, the risks, or where to get help and legal aid. Sharmin Islam (UNDP): three days of training cannot teach language, culture or job skills. Fariha Jasmin (Badabon Sangho): kafala, broker syndicates and weak control keep the risk high.
other_practical_details: Wage Earners' Welfare Board (Mahbub-ul Karim): anyone, documented or not, can become a member for BDT 400; up to BDT 200,000 one-time help for illness if applied for within a year of return; BDT 2,000 a month for up to seven years for up to two disabled children per family; up to BDT 400,000 for injury or loss of limb against a BDT 500 premium; a five-year life policy for BDT 1,000; on death, with a BDT 300 membership, the body is brought home from any country with BDT 35,000 for burial and transport, plus BDT 300,000 to heirs and up to BDT 1,000,000 more if insured. BOESL: operating since 1984; process is demand from an employer or a government-to-government deal, embassy verification, public notice, a test attended by the employer or its local representative, then help with all legal steps; has sent women to Jordan's garment sector free since 2010, with medical, pre-departure training and airport handover done by its officers. Badabon Sangho 2025 study: 27.6% of women migrated with no source of income. Marina Sultana: women are about 13.5% of total migration.
key_quote_bn: বিদেশে গিয়ে হয়রানি ও নির্যাতনের পর দেশে ফিরলেও আমরা তেমন কোনো পুনর্বাসনসহায়তা পাই না।

headline_en: Say no to going abroad by sea
destination_promised: Australia via Malaysia (Aung Aung U Jewel); a good job in Malaysia (Tarequr Rahman)
route_and_actual_destination: Jewel: Cox's Bazar to Myanmar, arrested there and jailed. Tarequr: by ship from Cox's Bazar to Myanmar, then Thailand, caught at the border on the way to Malaysia, jailed, returned.
promised_job_and_wage: 'Good job' in Malaysia (Tarequr); no wage stated
amount_per_person: Jewel: BDT 1,200,000. Tarequr: BDT 100,000 taken from family in Myanmar plus BDT 700,000 in Thailand
payment_method: Tarequr: demanded from the family in stages while he was in transit
how_money_was_raised: General (state minister): people sell land and borrow
perpetrator_type: brokers / sea-route trafficking ring
how_victim_met_them: Jewel fell in with brokers while a college student (no further detail)
trust_devices: promise of onward travel to Australia via Malaysia; stories of a good job told before departure
how_it_was_discovered: Jewel: arrested by police in Myanmar. Tarequr: money demanded from family once he was in Myanmar and again in Thailand; caught at the border.
what_happened_abroad: Jewel was jailed in Myanmar, contacted family with a policeman's help and came home with embassy help. Tarequr was jailed after being caught at the border and later returned. Coast Guard: people are brought from around the country, kept in the hills and elsewhere around Cox's Bazar, moved in small boats to large trawlers or ships; torture starts once aboard.
victims_count: 2 named victims spoke (a third, Hamida Yasmin, is listed without detail)
victim_home_districts: Cox's Bazar (Maheshkhali) for Tarequr; Jewel's district not stated
harm: Jail in Myanmar/Thailand-Malaysia border, money lost (BDT 1.2 million; BDT 800,000)
ransom_details: Tarequr: BDT 100,000 then BDT 700,000 taken from his family during transit. State minister: brokers hold people hostage and extract large sums from families, giving minimal food and water.
official_response: State Minister Nurul Haque: sea departures must stop; union-level campaigns. Cox's Bazar DC: administration active on the coast. Coast Guard zonal commander: such cases would fall if offenders were punished.
advice_or_warning_in_article: RRRC camp-in-charge Suraiya Akter Sweety: Rohingya girls in particular are lured with the promise of a 'better husband' and taken by sea to Malaysia and Indonesia. BRAC's Shariful Islam Hasan: mass graves of Bangladeshis and Rohingya were found in Thailand and Malaysia in 2015; Bangladesh tops the countries of irregular sea arrivals to Europe.
other_practical_details: Roundtable by BRAC and Prothom Alo with Australian government support, Cox's Bazar. Those who do reach shore are arrested by police there (state minister).
key_quote_bn: যাত্রার আগে তাঁদের নানা ধরনের স্বপ্নের কথা শোনানো হয়, কিন্তু জাহাজে তোলার পর থেকে শুরু হয় নির্যাতন–নিপীড়ন।

headline_en: Qatar will take new Bangladeshi workers; who will hear the cries of those already there?
destination_promised: Qatar (told work would be easy to find once inside and earnings high)
route_and_actual_destination: Qatar; workers end up jobless around Doha looking for day labour
promised_job_and_wage: No specific job; 'once you get into Qatar you will find work easily and earn a lot'
visa_type_claimed: 'Free visa' (worker sent without a specific job; a company name is on paper but there is no work)
how_money_was_raised: Land sale, high-interest loans, family debt
perpetrator_type: brokers and some licensed recruiting agencies; village-level middlemen
trust_devices: company name on the visa papers; verbal assurance that work is easy to find; fake contract papers (general)
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Qatar: no assured job exists; the company is on paper only
what_happened_abroad: Workers look for day labour or temporary work illegally, wait weeks without work, go months unpaid, some become undocumented, face police harassment, arrest or deportation, and lack food and medical care. Column links the shortage of work to the end of World Cup 2022 construction.
victims_count: 'thousands' (author's estimate, no figure)
harm: Debt, joblessness, unpaid wages, loss of legal status, risk of arrest and deportation
advice_or_warning_in_article: Author Dr Selim Reza (Centre for Migration Studies, North South University): no worker should go without a contract for a specific job; stop sending workers on 'free visas'.
other_practical_details: Opinion column, based on the author's conversations with workers in Qatar; no named victims. Qatar's labour minister said about 473,000 Bangladeshis work in Qatar and Qatar wants skilled workers (electricians, plumbers, welders, AC technicians) directly from five named TTCs.
key_quote_bn: কোম্পানির নাম কাগজে থাকলেও বাস্তবে কাজ নেই। তখন তাঁরা অবৈধভাবে দিনমজুরি বা অস্থায়ী কাজের সন্ধানে ঘুরতে থাকেন।

headline_en: Could not be saved even after paying BDT 4.8 million ransom, family says
route_and_actual_destination: Bangladesh to Dubai to Libya; held in a detention house in Libya; died in a Libyan hospital
amount_per_person: BDT 2,500,000 taken first for the journey; family says BDT 4,800,000 paid in all (article itemises 2,500,000 + 2,000,000 ransom + 250,000 for 'treatment')
amount_total: BDT 4,800,000 (family's figure)
how_money_was_raised: Sold all the family's land
perpetrator_type: village broker (from the neighbouring village) with Bangladeshi brokers living in Libya
perpetrator_names: Rafiqul Islam alias Bagha Dalal, of Purba Swarmangal village (next to victim's village), Rajoir, Madaripur
how_victim_met_them: Broker from the neighbouring village; details of approach not given
timeline: Left home about eight months before his death; died Tuesday about 1 pm Bangladesh time (week of 13 May 2026)
how_it_was_discovered: After arrival in Libya he was locked in a detention house and tortured, and ransom was demanded from the family
what_happened_abroad: Tachir Fakir (40), a tea-stall owner, was confined and tortured in Libya; after ransom was paid he fell seriously ill, was admitted to a Libyan hospital, the ring took more money for 'treatment', and he died there. A fellow Bangladeshi detainee phoned to confirm and sent a photo of the body.
victims_count: 1 (article notes three other Madaripur men, two from Dasar and one from Kalkini, died of broker torture in Libya in the previous two months)
harm: Death after repeated torture; family lost about BDT 4.8 million and all land; wife and three daughters left destitute
ransom_details: BDT 2,000,000 ransom extracted from the family by Bangladeshi brokers living in Libya after torture; a further BDT 250,000 taken on the pretext of hospital treatment
official_response: No case yet. Rajoir UNO Mahfuzul Haque: on a written application steps will be taken to bring the body home and legal action taken against the ring. Madaripur Additional SP Jahangir Alam: police sent to the home; action will follow a written complaint at the police station. The broker and his family have fled; his phone is off.
money_recovered: None
other_practical_details: Article says deaths from torture in detention houses (as opposed to boat sinkings) were previously rare. Related headline cites another youth who died after BDT 5,000,000 was taken for Italy.
key_quote_bn: দালাল টাকাও নিল, আমার স্বামীর জীবনডাও কাইড়া নিল। তারে দফায় দফায় নির্যাতন করে মারছে।

headline_en: Brick houses in village after village: how expatriates changed the upazila
route_and_actual_destination: Saudi Arabia; back in Bangladesh after 27 days
how_money_was_raised: Sold his own electronics shop to pay for the visa
trust_devices: fraudulent contract papers between a fake employer and worker (seen by Probashi Kallyan Bank officer in loan applications)
timeline: Returned 27 days after going
what_happened_abroad: Arif Hossain of Santoshpur, Sandwip was cheated after reaching Saudi Arabia and had to return within 27 days (no further detail)
victims_count: 1 named (Arif Hossain)
harm: Lost his shop and all assets
verification_mentioned: Probashi Kallyan Bank Sandwip branch senior officer Tanzim Ul Haque says the bank often sees fraudulent contracts with fake employers and workers
advice_or_warning_in_article: Tanzim Ul Haque (Probashi Kallyan Bank): people still sell their homesteads and go abroad on such papers and end up in trouble. Former UP member Md Samsuddin: fraud will not fall unless action is taken against traffickers; training is needed.
other_practical_details: Mainly a feature on remittance-driven change in Sandwip; the fraud part is short. Sandwip has a government technical training centre near the upazila complex (750 trained last year). BMET: 2,080 people from Sandwip went abroad in 2025.
key_quote_bn: ‘উপার্জনের আশায় নিজের ইলেকট্রনিক পণ্যের দোকানটি বিক্রি করে ভিসা নিয়েছিলাম। এখন আমার আর কোনো সম্বল নেই।’

headline_en: Dream or death journey? What we should do (roundtable, Sylhet, 18 April 2026)
route_and_actual_destination: Bangladesh to Oman (construction work), Dubai, Qatar, back to Dubai; then Oman, Iran, Turkey, Greece, North Macedonia, Serbia, back to Greece; then Bulgaria, Albania, Bosnia, Italy, France; deported from France to Bangladesh
visa_type_claimed: Australian visa, which was fake
amount_per_person: BDT 1,700,000 for the fake Australia visa (cost of the Europe journey not stated)
perpetrator_type: broker and agency (not named)
trust_devices: a visa was actually handed over (fake)
timeline: Worked in France about 4 years 8 months before being caught and returned; the Australia visa fraud came after his return, when he was farming and running a poultry farm
what_happened_abroad: Sujon Mia (Simtola village, Chhatak upazila, Sunamganj) left Oman over an iqama problem, worked in Dubai and Qatar, then travelled overland to Europe, working illegally to survive in several countries. In France he worked about 4 years 8 months, paid tax and completed the regularisation process, but was caught and sent back before the legal papers arrived.
harm: Deported from France before regularisation; BDT 1,700,000 lost to a fake Australian visa
official_response: None for his case. Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury said the government has declared zero tolerance for the broker syndicate and will identify Bangladeshi members of trafficking rings in Libya and elsewhere, bring them back and try them.
verification_mentioned: Md Nazmus Sakib (assistant director, District Employment and Manpower Office, Sylhet): the office registers people who want to go abroad through the government route, takes fingerprints and gives a three-day pre-decision training covering legal migration and avoiding brokers; he called for a rating system so people can pick the right agency. Hafiz Ahmed (director, Osmani airport) wants embassies to publish what each country costs and what work is available.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Mahbubul Mannan Chowdhury (acting regional head, Probashi Kallyan Bank, Sylhet): by the ministry's list, going abroad through the government route costs about BDT 160,000-170,000, but most people spend over BDT 400,000-500,000 through agencies; many take BDT 300,000-400,000 bank loans with instalments of about BDT 14,000 a month, and it can take 4-5 months or more to get work abroad. Nazmus Sakib: about 2,900 licensed agencies are all Dhaka-based; only a few agencies work directly in Sylhet, the rest act as brokers behind travel agencies and take more than the fixed limit. Mohammad Nasir Uddin (general secretary, Sylhet District Press Club): about 150 travel agencies in Sylhet are licensed but over 500 operate illegally, taking BDT 800,000 to 2,000,000 per person. Joni Lal Deb (ASP, 7 APBn, Osmani airport): trafficking and smuggling groups operate around the airport and target first-time travellers, including to carry drugs or contraband without understanding it. Shariful Islam Hasan (BRAC): Bangladeshis are the largest group crossing the Mediterranean; Madaripur, Shariatpur, Sylhet, Sunamganj, Habiganj and a few other districts are the main sources. Muktabis-un-Noor (president, Sylhet Press Club): even legally, many workers in the Middle East do not get the promised job and pay; women face sexual harassment; students who go abroad to study and stay to work end up in legal trouble. Md Salah Uddin (deputy director, passport office): learn the destination language and a skill first. Jakir Hossain (senior instructor, Sylhet TTC): about 99% go with no skill; Saudi Arabia now takes workers through skill verification.
other_practical_details: Passport fees (Sylhet passport office): regular 5-year BDT 4,025, 10-year BDT 5,750, super express BDT 10,350; apply with NID if 18 or over, birth registration if under 18; fee paid at a bank, then fingerprints; super express can deliver the same afternoon in Dhaka. Sylhet TTC runs Japanese, Italian, Korean and Arabic language courses and ILO-supported level-3 courses in electrical installation and food preparation, with a possible route to jobs in Italy. Probashi Kallyan Bank offers rehabilitation loans at 8% interest. Victims heard at the meeting had spent BDT 1,000,000-2,000,000 (airport director). Sylhet manpower office registered 35,290 people in 2025. The minister mentioned a planned 'Probashi card' with Bangladesh Bank to replace cash dealings with brokers. Commissioner Khan Md Reza-un-Nabi noted people are tortured for money in Libya.

key_quote_bn: এ সময় দালাল ও এজেন্সি ১৭ লাখ টাকা নিয়ে আমাকে ভুয়া ভিসা দিয়েছিল।

headline_en: Manpower export from the Cumilla region: prospects, challenges and what to do (roundtable)
destination_promised: Oman, then Saudi Arabia (returnee Fatema Akter; job type not stated)
route_and_actual_destination: Oman for five years, home on leave, then Saudi Arabia for two years; returned to Bangladesh sick
promised_job_and_wage: Promised wage not stated. Actual: BDT 12,000 in Oman (period not stated); in Saudi Arabia about BDT 3,000 for some of the time
perpetrator_type: Foreign employer (Fatema's case). Pattern described by speakers: dishonest agencies and unlicensed brokers
timeline: Five years in Oman, two years in Saudi Arabia
how_it_was_discovered: On the job abroad
what_happened_abroad: Fatema Akter: not given proper food, often poor-quality food; bad accommodation; made to work all the time; wages not paid regularly; not looked after. She fell ill in Saudi Arabia and had to come home.
victims_count: 1 named returnee; RMMRU research cited: about 31% of people who go abroad are cheated in some way
victim_home_districts: Cumilla region (district not stated for Fatema)
harm: Very low and irregular wages, poor food and housing, overwork, illness. She cannot go again: she is older and her passport shows an even higher age; she is now sick at home.
official_response: No case mentioned. Md Yusuf Molla (administrator, Cumilla City Corporation) said politicians receive many such complaints and have to pressure the middlemen to deliver or refund. Md Main Uddin (assistant director, Probashi Kallyan Centre, Cumilla): workers in trouble abroad can apply through the centre for legal help via the embassy.
money_recovered: Jesia Khatun (director, WARBE Development Foundation): a significant amount of money was recovered through mediation over the last three years (no figure). Yusuf Molla: pressure is applied on middlemen to refund.
verification_mentioned: Saiful Malik (additional SP, Sadar circle, Cumilla police): after registration, training, the contract and the bank account should be verified before final approval; papers should be verified before departure; without documents it is hard for police to act. Kamruzzaman (principal, TTC Cumilla): union parishads often do not know who from their area is going abroad.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Yusuf Molla: dishonest agencies lure people, take everything and do not send them; people sell land or borrow and are cheated; many who do go do not get the promised job or wage. Md Saiful Islam (additional deputy commissioner): with no one-stop service people turn to brokers, who handle the whole process, and the migrant often does not know how or at what cost he is going. Saiful Malik: many go through brokers without a valid contract and become irregular, are unpaid or confined; people should be encouraged to go through government channels such as BOESL, whose workers are comparatively better off. Md Atikur Rahman (assistant director, DEMO): agencies take excess money from unskilled and uneducated people. Badrul Huda (president, Multi-Party Advocacy Forum, Cumilla): someone who does not fully know what to do to avoid being cheated should not try to go. Farzana Alam Majumdar (BAIRA member, Cumilla): the main problems are unlicensed brokers, false promises, cash transactions, fraud and hiding the contract; payments should go through banks. Marina Sultana (director, programme, RMMRU): fraud happens at every step from the passport onward; lack of basic language and communication skills leads to abuse and low pay. Iqbal Mahmud (deputy team leader, The Asia Foundation): the 2023 amendment to the overseas employment law and January 2025 rules provide for regulating brokers (sub-agents), but registration has made little progress. Kamruzzaman: sending remittance through banks reduces fraud.
other_practical_details: Probashi Kallyan Bank (Rawnak Jahan, senior officer, Cumilla region): a loan applicant needs a BMET card, valid visa, passport and an NID from their own area, plus a capable guarantor; there are only four branches in Cumilla, and the Cumilla branch at Thomson Bridge covers 9 of 17 upazilas with three officers. Probashi Kallyan Centre (Main Uddin): district office of the Wage Earners' Welfare Board, started July 2023; education stipends for workers' children and an allowance for disabled children; financial help to bring a body home for BMET card holders; free ambulance from the airport; BDT 25,000 after the body arrives and up to BDT 300,000 in eligible cases; help recovering unpaid insurance and compensation through the embassy; overnight stay at the Wage Earners' dormitory near the airport; safe homes abroad for women workers and lawyers appointed at embassies. Saiful Malik: people with no case against them get police clearance within the set time; if it takes longer, contact the office. Yusuf Molla: discussing collateral-free loans of BDT 500,000 to 1,200,000 for returnees with some banks. Jesia Khatun: recruiting agencies are Dhaka-based, which is why brokers matter in the field. Md Ishaq (deputy director, Department of Youth Development): wants at least 15 days of compulsory language training.
key_quote_bn: ওমানে পাঁচ বছর কাজ করেছি মাত্র বারো হাজার টাকা বেতনে। আর সৌদি আরবে দুই বছর কাজ করে কিছুদিন প্রায় তিন হাজার টাকার মতো বেতন পেয়েছি।

headline_en: Who will rein in the death journey across the Mediterranean?
route_and_actual_destination: Classic route described: by air to Kenya (posing as safari/tourism), overland to Libya, then boat; held in Libyan detention houses; 113 returned to Dhaka from Libya (repatriation of 31 March 2026). Traffickers now use the Greece route because of tighter watch on the Italy route.
amount_per_person: One returnee paid BDT 8.2 million in stages, another BDT 7.3 million; more than 50 of the 113 said they paid over BDT 2 million to brokers
payment_method: in stages (instalments)
how_money_was_raised: One returnee said the homestead land was sold
perpetrator_type: broker/trafficking ring; Bangladeshis in Libya among the torturers; ransom collectors living in Bangladesh
timeline: One returnee had lived in Libya 14 years before attempting the 'game' (boat crossing)
what_happened_abroad: Held in Libya with almost no food (rice once in 20-25 days, one bowl shared by five; bread thrown at them; beatings). People are handed from group to group like goods; before boarding boats they are held in detention houses, tortured, and videos sent to relatives for more money.
victims_count: 113 returnees on one flight; about two-thirds from Madaripur. Boat of 4 April from Tajoura, Libya towards Lampedusa with about 105 people sank: 32 rescued, 2 bodies, 71 missing (Bangladeshis among them). Boat of 21 March towards Greece with 48 people: 26 rescued after six days adrift (21 Bangladeshi); 20 of the 22 dead or missing were Bangladeshi.
harm: Money lost (up to BDT 8.2 million each), starvation, beatings, deaths and disappearances at sea, returned empty-handed
ransom_details: Torture videos sent to families in Bangladesh; ransom collected in Bangladesh by people living there (no amounts for specific cases)
official_response: IOM paid air fare and travel home for the 113. Author (former foreign affairs adviser Touhid Hossain) argues returnees should be detained and questioned to identify who took the money and who collected ransom, with state protection for victims against threats.
money_recovered: None; returnees went home empty-handed
advice_or_warning_in_article: Touhid Hossain: a victim starts breaking the law from the moment he boards a flight to Kenya on a false safari/tourism story; irregular migration is making Bangladesh fall behind in legal labour migration.
other_practical_details: Account of the returnees comes from Bangladesh's ambassador to Libya, Maj Gen Habib Ullah. 'Game' is the migrants' word for the boat crossing.
key_quote_bn: একজন ধাপে ধাপে বিরাশি লাখ টাকা দিয়েছেন দালাল-মাফিয়াদের। একজন পাওয়া গেল তিয়াত্তর লাখ টাকা দেওয়া শেষ।

headline_en: No going abroad by sea
destination_promised: Europe (Greece/Italy via Libya); individual cases: Australia, UK (study), Saudi Arabia
route_and_actual_destination: Libya then boat towards Greece (two Sunamganj men died after boat lost its way); Sujon Mia: Middle East, then about 25 countries irregularly to France, detained by police and returned
promised_job_and_wage: Shahriar Zaman (UK): brokers said he could work legally alongside study; in practice he worked illegally at GBP 1 an hour where others got GBP 8
visa_type_claimed: Student visa (UK case); Australia visa (type not stated)
amount_per_person: BDT 1,700,000 paid by Sujon Mia for an Australia visa he believes is fake
perpetrator_type: village broker
trust_devices: issued visa (Australia) that the victim now believes is fake; promise of legal work alongside study
timeline: Shahriar Zaman was in the UK about 8 years (article also says 10 years); Ruksana Begum returned from Saudi about two years ago
how_it_was_discovered: Sujon Mia cannot travel on the Australia visa and suspects it is fake; Shahriar found no legal work on arrival in the UK
what_happened_abroad: Sujon Mia detained by police in France before he could regularise and sent back. Shahriar Zaman worked illegally for GBP 1/hour. Ruksana Begum (Bishwanath, Sylhet) went to Saudi Arabia through a broker, was given no permanent job and was abused in several ways.
victims_count: 3 returnees spoke; families of 2 Sunamganj men who died on a Libya-Greece boat also spoke
victim_home_districts: Sylhet (Bishwanath), Sunamganj; high-risk districts named: Madaripur, Shariatpur, Sylhet, Sunamganj, Habiganj, Kishoreganj
harm: Deaths at sea (two Sunamganj men); deportation from France; BDT 1.7 million lost on a suspected fake visa; underpaid illegal work; abuse in Saudi Arabia
ransom_details: Sylhet Divisional Commissioner: people are tortured in Libya and the video is shown to relatives to extract money (no amounts)
official_response: Expatriates' Welfare Minister Ariful Haque Chowdhury: zero-tolerance policy against the 'mafia syndicate'; plan for a 'Probashi Card' with Bangladesh Bank so payments go through a system instead of cash to brokers. Airport APBn says it is working to identify trafficking groups active around Sylhet airport.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Speakers: there is no legal way to go abroad by sea; legal departure is only through Dhaka, Chattogram and Sylhet airports. Sylhet airport director Hafiz Ahmed: follow training, registration and later monitoring steps. APBn ASP Joni Lal Deb: groups around the airport lure ordinary passengers with offers.
other_practical_details: Roundtable by BRAC and Prothom Alo with EU support, Sylhet, 18 April 2026. BRAC says it has assisted about 39,000 people at the airport over eight years and supports returnees from Europe with counselling and business start-up help. Press club president: many women workers face sexual harassment in the Middle East.
key_quote_bn: দেশে ফেরার পর ১৭ লাখ টাকা দিয়ে অস্ট্রেলিয়ার ভিসা করিয়েছিলেন; কিন্তু ওই ভিসায় তিনি এখন যেতে পারছেন না। তাঁর ধারণা ভিসাটি জাল।

headline_en: Promised Australia but taken to Nepal; parents cannot trace their son
route_and_actual_destination: Taken from home in Jashore on 12 September 2025 and to Kathmandu, Nepal, on 14 September; kept in a hotel there; never reached Australia
promised_job_and_wage: Labourer post in an Australian company, BDT 100,000 a month
visa_type_claimed: Australian worker (labour) visa
amount_per_person: BDT 1,500,000 fee, plus BDT 150,000 ransom, plus dollars worth BDT 100,000 taken from him in Nepal
amount_total: BDT 1,650,000 paid by the family, plus the BDT 100,000 in dollars taken
payment_method: Instalments: BDT 300,000 first, then BDT 1,200,000 after fake visa-grant papers were shown; the BDT 150,000 ransom was sent by mobile banking
how_money_was_raised: Sold 8 decimals of land with a lychee orchard in a hurry for only BDT 400,000; loans from five NGOs and a village samity at high interest (BDT 1,100,000); sold his engine van, his only source of income, for BDT 50,000; a further BDT 100,000 samity loan at interest. Total loans about BDT 1,250,000.
perpetrator_type: relative or neighbour (two brothers from the same village, one a returnee from abroad)
perpetrator_names: Tarikul Islam (45) and Nazmul Hossain (35), sons of Mokles Mollya, Kismat Mahmudpur village, Bagharpara upazila, Jashore
how_victim_met_them: Neighbours in the same village; Nazmul had lived abroad for a long time (Malaysia, according to his sister-in-law) and returned two years earlier; the brothers said they had obtained some Australian labour visas
trust_devices: broker was a returnee from abroad from the same village; fake Australian government visa-grant papers; medical test and fingerprinting in Uttara, Dhaka; promise to place him in the job within three months
timeline: Taken from home 12 September 2025; in Kathmandu from 14 September; court case filed 16 February 2026; last phone contact 9 March 2026, phone switched off from 12 March; still missing in mid-April 2026
how_it_was_discovered: When he was held in a Kathmandu hotel, his passport and dollars were taken, and money was demanded with threats; he told his parents by phone that he was being tortured
what_happened_abroad: Confined in a hotel in Kathmandu; passport and dollars worth BDT 100,000 taken; threatened and then physically and mentally tortured to extract more money; contact lost
victims_count: 1 (Sakib Hossain, 21, a class 12 college student)
harm: Son missing; about BDT 1,650,000 lost; land and the van sold; about BDT 1,250,000 of interest-bearing debt and no income; threats by phone from the brokers' people after the case was filed
ransom_details: BDT 150,000 demanded while he was held and paid by mobile banking (BDT 50,000 from the van sale plus BDT 100,000 loan); a further BDT 300,000 was then demanded to bring him back, which the father could not pay
official_response: Father filed a case on 16 February 2026 at the Human Trafficking and Migrant Smuggling Prevention and Suppression Tribunal-1, Jashore; the court ordered Bagharpara police to record it as an FIR, which was done. Investigating officer SI Gobinda Kumar Mondal says the investigation and efforts to arrest are ongoing. Both accused are absconding with phones off.
money_recovered: None
other_practical_details: Sequence of the trick: a small first payment (BDT 300,000), then fake visa-grant papers a few days later to trigger the balance, then a medical test and fingerprints in Dhaka, then removal to a third country (Nepal) where the passport is taken and ransom demanded. The accused Tarikul's wife says her husband was not involved and was named because of Nazmul.
key_quote_bn: এরপর তাঁরা আলমগীরকে অস্ট্রেলিয়া সরকারের ভিসা মঞ্জুরের ভুয়া কাগজপত্র দিয়ে অবশিষ্ট ১২ লাখ টাকা দাবি করেন।

Marina Sultana (RMMRU): 31 percent of people who go abroad are cheated, because there is no law for intermediaries. Farzana Alam Majumder (BAIRA member): main problems are false promises, fraud in cash transactions and keeping the contract hidden.

headline_en: Expatriates cannot be looked down on; the money they send keeps the economy running
perpetrator_type: sub-agents and brokers (general pattern, roundtable discussion)
verification_mentioned: None exists for sub-agents: speakers note there is no law or registration for intermediaries. Recommendations made: BMET should register all sub-agents; a single national migration database; legal bank transactions to be made mandatory.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Saiful Malik (Additional SP, Cumilla): people are cheated mostly because they do not know the rules, and those who go by irregular channels face the most problems; train before going (computer and driving skills raise demand and pay). Marina Sultana (RMMRU): 31 percent of people who go abroad are cheated, because there is no law for intermediaries. Farzana Alam Majumder (BAIRA member, sub-agent): the main problems are false promises, fraud in cash transactions, and keeping the contract hidden.
other_practical_details: Roundtable in Cumilla on 11 April 2026 (Democracy International and Prothom Alo). Problems listed by WARBE: going without skills, broker fraud, excess cost, not getting wages or papers abroad. Abroad: abuse, overwork, withheld wages, no help with complaints. Officials admit there is no one-stop service, which is why people turn to brokers. Probashi Kallyan Bank has only 4 branches for Cumilla's 17 upazilas; the Tomsom Bridge branch has 3 staff serving 9 upazilas. Proposals: migration information desks ('migration corners') and complaint committees at union level. No specific fraud case is described.
key_quote_bn: বিদেশে যাওয়া ৩১ শতাংশ মানুষ প্রতারণার শিকার হন মাধ্যমকারীদের জন্য কোনো আইন না থাকার কারণে।
