headline_en: Impunity makes human traffickers reckless (editorial)
route_and_actual_destination: Libya, then a rubber boat towards Greece that lost its way in the Mediterranean and drifted for six days
how_money_was_raised: The poor family sold their last assets, cows and land
perpetrator_type: brokers (not named)
timeline: Boat left on 21 March 2026 and drifted six days
how_it_was_discovered: The boat lost its way at sea and food ran out
what_happened_abroad: Died of starvation on the drifting boat; bodies were thrown into the sea
victims_count: 20 Bangladeshi young men dead or feared missing; 12 of the dead from Sunamganj
harm: Death by starvation at sea (Shayek Ahmed, 23, and others); BDT 1,200,000 and the family's land and cattle lost
official_response: Home Ministry figures: about 4,500 trafficking cases in 2020 to 2024, with 94 to 95 percent of accused acquitted; most incidents never become cases.
other_practical_details: CID: 17,000 Bangladeshis were sent to Italy by irregular routes in the past year. The editorial also notes trafficking rings active towards Malaysia and Australia and deaths of young men sent to Russia with high-wage promises who ended up on the Ukraine battlefield.
key_quote_bn: গত ২১ মার্চ রওনা দেওয়া রাবারের নৌকাটি ভূমধ্যসাগরে পথ হারিয়ে ছয় দিন ভেসে ছিল। খাবার ফুরিয়ে যাওয়ায় অনাহারে তাঁর মৃত্যু হয়।

headline_en: People die, no one is tried, trafficking does not stop
route_and_actual_destination: Sent to Libya, where he ended up in jail; returned to Bangladesh after a long time in jail. Typical Italy route per analysis: Bangladesh to Nepal, India or Sri Lanka, then Dubai, then Egypt or Tunisia, then Libya, then across the Mediterranean.
amount_per_person: BDT 500,000 (Delowar Hossain's family)
how_money_was_raised: Borrowed at interest from a samity (savings group) and acquaintances
perpetrator_type: village broker; organised international trafficking network
how_it_was_discovered: He was sent to Libya instead of Italy and jailed there
what_happened_abroad: Jailed in Libya for a long time. General findings: people are kidnapped on the way and tortured for ransom, held in prisons without papers, and some forced into prostitution.
victims_count: 1 in the main case; CID says more than 17,000 Bangladeshis were sent to Italy this way in the past year
victim_home_districts: Patuakhali (Kalapara, main case); CID trafficking hotspots: Madaripur, Shariatpur, Jashore, Cox's Bazar, Cumilla, Sylhet, Faridpur
harm: Imprisonment in Libya; family unable to repay the BDT 500,000 loan
ransom_details: General: ransom collected from families after kidnapping and torture on the route; in the 2024 Christmas Island case ransom was collected in Bangladesh (no amounts given)
official_response: Home Ministry: of 4,427 cases under the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act in 2020 to 2024, 94 to 95 percent of accused were acquitted. CID anti-trafficking unit: 536 cases in 2018 to 2025 with 1,657 accused, only 353 arrested. Over the 2020 Mizda (Libya) killing of 26 Bangladeshis, CID investigated 14 cases with 222 accused, 136 arrested, and 4 Interpol red notices. RAB arrested two members of a fake-visa ring (announced 30 March 2026).
advice_or_warning_in_article: Md Sibgat Ullah (Additional IGP, former CID chief): evidence is hard to produce because events happen abroad, and victims often settle once they get money back, so accused are acquitted. Tasneem Siddiqui (RMMRU): routes are now multi-layered and run by disconnected rings; if the state holds everyone to account, trafficking from inside the country can largely be controlled.
other_practical_details: Other cases and routes: (1) about 22 migrants dead or missing on a boat from Libya to Greece, 20 believed Bangladeshi; 26 of 48 rescued on 26 March 2026. (2) 2024: 41 Bangladeshis taken from Malaysia to Indonesia and then by sea to Australia's Christmas Island, with ransom collected at home. (3) 2024: Bangladeshis lured with chocolate factory jobs in Russia, routed via Saudi Arabia and forced into the Ukraine war; two arrested, one a Russian national. (4) Marriage lure to China: 10 arrested including two Chinese nationals. (5) Fake-visa ring for Australia and Europe took up to BDT 2,000,000 per victim. Routes: Thailand to Cambodia or Laos; Brazil then Mexico to the US; Dubai as transit to Serbia and Macedonia; Nepal route for Canada; Cox's Bazar coast by sea to South-East Asia; Indian land border most used. CID: 6,260 Bangladeshis brought back from Libya between October 2022 and December 2025 (3,463 in 2025). BRAC 2024 study of 557 Libya returnees: 63 percent were imprisoned, 79 percent of those physically tortured, 54 percent never got three meals a day. IOM: 559 deaths in the Mediterranean in January and February 2026 against 287 a year earlier. CID has an office at Dhaka's Shahjalal airport.
key_quote_bn: সমিতি ও পরিচিতদের থেকে সুদে পাঁচ লাখ টাহা নিয়া পোলারে বিদেশ পাডাইছি (পাঠিয়েছি)। পোলা বিপদে পড়ছে। লোনের টাহাও দিতে পারতেছি না।

headline_en: Two Bangladeshi young men die in Libyan detention camp; families wait for the bodies
route_and_actual_destination: Elias: Qatar (where he had worked for about three years) to Libya in early August 2025. Faruk: Bangladesh via Saudi Arabia to Libya about four months before his death. Both were held in a detention camp in Libya and never reached Italy.
amount_per_person: BDT 2,000,000 from Elias's family; BDT 1,200,000 from Faruk's family
amount_total: BDT 3,200,000 from the two families
payment_method: Elias's family paid in several instalments, handed to the broker Habib Master
perpetrator_type: village broker working with a Libya trafficking ring; Bangladeshi broker in Qatar
perpetrator_names: Habib Master alias Habibur Rahman Khandaker, of Gopalpur area, Dasar upazila, Madaripur, a former madrasa teacher; an unnamed Bangladeshi broker in Qatar who lured Elias
how_victim_met_them: Elias was lured by a Bangladeshi broker while working in Qatar; Faruk went through the local broker Habibur Rahman
trust_devices: local broker known in the area who had sent more than 300 young men from Kalkini and Dasar to Italy via Libya
timeline: Elias: reached Libya early August 2025, died 23 March 2026 (about 8 months held); family told 4 days later. Faruk: left about 4 months earlier, died 18 March 2026; family told 25 March.
how_it_was_discovered: Elias's family learned he had gone only after he reached Libya; the deaths were concealed and the families were told days later through a local broker
what_happened_abroad: Both were held in a detention camp ('game ghor') in Libya and tortured physically and mentally to extract money from their families; both died from the torture
victims_count: 2 dead; locals say the same broker still has at least 100 migrants in Libyan detention
harm: Two deaths under torture in detention (Elias Howlader, 25; Faruk Howlader, 35); BDT 2,000,000 and BDT 1,200,000 lost; bodies not yet returned
ransom_details: BDT 2,000,000 in several instalments from Elias's family, paid to Habib Master; BDT 1,200,000 from Faruk's family, extracted while he was held
official_response: No case filed yet; Madaripur police superintendent says a case will be taken if the families complain and that operations to catch brokers continue. The broker has long been out of police reach.
money_recovered: None. The broker met Elias's family in Dhaka and promised to bring the body home and pay compensation, without giving a date.
other_practical_details: Faruk's family say they are not going to police for now because the broker has said he will bring the body, and they fear he will not if they seek justice first. Elias's father said both his sons were doing well in Qatar before Elias left without telling the family. Faruk was a mason in Bangladesh.
key_quote_bn: ছেলের মুখের দিকে চাইয়ে আমি অনেক কষ্ট করে ২০ লাখ টাকা দালাল হাবিব মাস্টারের কাছে দিই। তবুও আমার ছেলেডা মরে গেল।

perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency syndicate; official

key_quote_bn: মালয়েশিয়ায় কর্মী পাঠানোর নাম করে চক্র গড়ে তুলে বিপুল পরিমাণ অর্থ আত্মসাৎ করার অভিযোগ রয়েছে।

headline_en: The American dream and Bangladeshis in the maze of immigration fraud
destination_promised: United States (permanent residence or green card)
route_and_actual_destination: Brokers bring people only as far as crossing the southern or northern US border, according to the columnist
visa_type_claimed: Green card through 'investment', as advertised
amount_per_person: USD 60,000 taken from one person in New York; brokers charge BDT 5,000,000 to 6,000,000 per person to bring someone across the US border
amount_total: Millions of dollars in the US; crores of taka from thousands of people in Dhaka (no exact figure)
perpetrator_type: fake immigration lawyer and his firm (Bangladeshi in New York); unlicensed office in Dhaka
perpetrator_names: Not named: a Bangladeshi in New York posing as an immigration attorney and his firm, with offices in upscale areas of Dhaka
how_victim_met_them: Flashy advertisements in mainstream media and on social media
trust_devices: false identity as an immigration attorney; well-furnished offices in upscale areas of Dhaka; flashy advertisements promising a green card for an 'investment' of BDT 5 to 6 million
victims_count: Thousands in Dhaka, plus Bangladeshi and other migrants in the US (no exact number)
harm: Money lost; victims left destitute
official_response: None reported; the fraud was exposed in a report by ABC Channel 7 in New York and other media

The columnist says the brokers do not care what happens to the person after the border crossing or whether they are caught, and that even highly educated Bangladeshis have been cheated by such 'lawyers'.
key_quote_bn: প্রতারকেরা জনপ্রতি ৫০ থেকে ৬০ লাখ টাকা নেয় শুধু যুক্তরাষ্ট্রের দক্ষিণ কিংবা উত্তর সীমান্ত দিয়ে একজনকে নিয়ে আসার জন্য।

headline_en: Masud Uddin Chowdhury remanded in human trafficking case
amount_per_person: BDT 150,000 extra per worker, extorted from the complainant recruiting agent
amount_total: BDT 12 crore 56 lakh 1 thousand for 841 workers from the complainant; about BDT 24,000 crore allegedly extorted from other recruiting businesses
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency syndicate; official
perpetrator_names: Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, managing director of M International Limited [এম ইন্টারন্যাশনাল লিমিটেড], former Feni-3 MP; co-accused: former expatriates' welfare minister Imran Ahmed, former secretary Ahmed Munirus Salehin, Benzir Ahmed (owner of Ahmed International, former MP), Md Ruhul Amin Swapan (owner of Catharsis International); 103 accused in all
victims_count: 841 workers' extra payments cited in the complaint (the complainant is a recruiting agency owner)

headline_en: Masud Uddin: 1/11, power, rewards and controversy
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency syndicate; official
perpetrator_names: Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, former Feni-3 MP, who obtained a recruiting licence after retiring in 2014
official_response: Arrested by Dhaka DB at his Baridhara DOHS home on the night of 23 March 2026 and remanded for 5 days in the Paltan human trafficking case, filed 3 September of the previous year by Altab Khan, owner of Afia Overseas, against 103 accused. DB says he faces 11 cases in Feni and Dhaka (murder, attempted murder, human trafficking and others); the Anti-Corruption Commission and CID are investigating several allegations.
other_practical_details: Mostly a political profile of his role in the 2007 military-backed takeover. On migration it says only that he was accused of making huge sums through a syndicate for sending workers to Malaysia; the prosecutor told the court he 'took BDT 24,000 crore in the name of sending people abroad'.

headline_en: The government must take a hard line (editorial)
route_and_actual_destination: Died on the way in an unfamiliar country (place not stated in the editorial)
how_money_was_raised: Loan of BDT 900,000, beyond the family's means
perpetrator_type: village broker (broker rings from village to city)
trust_devices: stories of success abroad; examples of relatives who prospered abroad; promise of a valid visa and safe journey; local brokers using social ties to win trust
how_it_was_discovered: Pattern described: the journey starts with a promise of a valid visa and safe travel, then the route changes midway
what_happened_abroad: Pattern described: long journeys through jungle and borders with hunger, illness and insecurity; in many cases people are held in Libya or elsewhere and torture videos are sent to families to extract ransom

key_quote_bn: বৈধ ভিসা ও নিরাপদ যাত্রার প্রতিশ্রুতি দিয়ে শুরু হলেও মাঝপথে বদলে যায় রুট।

headline_en: Fraud rings and traffickers must be stopped (editorial)
destination_promised: Russia (ordinary civilian jobs such as cook or cleaner)
route_and_actual_destination: Russia, then the front line of the Ukraine war
promised_job_and_wage: Cook or cleaner; wage not stated
perpetrator_type: recruiting agency; Bangladeshi already abroad (ringleader living in Moscow)
perpetrator_names: 'SP Global' [এসপি গ্লোবাল] named as one such firm; ringleader described as a Bangladeshi living in Moscow (not named)
how_it_was_discovered: After arrival in Russia, when they were forced to sign a military contract written in Russian; one Russian commander told a victim he had been 'sold'
what_happened_abroad: Forced to sign Russian-language military contracts and pushed to the front; made to collect bodies from the battlefield and move the wounded; those who refused were tortured
victims_count: At least 40 Bangladeshis believed killed in recent months
harm: Deaths in the war (at least 40 believed dead), torture of those who refused, unknown number still trapped
official_response: Editorial says an inquiry committee and cases against traffickers are not enough; calls for high-level diplomatic talks with Russia, a count of those trapped, their return, and cancellation of the licences of the agencies involved. Investigators suspect the ring colluded with Russian authorities.
other_practical_details: Based on an Associated Press investigation. Recruiters target people from disadvantaged areas. Victims could not read the Russian contract they were made to sign.
key_quote_bn: সেখানে পৌঁছানোর পর রুশ ভাষায় লেখা সামরিক চুক্তিতে তাঁদের জোরপূর্বক সই করিয়ে নেওয়া হয়।

headline_en: US embassy in Dhaka explains how the 'visa bond pilot programme' works
destination_promised: United States (B1/B2 business or tourist visa)
visa_type_claimed: B1/B2 visit visa
amount_per_person: Visa bond of up to USD 15,000 (about BDT 1,835,000)
perpetrator_type: online contact (third-party websites; warning only, no case reported)
advice_or_warning_in_article: US Embassy Dhaka: do not pay the bond before the interview; paying early does not guarantee a visa, third-party websites may be fraudulent, and money paid before the interview is not refundable.
other_practical_details: Procedure per the embassy: after the interview, if eligible, the consular officer gives payment instructions with a direct pay.gov link; the bond must be paid within 30 days; a single-entry visa valid for at most 3 months is issued; entry only through designated ports of entry; after return, if all conditions were met (including not working in the US and leaving on time) the bond is cancelled automatically and the money refunded. In force from 21 January 2026. No fraud case is reported in the article.
key_quote_bn: ভিসা ইন্টারভিউর পর যোগ্য হলে কনসুলার কর্মকর্তা আপনাকে ‘pay.gov’–এর সরাসরি লিংকসহ পরিশোধের নির্দেশনা দেবেন।

visa_type_claimed: B1/B2 visit visa

perpetrator_type: online contact (third-party websites; warning only, no case reported)
advice_or_warning_in_article: US Embassy Dhaka (verified Facebook page, 19 January 2026): do not pay the bond before the interview; paying early does not guarantee a visa, third-party websites may be fraudulent, and money paid before the interview is not refundable.
other_practical_details: From 21 January 2026, Bangladeshis approved for a B1/B2 visa must post a bond of up to USD 15,000; holders of valid B1/B2 visas issued before that date are exempt; the bond is refunded if visa conditions are followed. Bangladesh is one of 38 countries on the list. No fraud case is reported in the article.
key_quote_bn: সাক্ষাৎকারের আগে বন্ড পরিশোধ করবেন না। আগাম বন্ড পরিশোধ করলে তা ভিসার নিশ্চয়তা দেয় না এবং তৃতীয় পক্ষের ওয়েবসাইট প্রতারণামূলক হতে পারে।

headline_en: 35 workers return from Russia after losing their jobs
route_and_actual_destination: Went to Russia with BMET clearance in July 2025; placed with a different company from the one on the clearance; sent back to Dhaka on a Qatar Airways flight
promised_job_and_wage: Factory worker under the contract; wage not stated
amount_per_person: About BDT 700,000 each on average
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency (sent with BMET clearance; not named) and foreign employer
perpetrator_names: Recruiting agency not named. Russian company named on the BMET clearance: Mars International Limited Trade Development [মার্স ইন্টারন্যাশনাল লিমিটেড ট্রেড ডেভেলপমেন্ট]
trust_devices: BMET clearance naming a Russian employer; employment contract for factory work
timeline: Sent July 2025; first 35 returned 18 January 2026 (about six months later)
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Russia: they were placed in a different company from the one named on the clearance and made to do building construction instead of factory work
what_happened_abroad: Employed by a different company, made to do construction work, then dismissed without any clear reason and sent home
victims_count: 35 returned in the first batch; returnees say 120 Bangladeshi workers are being dismissed and sent back in phases
victim_home_districts: Gaibandha, Manikganj, Mymensingh, Sirajganj, Dhaka, Chapainawabganj (the six named complainants)
harm: Job loss and forced return after about six months; about BDT 700,000 spent per person
official_response: None reported. The Expatriates' Welfare Desk and Civil Aviation Security helped at the airport; BRAC Migration Programme gave transport and emergency support.
other_practical_details: Shows that a BMET clearance did not prevent the employer and the job being switched after arrival. Named complainants: Moshiur Rahman (Gaibandha), Asmat Ali (Manikganj), Haiyul Mia (Mymensingh), Azadul Haque (Sirajganj), Prosenjit Rajbongshi (Dhaka), Md Abdullah (Chapainawabganj). Source is a BRAC Migration Programme press release.
key_quote_bn: চুক্তি অনুযায়ী কর্মীদের কারখানার শ্রমিক হিসেবে কাজ দেওয়ার কথা থাকলেও তাদের ভবন নির্মাণের কাজ করানো হয়েছে।

headline_en: Will migrant workers only ever earn their keep?
destination_promised: Saudi Arabia (pest control worker, used as the worked example)
promised_job_and_wage: Pest control worker in Saudi Arabia: set monthly wage 700 riyal (BDT 22,400), 8 hours a day, 2-year contract
amount_per_person: About BDT 570,000 total: about BDT 460,000 recruiting agency fee; about BDT 60,000 for passport, medical test, Takamol certificate, PDO training and police clearance; about BDT 50,000 to sub-agents at various levels
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency and sub-agents (general pattern, column)
harm: Two years' earnings (BDT 537,600) minus living costs (about BDT 200,000) leave BDT 337,600, which does not cover the roughly BDT 570,000 migration cost; shortfall about BDT 232,000, so the worker in effect has to work four years with almost no gain.
other_practical_details: Columnist (Nahid Hasan) says Saudi law requires employers to bear the worker's visa and recruitment costs but this is often not followed. Under the earlier Malaysia G2G system many workers went for only the BDT 35,000 airfare; it ended after recruiting agencies opposed it. Rangpur division has very few licensed agencies, so people there know little about the process and fear broker fraud. No specific victim named.
key_quote_bn: এর বিপরীতে একজন শ্রমিককে বিদেশে পাঠাতে নিয়োগকারী এজেন্সি ফি বাবদ নেয় প্রায় ৪ লাখ ৬০ হাজার টাকা।

headline_en: Citizens going abroad advised to avoid any website other than MyGov
perpetrator_type: online contact (fake websites imitating a government portal)
perpetrator_names: Fake domains named: apostillemygovbd.news, apostille-mygovbd.com (identified, carrying forged certificates); apostile.mygov-bd.com and apostiller-bd.com (shut down)
trust_devices: domain names closely resembling the government's mygov.bd domain; forged apostille certificates
official_response: Ministry of Foreign Affairs wrote to Bangladesh Police in August (2025) asking to shut the fake domains and act against the forgers; two fake sites were shut down; work to identify the forgers and close other fake domains is ongoing. No arrests reported.
advice_or_warning_in_article: a2i (Aspire to Innovate): do not enter any suspicious link or website, or give personal information, anywhere other than https://www.mygov.bd/ for apostille.
other_practical_details: Online apostille (attestation of public documents and certificates for use abroad) is run by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs through the MyGov portal (https://www.mygov.bd) under a2i; about 1.7 million applications were settled in 11 months. A ring is forging 'apostille certificates' using look-alike domains. The article does not report amounts or victims.
key_quote_bn: একটি অসাধু চক্র ‘অ্যাপোস্টিল সনদ’ জালিয়াতির মাধ্যমে প্রতারণামূলক কার্যক্রম চালিয়ে এ সেবার বিশ্বাসযোগ্যতা ক্ষুণ্ণ করার অপচেষ্টায় লিপ্ত রয়েছে।

headline_en: 'They did not take my brother to Italy safely, they killed him on the way'
route_and_actual_destination: Left Bangladesh 8 Oct 2025; India, Sri Lanka, Egypt, then Benghazi, Libya; held in a detention house; put on a boat the night of 1 Nov 2025; shot dead shortly after departure
amount_per_person: BDT 2,200,000 contract, then BDT 2,000,000 more extracted while he was held in Benghazi; BDT 4,200,000 in total
payment_method: Two payments (first BDT 22 lakh, later BDT 20 lakh); method not stated
how_money_was_raised: Father sold all his land
perpetrator_type: Bangladeshi already abroad (neighbour living in Libya) with a relative as local agent
perpetrator_names: Shipon Khan (from the same area, in Libya for 10 years) and his brother Selim Khan, Adityapur village, Kunia union, Madaripur Sadar
how_victim_met_them: Same village; contract made through the broker's brother Selim Khan
trust_devices: neighbour from the same area; locals say he sent over 50 young men from Adityapur to Italy in one year
timeline: Left 8 Oct 2025; killed 1 Nov 2025; family told by a broker on 18 Nov 2025
how_it_was_discovered: A broker told the family on 18 Nov that he had been killed on 1 Nov; the family was never shown the body
what_happened_abroad: Locked in a detention house in Benghazi until a further BDT 20 lakh was paid; put on a migrant boat; pirates attacked soon after departure and he was shot dead; body set adrift at sea
victims_count: 1 (Imran Khan, 25, BA graduate)
harm: Death; BDT 4,200,000 lost; all family land sold
ransom_details: BDT 2,000,000 extracted by the broker ring while he was held in the Benghazi detention house; sister says Shipon took the money by pressure and threats
official_response: Additional SP (crime and investigation) Jahangir Alam: legal action if the family complains; police are looking into it. Shipon and Selim Khan's family have fled their home.
other_practical_details: The agreed price doubled once the migrant was in Libya and could not turn back. Victim was an educated only earning son who could not find a good job at home.
key_quote_bn: বাবার যত জমিজমা ছিল সব বিক্রি করে শিপনকে প্রথমে ২২ লাখ, পরে আরও ২০ লাখ টাকা দিছে।

headline_en: Two 'freeze to death' in the Mediterranean; family gets the news 21 days later
route_and_actual_destination: Dhaka to United Arab Emirates to Libya; boarded an engine boat from the Libyan coast on 14 Oct 2025; died at sea
amount_per_person: BDT 1,500,000 each
amount_total: BDT 3,000,000 from the two families
payment_method: BDT 1,500,000 paid in one go (Jafar's father)
how_money_was_raised: Borrowing (Sirajul's wife)
perpetrator_type: village broker
perpetrator_names: Lokman Sardar, Char Bajitpur village, Madaripur Sadar (denies involvement); an unnamed 'bigger broker' mentioned by his sister-in-law
how_victim_met_them: Same village; people approached him after his two sons reached Italy
trust_devices: broker's own two sons had reached Italy; promise of crossing the Mediterranean by ship; promise of reaching Italy 'without any trouble'; belief that everyone is crossing and arriving
timeline: Left home 1 Sep 2025; boarded boat 14 Oct; boat ran out of fuel mid-sea and drifted a week; died 21 Oct; families told on 11 Nov, 21 days later
how_it_was_discovered: Families heard from fellow passengers that the two had died; when confronted, the broker admitted it. Before that he had said they were missing after being caught by Libyan police, and alive.
what_happened_abroad: About 50 people put on a small engine boat instead of a ship; fuel ran out in the middle of the Mediterranean; several, including the two, froze to death on the boat
victims_count: 2 named dead (Jafar Bepari, 40; Sirajul Hawlader, 35) among several deaths on a boat of about 50
harm: Two deaths; BDT 3,000,000 lost; debt; young children left behind
official_response: Madaripur Additional SP Jahangir Alam: legal action if the families file a written complaint; operation under way to catch the accused broker, who is in hiding
advice_or_warning_in_article: Additional SP Jahangir Alam: do not fall into brokers' hands; go abroad after government training
other_practical_details: The broker ring kept the deaths secret for three weeks and gave a false story (police detention) meanwhile. The vessel promised (ship) and the vessel used (small engine boat) differed.
key_quote_bn: টাকা নেওয়ার আগে তাঁদের জাহাজে ভূমধ্যসাগর পাড়ি দেওয়ার কথা বলা হয়েছিল। কিন্তু তাঁদের ছোট্ট একটি ইঞ্জিনচালিত নৌকায় ওঠানো হয়।

headline_en: They are Bangladeshis who went to Russia for jobs and are being made to fight
destination_promised: Russia; jobs in oil, construction or logistics
route_and_actual_destination: Direct to Russia on valid work visas, then sent to the Ukraine front. RMMRU: others are first taken to Saudi Arabia on tourist or Umrah visas, then made to sign a contract and sent to the battlefield.
promised_job_and_wage: High-paid work in oil, construction or logistics; wage not stated
visa_type_claimed: valid work visa (also tourist and Umrah visas per RMMRU)
perpetrator_type: local brokers, travel or recruiting agencies and international facilitators
perpetrator_names: Friendship and Co-operative Recruitment (travel agency through which Afzal Hossain Meraj went); 'MD Sohel', a Bangladeshi promoting Russian army service on Facebook
trust_devices: valid visa and legal departure; promise of high-paid civilian work; a real job for the first months (Meraj worked four months before being laid off); Facebook promotion of army benefits
timeline: Meraj went 10 Aug 2024, worked 4 months, laid off, then went to the war through a ring; father applied to the Foreign Ministry 22 Apr 2025; returned about Sep 2025; BRAC began receiving applications from late 2024
how_it_was_discovered: After arrival in Russia: passports confiscated and workers forced into the military; families learn from last messages and photos in Russian uniform
what_happened_abroad: Passports seized, forced to join the Russian military and sent to fight in Ukraine. Meraj was injured in a mine blast and spent 25 days in hospital. Ayon Mondal (Bagerhat) last messaged that he was being taken towards the Ukrainian border; Amit Barua (Cumilla) was photographed in Russian uniform; both missing. Mohammad Yasin Sheikh (22) was killed on 27 Mar 2025.
victims_count: 10 families have applied to BRAC; about a dozen families contacted the Moscow embassy (AFP, Apr 2025); true number unknown
harm: Forced combat, injury, disappearance, at least one death; BDT 7 to 8 lakh spent
official_response: Foreign Ministry (9 Feb 2025) asked the Moscow embassy for details, asked ministries to act against the recruiting and travel agencies involved, and asked airports to take special care with travellers holding Russian tourist visas; one member of a trafficking ring arrested. BRAC submitted rescue applications to the Foreign Ministry and case documents to CID. Meraj returned with help from the Bangladesh Embassy in Moscow.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Shariful Hasan (BRAC, migration and youth): government must find out how many were forced to fight, returned or died, and build awareness so no one is cheated or forced to fight. Tasneem Siddiqui (RMMRU): gave a report to the information adviser calling for awareness.
other_practical_details: Source is the BRAC report 'Promises Written in Blood: How Legal Migration Turned into Forced Recruitment in the Russia-Ukraine War', based on survivor accounts, family testimony and documents. A valid visa and legal exit did not protect these workers. Meraj's father alleged his son was 'sold' to the Russian army.
key_quote_bn: রাশিয়ায় পৌঁছানোর পর পাসপোর্ট বাজেয়াপ্ত করে সামরিক বাহিনীতে যোগ দিতে বাধ্য করা হয়।

perpetrator_type: official (some sports federations and associations, as alleged)
trust_devices: place in an official sports team; government order (GO) for the tour

official_response: National Sports Council letter of 9 Oct 2025: federations must send the GO proposal at least 10 days before the flight and submit proof of each selected player's fitness and performance
verification_mentioned: Previously federations sent only names for the GO and NSC did not check whether the person was really a player; NSC will now check selection evidence
advice_or_warning_in_article: Farhad Jesmin Liti (former athlete, chair of BOA Athletes Commission): hears that some federations take fake players; welcomes the rule as accountability. NSC director Aminul Ehsan: questions of trafficking in the name of sport do arise in places.

headline_en: Editorial: effective action needed to stop fraud ('free visa')
destination_promised: Middle East Arab countries; no specific job (so-called 'free visa')
route_and_actual_destination: Workers reach the destination country but 43% find no work (OKUP survey)
promised_job_and_wage: None: a 'free visa' gives only entry or a purchased sponsorship, with no specific job arranged
visa_type_claimed: 'free visa' (sold sponsorship)
amount_per_person: About five times the government-set cost (OKUP study); figure in taka not stated
how_money_was_raised: OKUP survey: 72% took loans, 11% mortgaged land, 6% sold family land
perpetrator_type: village brokers and dishonest recruiting agencies
trust_devices: the name 'free visa'
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival: no job
what_happened_abroad: Workers face uncertainty; 43% got no work

Calls for strict action against brokers and agencies, enforcement of the government-set migration cost, skills training, and grassroots awareness that a free visa is a trap.

headline_en: Driven to New York by climate disaster at home, and afraid of deportation there too
destination_promised: United States (New York), to seek asylum; no job promised
route_and_actual_destination: Left Bangladesh February 2023; 11 countries by air and land over 9 months; surrendered to border officials in Arizona; then New York (Kensington, Brooklyn)
visa_type_claimed: None; irregular crossing of the US-Mexico border followed by a political asylum application
amount_per_person: USD 41,000 for travel and broker costs (Hossain, from Feni)
how_money_was_raised: Sold his land and borrowed about USD 33,000 from relatives and friends
perpetrator_type: Broker (smuggler)
how_victim_met_them: Not stated for the broker. He heard that many people were getting asylum in the US; a friend suggested Brooklyn because of its large Bangladeshi community.
trust_devices: word that many people were being granted asylum in the US; a friend's advice about the Bangladeshi community in Brooklyn
timeline: Left February 2023; 9 months on the road; held 3 days at the border; asylum application filed April 2024; work permit seven months later; hearing still pending
how_it_was_discovered: After arrival: asylum turned out far harder than expected, and deportation raids began under the Trump administration
what_happened_abroad: Held for three days in a room with 15 people by Arizona border officials, then released. Worked as a restaurant kitchen helper, then bicycle food delivery, now full time at a Bengali sweet shop and cafe in Kensington, six or seven days a week, sharing a basement flat with two roommates. Lives in fear of ICE; keeps his asylum papers and hearing notices in a folder and his lawyer on speed dial.
victims_count: 1 Bangladeshi case (Hossain). CBP records analysed by CJI and Documented show about 100 Bangladesh-born people among those apprehended in 2024 from the disaster-hit areas studied.
victim_home_districts: Feni; Noakhali is the top origin district in the border records (over 30%)
harm: Land sold and about USD 33,000 of debt; separated from wife and daughter; uncertain asylum case and risk of deportation; says he would not have come had he known how hard it is
official_response: US: detained three days and released; asylum case pending in immigration court; ICE detained two Bangladeshis from Noakhali working in Buffalo, New York. No Bangladesh action mentioned.
verification_mentioned: The article states that the effect of climate-related flooding on income and livelihood is not an admissible ground for asylum; Hossain's application rests on his support for an opposition party.
advice_or_warning_in_article: The article reports that there is no specific US protection for people fleeing climate disasters. Hossain: if he had known it was this hard he would not have come. In a WhatsApp voice note shared by Bronx imam Sheikh Tidiane Ndao, a migrant back from immigration court warned that officials are giving people only two weeks to submit all documents.
other_practical_details: Border crossings from Bangladesh rose 150% from 2019 to 2024 in the CJI and Documented analysis; Feni is among the top 10 Bangladeshi origin towns. Translated investigation that also covers Guatemala and Senegal. The Senegal part describes a trick: smugglers posing as travel agents post TikTok and Instagram videos in the local language saying the journey is comfortable and work permits and jobs are easy, advertise visas and air tickets, and pass people to other smugglers on the route via Nicaragua. About 100,000 Bangladeshis are estimated to live in New York.

amount_per_person: BDT 1,500,000 from Naimul Haque; others not broken down

payment_method: Handed to the accused in person (Naimul); otherwise not stated
