headline_en: Living in misery abroad after broker ring's fraud; family in worry
route_and_actual_destination: Went to Saudi Arabia in May 2025; no job and no iqama arranged (family's account)
promised_job_and_wage: Driving a company vehicle, BDT 70,000 to 80,000 a month; company would arrange the driving licence
amount_per_person: BDT 500,000; a further BDT 150,000 demanded abroad for the driving licence
how_money_was_raised: Sold a motorcycle, mortgaged land and borrowed at interest
perpetrator_type: relative or neighbour
perpetrator_names: Khairul Islam (33) and Shariful Islam (28), neighbours, Bichhali village, Narail Sadar
how_victim_met_them: Neighbours in the same village
trust_devices: neighbours; promise of a good job with iqama; promise that the company would arrange the driving licence
timeline: Left May 2025; report late Sep 2025, about four months with no stable work
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival: no job was arranged and more money was demanded; iqama not done when the family could not pay
what_happened_abroad: No work, no iqama, was held and the family threatened from an unknown number; escaped; now hiding from police, short of food
harm: BDT 500,000 spent with mortgage and interest debt; undocumented and at risk of arrest in Saudi Arabia
ransom_details: Not a stated ransom sum: after the family could not pay the new demand, he was held and a caller from an unknown number said he would be in danger unless money was paid
official_response: Mother Parvin Begum filed a case in Narail court (date printed as 22 October); court ordered PBI Jashore to investigate; SI Mohidul Islam says investigation is ongoing. A village arbitration (salish) failed.
other_practical_details: Accused Shariful denies it: says Shimul was given the driving job but could not drive, was placed in another company, ran away and now works with Shariful's cousin, and that the iqama was done. Typical trick: a new charge appears after arrival (licence fee) and the iqama is withheld until it is paid.
key_quote_bn: ওরা বলছিল, কোম্পানির পক্ষ থেকে লাইসেন্স করে দেবে। পরে লাইসেন্স করতে আরও দেড় লাখ টাকা চাইছে।

headline_en: Crores taken with the lure of jobs abroad; ringleader arrested
route_and_actual_destination: Victims were handed forged visas (article does not say anyone travelled)
promised_job_and_wage: 'Attractive' job with a large salary; figures not stated
visa_type_claimed: Italy visa (forged)
amount_total: Several crore taka from at least 100 people (the article's opening line says 'hundreds of crores', including money taken for promised government posts)
payment_method: bank (several bank accounts)
perpetrator_type: fraud ring with local collectors in several districts
perpetrator_names: Josna Khatun (35), ringleader, from Daljitpur village, Narail, husband Mehedi Hasan, arrested in Ibrahimpur, Kafrul, Dhaka; Milon Mia of Faridpur (collected people from various areas)
how_victim_met_them: Local ring members collected people from different areas
trust_devices: visa document (forged); payment through bank accounts; promise of high salary
victims_count: At least 100
victim_home_districts: Ring's network: Faridpur, Narail, Narsingdi, Kishoreganj, Chandpur, Chattogram and other districts
harm: Money lost; passports of many victims held back to harass them
official_response: CID Dhaka Metro East arrested Josna Khatun on 23 Sep 2025; she is the named main accused in a fraud case at Paltan police station; Milon Mia arrested earlier and sent to court
other_practical_details: The same ring also took money promising important government posts. Holding the victim's passport was used as leverage.
key_quote_bn: পরে কয়েক ব্যাংক অ্যাকাউন্টের মাধ্যমে ভুক্তভোগীদের কাছ থেকে মোটা অঙ্কের টাকা নিয়ে দেওয়া হতো ভুয়া ভিসা।

headline_en: No UAE authority has imposed a visa ban on Bangladeshis: Bangladesh embassy
visa_type_claimed: UAE visas sold online (type not stated)
perpetrator_type: online contact (so-called visa processing centre website)
perpetrator_names: uaevisaonline.com
how_victim_met_them: Website
trust_devices: website presenting itself as a visa processing centre; Dubai head-office address printed on the site; article on the site about a UAE visa ban that Bangladeshi media repeated
how_it_was_discovered: Bangladesh Embassy in Abu Dhabi reviewed the site: registrant and technical contacts are in the UK, registrar contact in the US, company phone number in India, and the Dubai head-office building/house number does not exist
victims_count: Not stated; embassy says most customer reviews complain of being cheated financially
harm: Financial loss reported by customers (amounts not stated)
official_response: Embassy press release (22 Sep 2025): UAE authorities confirmed no authority announced a visa ban on Bangladeshis; the website's information is false
verification_mentioned: Embassy checked the website's registration details and physical address and customer reviews
advice_or_warning_in_article: Bangladesh Embassy, Abu Dhabi: do not be misled by baseless news; be more responsible when publishing or sharing such information
other_practical_details: A check anyone can copy: compare a visa site's domain registration country, phone number country and claimed office address; here all four pointed to different countries and the address did not exist.
key_quote_bn: দূতাবাস নিশ্চিত করেছে যে ঠিকানাটিতে ব্যবহার করা বিল্ডিং/ বাসা নং–এর কোনো অস্তিত্ব নেই।

headline_en: The dream of going abroad versus harsh reality (first-person account from Riyadh)
destination_promised: Saudi Arabia; job in a 'good chocolate company' (chocolate factory)
route_and_actual_destination: Dhaka (Shahjalal airport) to King Khaled airport, Riyadh; taken by a driver to a company room in Malaz, Riyadh. Visa turned out to be for a manpower supply company, not a chocolate factory.
promised_job_and_wage: Chocolate factory job; wage not stated
visa_type_claimed: work visa (actually a supply-company visa)
amount_per_person: BDT 400,000 for the visa, plus extra sums taken on various pretexts at the agency office on departure day
payment_method: instalments to the agency (sometimes BDT 50,000, sometimes BDT 100,000)
how_money_was_raised: BDT 400,000 borrowed from relatives
perpetrator_type: Bangladeshi already abroad (from the neighbouring village) plus a chain of brokers and a Dhaka agency
perpetrator_names: 'Abdullah' (pseudonym), from the neighbouring village, about five years in Saudi Arabia, living in 'Al Bisa' near the Yemen border; Dhaka agency not named
how_victim_met_them: Man from the neighbouring village, known locally as polite; friendship built over phone calls
trust_devices: known man from the next village with a good reputation; repeated phone reassurance; when the guardian asked directly whether it was really a chocolate factory, he said 'trust me, nothing to worry about'; a Dhaka agency handled the papers
timeline: No work for two months after arrival; later moved himself to another company where he has worked about four years
how_it_was_discovered: After arrival in Riyadh: a month passed with no work while buying his own food, then learned the visa and the villa belonged to a supply company
what_happened_abroad: Kept in a company room with no job for two months; 'Abdullah' kept saying today or tomorrow; spoke to five of the brokers; finally found a transfer to another company through his own contacts
victims_count: 1 (writer); says he saw countless others worse off, some sleeping on the street
harm: BDT 400,000 debt, two months without work or income, mistreatment and extra charges at the agency office
verification_mentioned: None available to him: he says there was no way to know in Bangladesh that the visa had passed through six brokers
advice_or_warning_in_article: Writer's warning: fraudsters have spread a net in the Saudi labour market; brokers bring workers through agencies on false promises and cannot give work, so workers must hunt for jobs themselves
other_practical_details: The visa passed through six brokers, each taking a cut. Supply companies (as described by the writer) hire workers out elsewhere at a high price, and wages often go unpaid. Agency staff in Dhaka behaved badly and extracted more money on the day papers were handed over, just before the flight.
key_quote_bn: বিদেশে পাড়ি জমানোর পর বুঝেছি ভিসা ছয়জন দালালের হাতবদল হয়ে আমার হাত পর্যন্ত পৌঁছেছিল।

headline_en: CID files money laundering case against Malaysia syndicate
route_and_actual_destination: Workers were sent to Malaysia
visa_type_claimed: work visa
amount_per_person: BDT 150,000 taken per worker by FiveM International, of which BDT 107,510 was laundered (case statement)
amount_total: More than BDT 100 crore laundered from 9,372 workers (may change during investigation)
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agencies owned by former MPs and a former minister's family (syndicate)
perpetrator_names: FiveM International (Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, former MP Feni-3; wife Jesmin Masud; daughter Tasnia Masud); Ahmed International (Benzir Ahmed, MP Dhaka-20); Snigdha Overseas Limited (Nizam Uddin Hazari, former MP Feni-2); Orbitals Enterprise (Kashmeri Kamal, wife of former finance minister A H M Mustafa Kamal); Catharsis International (Ruhul Amin alias Swapan, former BAIRA secretary general). 33 accused in total.
timeline: Syndicate sending began 2022; market closed 31 May 2024; about 500,000 workers went in that period; case filed 28 Aug 2025
how_it_was_discovered: CID money-laundering inquiry and victim testimony; Prothom Alo reports of 30 and 31 May and 17 Sep 2024
victims_count: 9,372 workers sent through FiveM International named in this case
harm: Workers paid money obtained by fraud; over BDT 100 crore moved abroad
official_response: CID Sub-Inspector Md Moniruzzaman filed a case at Banani police station under the Money Laundering Prevention Act against 33 people on 28 Aug 2025; CID to investigate
other_practical_details: The Malaysia market has been run by a syndicate of selected agencies several times in the past decade and a half; the latest round ran 2022 to 31 May 2024.
key_quote_bn: কর্মীপ্রতি ফাইভএম দেড় লাখ টাকা নিয়েছেন। এর মধ্যে এক লাখ ৭ হাজার ৫১০ টাকা পাচার হয়েছে।

headline_en: Dipu held in a broker ring's den in Libya; the torture stops when money is paid
route_and_actual_destination: To Libya, then by sea to Italy was the plan. Reached Libya 23 Sep 2023; never reached Italy; still held in Libya after 1 year 10 months. Second boat attempt got near Albania before he was seized by another group.
amount_per_person: BDT 950,000 contract price; about BDT 4,500,000 paid in total so far
amount_total: About BDT 4,500,000 (family's claim); a further BDT 2,500,000 demanded
how_money_was_raised: Sold homestead land; brother-in-law (Saudi returnee) also contributed
perpetrator_type: village broker (neighbour, now abroad) and Libyan mafia groups
perpetrator_names: Fazlul Haque (Fazlu), son of Mofiz Kazi, Manikdi Purbakanda village, Bhairab, Kishoreganj; has a two-storey house near the victim's home
how_victim_met_them: Same village, house next door; broker had been sending people abroad for seven years
trust_devices: broker is a neighbour; seven years in the business; earlier people from the area reached their destination through him
timeline: Reached Libya 23 Sep 2023; a few days later detained by law enforcers, then passed to a mafia group; ransom call after 1.5 months; 4 months under the broker; first boat turned back; 4 more months; second boat, seized near Albania; then 8 months under the broker with no demands; 15 Jul 2025 broker asked BDT 850,000, family refused; 16 Jul a group took Dipu from the house; torture videos from 24 Jul 2025
how_it_was_discovered: Phone call to the family about 1.5 months after arrival in Libya showing torture video and demanding BDT 1,100,000 within one day
what_happened_abroad: Detained, sold between groups, tortured every few days with a cloth tied over his face while the family watches on video call; two failed sea crossings
harm: About BDT 4,500,000 lost, homestead sold, repeated torture, still captive at time of report
ransom_details: BDT 1,100,000 to mafia group (demanded within one day, paid); BDT 1,000,000 to broker for first crossing; BDT 900,000 for second crossing; BDT 500,000 for release after capture near Albania; BDT 850,000 demanded 15 Jul 2025 (refused); now BDT 2,500,000 demanded. How paid is not stated.
official_response: Brought to the notice of Bhairab UNO Shabnam Sharmin, who said she would think about what can be done; no case or arrest reported
other_practical_details: Pattern: each payment leads to a new demand; the victim is released by one group only to return to the broker's control, who then charges again for the next crossing. Broker's sister says he is abroad and 'trying to free Dipu'. Related headline in the article: 63% of Bangladeshis going to Europe via Libya are taken captive.
key_quote_bn: ভিডিও কলে নির্যাতনের দৃশ্য দেখানো হয় পরিবারকে। টাকা দিলে থামে নির্যাতন।

headline_en: BSB Global Network's Khairul Bashar remanded for another 13 days
destination_promised: Foreign universities (countries not stated); higher study
route_and_actual_destination: Many students were never applied for at any foreign university; some went abroad and were cheated there in various ways (details not given)
visa_type_claimed: student visa (university admission, scholarship and visa processing)
amount_total: Not stated ('huge amount')
payment_method: Money was deposited in various bank accounts of Bashar and family
perpetrator_type: study-abroad consultancy (licence status not stated)
perpetrator_names: BSB Global Network; chairman Khairul Bashar; wife Khandaker Selima Rowshan; son Arsh Ibne Bashar
how_victim_met_them: Attracted through flashy advertisements
trust_devices: fake visa processing; invented claims of representing institutions; flashy advertisements; promise of admission and scholarships
timeline: Ring operated 2018 to 2024 (CID preliminary inquiry)
how_it_was_discovered: CID inquiry found that for many students no application had been made to any foreign university
what_happened_abroad: Some who did go abroad were cheated in various ways (not detailed)
victims_count: 448 victims have come forward so far; CID thinks the real number is higher
harm: Money lost (amount not stated)
official_response: CID filed a Money Laundering Prevention Act case at Gulshan police station on 4 May 2025; Bashar arrested in Dhanmondi on 14 July, 10-day remand from 15 July; on 13 Aug 2025 Dhaka CMM court granted 13 more days of remand in 5 separate fraud cases (police had asked for 31). Several victims have filed fraud and forgery cases at various police stations.
other_practical_details: CID says the family withdrew students' money from the bank accounts to buy immovable property, run businesses and move money illegally.
key_quote_bn: তবে অনুসন্ধানে জানা যায়, শিক্ষার্থীদের অনেকের নামে বিদেশি কোনো বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ে আবেদনই করা হয়নি।

headline_en: Editorial: the opportunity must be used, even if late (Malaysia to take workers who missed the May 2024 deadline)
payment_method: cash (ring collects passports and cash)
perpetrator_type: organised ring (not named)
trust_devices: promise of jobs in Sabah province, Malaysia
how_it_was_discovered: Bangladesh High Commission in Malaysia said it found evidence of the ring's fraud and issued a warning
harm: Passports and cash handed over to the ring; amounts not stated
official_response: Bangladesh High Commission in Malaysia issued a public warning
verification_mentioned: High Commission: there is currently no agreement or MoU between Bangladesh and Malaysia for sending workers to Sabah, so any Sabah offer is not through an agreed channel
advice_or_warning_in_article: Bangladesh High Commission in Malaysia: do not fall for rings collecting passports and cash for Sabah. Editorial: government must stay alert so no new Malaysia syndicate forms
other_practical_details: Separate case in the same editorial: 16,970 workers who had final clearance could not go to Malaysia by 31 May 2024 (some could not get air tickets, some did not get the employer's final consent); many had paid agencies lakhs of taka. Malaysia has now approved taking workers from this group through the state agency BOESL, in construction and tourism. Tourism: demand letter attestation information must be submitted on Malaysia's FWCMS online portal per a checklist; construction: applications go through Construction Labour Exchange Centre Berhad (CLAB) into FWCMS. Editorial also says some workers who reach Malaysia do not get the promised job and live in inhumane conditions, and that a large syndicate involving ministers and MPs formed under the previous government.
key_quote_bn: মালয়েশিয়ার সাবাহ প্রদেশে কর্মী পাঠানোর কথা বলে বাংলাদেশিদের কাছ থেকে পাসপোর্ট ও নগদ টাকা সংগ্রহ করছে এই চক্র।

headline_en: BSB Global Network's Khairul Bashar on three days' remand again
destination_promised: Abroad for higher study (countries not named in this article)
route_and_actual_destination: Many never had any application made to a foreign university; some did go abroad and were cheated in various ways there (CID)
visa_type_claimed: Student visa (admission, scholarship and visa processing)
amount_total: BDT 1 crore 18 lakh in this fraud case; the separate CID money-laundering case concerns students' money taken 2018-2024
perpetrator_type: student visa consultancy (study-abroad agency)
perpetrator_names: BSB Global Network; chairman Khairul Bashar; his wife Khandaker Selima Rowshan and son Arsh Ibne Bashar (named by CID as running the ring with him)
how_victim_met_them: Attracted through flashy advertisements
trust_devices: fake visa processing; made-up claims of representing foreign universities; flashy advertisements; offers of admission and scholarships
timeline: Ring operated 2018-2024 (CID). Arrested 14 July 2025; 10 days' remand from 15 July; 3 more days granted Wednesday 6 August 2025.
how_it_was_discovered: CID inquiry found that for many students no application had been made to any foreign university at all
what_happened_abroad: Some students who did go abroad were cheated in various ways (no detail given)
victims_count: 448 have reported to CID so far; real number thought to be higher
harm: Large sums lost; no admission or visa
official_response: Dhaka CMM court granted Gulshan police 3 days' remand (10 sought) in another fraud case; earlier 10 days' remand for CID in the money-laundering case filed 4 May 2025 at Gulshan police station.
verification_mentioned: CID's finding implies a check: many students had no application lodged with any university in their name.
other_practical_details: CID says the family kept students' money in various bank accounts, withdrew it to buy immovable property and run businesses, and transferred money illegally.
key_quote_bn: শিক্ষার্থীদের অনেকের নামে বিদেশি কোনো বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ে আবেদনই করা হয়নি।

headline_en: Malaysia decides to recruit the workers who could not go
route_and_actual_destination: Did not travel: 16,970 workers who had final clearance could not enter Malaysia by 31 May 2024
promised_job_and_wage: Now to be hired in construction or tourism (wage not stated)
timeline: Missed the 31 May 2024 deadline; Malaysian approval announced 1 August 2025
how_it_was_discovered: Some could not get air tickets; others never received the employer's final consent or the employer's confirmation that they would be received at the airport
harm: Could not travel despite completing all steps and holding final clearance
official_response: Bangladesh High Commission in Kuala Lumpur (revised notice, 1 August 2025): Malaysian authorities have approved employing, from among those who could not come by 31 May 2024, workers through BOESL (Bangladesh Overseas Employment and Services Limited, the state-owned recruiter) in construction or tourism.
other_practical_details: Procedure in the notice: for tourism workers, employers submit demand-letter attestation information per the attached checklist on Malaysia's FWCMS (Foreign Workers Centralized Management System) online portal; for construction workers, applications go through Construction Labour Exchange Centre Berhad (CLAB) into FWCMS; originals and one photocopy set of everything submitted go to the Bangladesh High Commission. Recruitment is through BOESL, not private agencies.
key_quote_bn: উল্লেখ্য, গত বছর মালয়েশিয়ায় যেতে সব প্রক্রিয়া শেষে চূড়ান্ত ছাড়পত্র নিয়েও যেতে পারেননি ১৬ হাজার ৯৭০ কর্মী।

headline_en: Bangladesh High Commission warns of fraud in worker recruitment for Malaysia
payment_method: Cash (the ring is collecting passports and cash)
perpetrator_type: organised fraud ring (not named)
trust_devices: false publicity that Sabah is recruiting Bangladeshi workers; collecting passports along with cash
timeline: Warning issued Friday 1 August 2025
how_it_was_discovered: Came to the notice of the Bangladesh High Commission in Kuala Lumpur, which says it found evidence of widespread fraud
harm: Passports and cash taken for a recruitment channel that does not exist
official_response: Bangladesh High Commission, Kuala Lumpur, published a warning notice on its Facebook page; says talks with the relevant authorities are continuing.
verification_mentioned: High Commission: there is currently no agreement or MoU between Bangladesh and Malaysia for sending workers to Sabah, and Sabah authorities have taken no decision to recruit Bangladeshis; if permission is given it will be announced on the High Commission's website.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Bangladesh High Commission, Kuala Lumpur: until an agreement or MoU on Sabah is signed, do not be misled by these rings' false publicity and do not enter into any transaction with them.
other_practical_details: Check the Bangladesh High Commission Kuala Lumpur website for any Sabah recruitment announcement before paying anyone.
key_quote_bn: বাংলাদেশ থেকে মালয়েশিয়ার সাবাহ প্রদেশে কর্মী নেওয়ার জন্য বর্তমানে মালয়েশিয়ার সরকারের সঙ্গে বাংলাদেশ সরকারের কোনো চুক্তি বা সমঝোতা নেই।

headline_en: Trying to go abroad to study, they fell into BSB Global Network's trap
route_and_actual_destination: Never left Bangladesh (those quoted)
visa_type_claimed: Student visa
amount_per_person: BDT 17 lakh each (lawyer couple Zahidul Haque Khan and Rownak Jahan); BDT 13 lakh (Amir Hossain); BDT 16 lakh (Jannatul Ferdous)
amount_total: BDT 18,29,57,680 (about 18.3 crore) from 141 students in CID's money-laundering case; BDT 1.8 crore in a separate case by 23 people
how_money_was_raised: Sold land (Amir Hossain)
perpetrator_type: student visa consultancy (study-abroad agency)
perpetrator_names: BSB Global Network; chairman Khairul Bashar; his wife Khandaker Selima Rowshan and son Arsh Ibne Bashar (named by CID as running the ring with him); general manager Abu Zahid
how_victim_met_them: Victims contacted the firm; CID says it drew students in with flashy advertisements
trust_devices: flashy advertisements; offers of foreign university admission, scholarships and visa processing; promise of a visa within three months; established firm that had sent some students abroad
timeline: CID: ring operated 2018-2024. Cases filed from October 2024 to 30 June 2025. Amir Hossain was told the visa would come within three months. Bashar arrested 14 July 2025.
how_it_was_discovered: The visa never came; when victims asked for the money back the firm did not return it
victims_count: 448 victims have reported to CID (real number may be higher); 141 in the money-laundering case; cases by at least 100 individuals
victim_home_districts: Shariatpur (Amir Hossain, living in Dhaka); others not stated
harm: BDT 13-17 lakh lost per person; land sold; no visa and no refund
official_response: CID arrested Khairul Bashar in Dhanmondi on 14 July 2025 in a money-laundering case CID filed at Gulshan police station on 4 May 2025. Fraud case filed at Gulshan on 5 May on behalf of 18 people; another by 23 people on 28 December 2024; one by Jannatul Ferdous in September 2024. Arrest warrants in many cases and a travel ban. GM Abu Zahid was arrested 11 December 2024 and got bail 23 February 2025. Gulshan OC: nine cases at his station.
money_recovered: None for those quoted; the GM's lawyer says the firm will refund those who could not go abroad
other_practical_details: Even two practising lawyers were cheated. The firm's defence is that it has a good reputation and has sent many students abroad.
key_quote_bn: আমাকে বলা হয়েছিল তিন মাসের মধ্যে ভিসা হবে, আমি কানাডায় উচ্চশিক্ষার জন্য যেতে পারব; কিন্তু বিএসবি গ্লোবাল নেটওয়ার্ক আমার ভিসার ব্যবস্থা করতে পারেনি।

headline_en: How did you cheat so many students: court to Khairul Bashar
destination_promised: Canada, Australia and other countries, for higher study
route_and_actual_destination: Not sent abroad
visa_type_claimed: Student visa (higher study)
amount_per_person: BDT 10 lakh (student Naim Howlader); BDT 17 lakh (a lawyer who spoke in court)
amount_total: BDT 18 crore from 141 students (CID case). The complainants' lawyer told the court at least BDT 4,000 crore from 1,000 students; the prosecutor said several thousand crore from several hundred students (figures as stated in court).
how_money_was_raised: Father borrowed on interest, still being repaid (Naim Howlader)
perpetrator_type: student visa consultancy (study-abroad agency)
perpetrator_names: BSB Global Network; chairman Khairul Bashar (home district Brahmanbaria)
trust_devices: refund cheques that the bank repeatedly dishonoured; photos of Bashar with former prime minister Sheikh Hasina and her ministers (shown to the court by the complainants' lawyer)
timeline: Students had been asking for refunds for three to four years (complainants' lawyer). Arrested 14 July 2025; produced in court 15 July 2025.
victims_count: 448 have reported to CID; over 200 victims gathered at the court; 70-80 have filed cases in that court alone
harm: Money lost with no visa and no refund; families in debt; victims who went to the office for refunds were beaten by Bashar's men (complainants' lawyer, with photos)
official_response: Dhaka CMM court (Additional CMM Sanaullah) granted CID 10 days' remand in the money-laundering case. Bashar told the court he was 'a victim of circumstances' and that he knew of 70 cases against him. Victims threw eggs at him in the court building.
money_recovered: None; refund cheques bounced
other_practical_details: A refund cheque is not a refund: the cheques given here were repeatedly dishonoured. The lawyer alleged a 'Bashar bahini' that beat people who came to the office to ask for money.
key_quote_bn: টাকা ফেরত দেওয়ার নাম করে যেসব চেক তিনি দিয়েছিলেন, সেগুলো ব্যাংক থেকে বারবারই প্রত্যাখাত হয়েছে।

headline_en: Rohingya couple come to get passports in Faridpur; son-in-law and 2 brokers also detained
amount_total: BDT 30,000 taken from the couple for arranging passports
perpetrator_type: passport office brokers
perpetrator_names: Siam Ahmed (27), Kamalapur area, and Rashed Khan (30), Bottola area, Faridpur town; Faridpur Regional Passport Office
timeline: Money paid and incident on the same day, Sunday 13 July 2025, about 3pm
how_it_was_discovered: After taking the money the brokers started no passport work and began threatening them; when the son-in-law protested they beat him and he went into the passport office to ask Ansar guards for help
victims_count: 3 (Rohingya couple and their son-in-law)
victim_home_districts: Cox's Bazar (Marigola village, Sadar upazila, as stated)
harm: BDT 30,000 lost; son-in-law beaten; the three Rohingya themselves detained
official_response: Police detained the three Rohingya and the two brokers. Kotwali OC Md Asaduzzaman: the Rohingya are being questioned and will be sent back to their camp or their residence; legal action is being taken against the brokers.
other_practical_details: About passport brokers, not a migration case; the article does not say why the passports were wanted or that they were going abroad for work. Detained: Abdus Sobahan (75), wife Hasina Begum (45), son-in-law Md Toyob (30).
key_quote_bn: দালালদের মাধ্যমে পাসপোর্ট করতে এসে প্রতারণার শিকার হয়েছেন।

headline_en: What preparation do workers going abroad need
perpetrator_type: brokers (general pattern, no specific case)
verification_mentioned: Article (citing BMET's website): the list of legal recruiting agencies and of technical training centres is on bmet.gov.bd; the nearest District Employment and Manpower Office gives information on approved agencies; check whether the destination country is officially approved to take Bangladeshi workers; verify the visa, passport and employment contract; BMET emigration clearance (smart card) confirms legality.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Prothom Alo personal-finance article: start the process only through a government-approved recruiting agency; pay through a bank and keep receipts; tell the family everything; read salary, job type, housing and medical terms in the contract before signing; do not accept any tempting offer without checking. Brokers typically press you to act fast, do not show proper papers and hide their identity. Leaving by sea or any route other than the three international airports (Dhaka, Chattogram, Sylhet) is a punishable offence.
other_practical_details: General advice piece with no specific case. Probashi Kallyan Bank migration loan: no collateral, up to BDT 3 lakh for new and re-entry visas, terms 3 and 2 years, 9% simple interest, two-month grace then monthly instalments; needs photo, voter ID, address, certificate, passport, visa and smart card copies, one guarantor's papers and three bank cheques, and an account at the bank. 'Ami Probashi' app has a free chat-based CV builder in Bangla and English. Documents listed for legal travel: valid passport, employment visa, air ticket, appointment letter or contract, medical certificate where applicable, BMET clearance or smart card. Probashi Kallyan desk at the airport for help on departure.
key_quote_bn: দালালেরা সাধারণত দ্রুত কাজ করিয়ে দেবে বলে চাপ দেয়, সঠিক কাগজপত্র দেখায় না ও নিজের পরিচয় গোপন রাখে।

headline_en: ACC case against 4 BMET officials and owners and officers of 5 agencies
destination_promised: Middle East including Saudi Arabia, as domestic workers (women)
promised_job_and_wage: Domestic worker (wage not stated)
perpetrator_type: officials and licensed recruiting agencies acting together
perpetrator_names: BMET: deputy director (emigration) Md Sajjad Hossain Sarkar; assistant director (emigration) Md Hossain Ullah Akanda; manpower survey officer Md Nizamuddin Patwari; office assistant and computer operator Md Azad Hossain. Agencies: H A International (managing partner Md Anwar Hossain); K H Overseas (managing partner Md Salauddin); Makka Overseas (proprietor Md Jamal Hossain); Tasnim Overseas (managing partner Md Anwar Hossain Bhuiyan); S M Manpower (partner Ekramul Haque). No licence numbers printed.
trust_devices: BMET emigration clearance issued on applications carrying another woman's passport number
timeline: ACC raid on the BMET office 29 May 2025; case filed Thursday 3 July 2025
how_it_was_discovered: ACC raid on the BMET office in Dhaka and checking of preserved records
victims_count: Four under-age women (below 25) found to have been given clearance; total number not stated
harm: Women sent abroad as domestic workers on false passport details; under-age women cleared in breach of the ministry circular
official_response: Anti-Corruption Commission assistant director Swapan Kumar Roy filed the case against the nine; ACC says further investigation is under way.
verification_mentioned: ACC: applications were approved without checking the passport number against the BMET database.
other_practical_details: Method: agencies submitted applications using another woman's passport number in place of the real applicant's, and BMET officials approved clearance without verifying, allegedly for financial gain. A ministry circular sets 25 as the minimum age for women going to the Middle East as domestic workers.
key_quote_bn: প্রকৃত আবেদনকারীর পরিবর্তে অন্য নারীর পাসপোর্ট নম্বর দিয়ে আবেদন জমা দিয়ে তা বিএমইটির ডেটাবেজে যাচাই না করে ছাড়পত্রের অনুমোদন দেওয়া হয়।

headline_en: The dream of going to Canada became Afaz Uddin's undoing
destination_promised: Canada (to be taken there from Kuwait)
route_and_actual_destination: Never left Kuwait
promised_job_and_wage: Salary of BDT 4-5 lakh in Canada (job not specified)
visa_type_claimed: Canada visa (type not stated)
amount_per_person: BDT 24 lakh
amount_total: BDT 24 lakh
payment_method: Mobile banking: sent to several bKash numbers supplied by the fraudster, August to December 2024
how_money_was_raised: All his savings from 30 years in Kuwait plus loans from acquaintances and relatives, on which interest is being paid
perpetrator_type: online contact
perpetrator_names: A man calling himself Asadul Islam, who claimed to be in Canada; 20-25 unnamed associates accused in the case. When Prothom Alo called the number on 4 June, the man answering said his name was Hanif, not Asadul.
how_victim_met_them: Facebook advertisement 'opportunity to go to Canada at low cost'; he called the mobile number in the ad in the first week of August 2024
trust_devices: Facebook advertisement; claim to be living in Canada; repeated assurance that the visa would come very soon
timeline: First contact first week of August 2024; payments through December 2024; phone later switched off; case filed 22 May 2025
how_it_was_discovered: After the money was sent he was repeatedly told the visa was coming; then the fraudster's phone number was found switched off
victims_count: 1 (Afaz Uddin Molla, 58, a worker in Kuwait for 30 years)
harm: BDT 24 lakh lost; family nearly destitute and paying interest on loans
official_response: His wife Roksana Akter filed a case at Jatrabari police station, Dhaka, on 22 May 2025 naming Asadul and 20-25 unidentified associates; the court ordered CID to investigate.
money_recovered: None reported
verification_mentioned: The wife asked many times to talk to Asadul on a video call; he never agreed. Public prosecutor says CID should identify each member through the bKash numbers in the case.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Dhaka Metropolitan Sessions Judge Court chief public prosecutor Omar Faruq Faruqi: no one should put money in on the strength of flashy social media advertisements; go abroad through licensed institutions that regularly send people, which leaves less chance of being cheated.
other_practical_details: Victim was already a migrant worker abroad, targeted for onward migration. Refusal of a video call and payment only to personal bKash numbers were the warning signs in this case.
key_quote_bn: বহুবার তিনি আসাদুলের সঙ্গে ভিডিও কলে কথা বলতে চেয়েছিলেন; কিন্তু আসাদুল রাজি হননি।

headline_en: Bangladesh-Malaysia corridor: how can the problems in sending workers be solved?
route_and_actual_destination: Over four lakh workers went to Malaysia in 2022-2024; about 17,000 with visas and tickets could not enter before the 30 May 2024 deadline
promised_job_and_wage: Promised jobs in Malaysia that many did not get
visa_type_claimed: Calling visa
amount_per_person: About BDT 5 lakh charged per migrant; an extra BDT 1.5 lakh per worker allegedly charged for processing through the syndicate
how_money_was_raised: Loans (workers left heavily indebted)
perpetrator_type: syndicate of selected licensed recruiting agencies
trust_devices: valid calling visa; air ticket; selected agencies approved under the government-to-government MoU
timeline: MoU signed 2021; recruitment 2022-2024; entry deadline for calling visas 30 May 2024; market closed for about a year; Malaysian letter dated 23 April 2025; adviser's visit 13 May 2025.
what_happened_abroad: Some companies could not provide work; many workers without jobs went hungry or half-fed; rights groups documented abuse and debt bondage
victims_count: About 17,000 could not travel despite visa and ticket (Malaysia's figure about 11,000; adviser said Malaysia would initially take about 8,000); over 4 lakh went in 2022-2024
harm: High migration cost and debt; no job on arrival; those who paid all or most of the cost but could not travel left in debt
official_response: Bangladesh police and the Anti-Corruption Commission opened investigations; complaints filed against the syndicate under the human trafficking law; in October (2024) police asked Malaysia to arrest and return two migration businessmen accused of trafficking, money laundering and embezzlement; ACC is investigating some agency owners and former MPs. Malaysia's human resources ministry secretary-general asked Bangladesh in a 23 April letter to review and withdraw 'unsubstantiated allegations' to improve Malaysia's US TIP rating. UN human rights office criticised the situation.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Columnist Dr Mohammad Rashed Alam Bhuiyan (Dhaka University; RMMRU researcher): do not bring back a system that allows a syndicate; open sending to all agencies as Malaysia does for other source countries; domestic cases must proceed even if allegations are withdrawn under pressure; resolve the cases of those who could not go.
other_practical_details: Agencies reportedly paid large sums to be enlisted. The syndicate is said to have doubled migration cost over ten years. The US has said in at least 8 of the last 10 years that Malaysia fails minimum anti-trafficking standards.
key_quote_bn: সে সময় অভিযোগ ওঠে যে শ্রমিকেরা হাজার হাজার ডলার পরিশোধ করেও মালয়েশিয়াতে প্রতিশ্রুত চাকরি পাননি

headline_en: Accused of fraud with fake visas and air tickets; one detained by RAB
destination_promised: Turkey (work); later changed to Saudi Arabia
route_and_actual_destination: Never left Bangladesh
amount_per_person: BDT 610,000 (Abdul Gani)
amount_total: About BDT 1 crore taken over a few years, according to local residents
payment_method: Handed to the broker in person, along with the passport
how_money_was_raised: Sold everything he owned and borrowed at high interest (dadon)
perpetrator_type: village broker
perpetrator_names: Shafiqul Islam (42), Patira village, Kaladaha union, Fulbaria upazila, Mymensingh; known locally as a manpower broker ('adam byabshayi')
how_victim_met_them: Known in his own area as a manpower broker
trust_devices: fake visa; fake air ticket in the name of 'Jazeera Airways'; promise to send to Saudi Arabia within 20 days when Turkey fell through; promise of a refund
timeline: Kept waiting 1.5 years for Turkey; then told Saudi Arabia within 20 days; fake ticket and visa given 18 February 2025; broker fled the area from 10 April; detained by RAB on 29 May 2025. RAB says he had been doing this for about three years.
how_it_was_discovered: After the ticket and visa were handed over it was found that both were fake (the article does not say where or how)
victims_count: Two complainants named; they say many people in surrounding areas were cheated
victim_home_districts: Mymensingh (Fulbaria: Shushuti village; Pahar Anantapur village, Rangamatia union)
harm: BDT 610,000 lost by one complainant; debt to moneylenders; threats when asking for money back
official_response: RAB-14 detained Shafiqul at Joydebpur Technopara, Gazipur, at about 1:45am and handed him to Fulbaria police station. RAB-14 commander Naymul Hasan said a case would be filed under regular law; Fulbaria OC said the complaint would be verified before legal action.
money_recovered: None; refund was promised but he fled
other_practical_details: RAB says he made fake tickets in the names of 'Jazeera Airways', 'Air Arabia', 'Salam Air', 'Egypt Air' and others. Complainants: Abdul Gani (30) and Nazmul Haque; the article attributes the second complainant's statement to 'Abdul Gani' as well, apparently a misprint. Pattern: destination switched after a long delay, then forged travel documents produced to keep the victim waiting.
key_quote_bn: গত ১৮ ফেব্রুয়ারি ‘জাজিরা এয়ারওয়েজ’ নামের একটি প্রতিষ্ঠানের ভুয়া বিমানের টিকিট ও ভিসা দেওয়া হয়েছিল। পরে জানা যায়, টিকিট ও ভিসা দুটোই নকল।

headline_en: Three arrested including two Chinese nationals on human trafficking charges
destination_promised: China, as the wife of a Chinese national
route_and_actual_destination: Bashundhara Residential Area, Dhaka -> Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport; stopped before departure
perpetrator_type: foreign nationals with local brokers
perpetrator_names: Chinese nationals Hu Jun Jun (30) and Zhang Leiji (54) [হু জুন জুন, ঝাং লেইজি]; Bangladeshi Md Nayan Ali (30); a house in Bashundhara Residential Area, Dhaka
how_victim_met_them: Through Nayan Ali, a local associate of the two Chinese men, who had built ties with brokers around the country
trust_devices: formal marriage in March with a BDT 10 lakh denmohor; passport and other papers made in her name at a false address; air ticket bought in her name
timeline: The Chinese men came to Bangladesh about a year earlier; marriage in March 2025; trafficking attempt Monday night (26 May 2025)
how_it_was_discovered: At the roundabout by the airport's main entrance the 19-year-old told Airport Armed Police Battalion officers that the two men were trying to traffic her to China
victims_count: One 19-year-old woman; police say other women victims were in the Bashundhara house
harm: Coerced marriage through threats and inducements; taken from the house by force to the airport without being told she was being flown to China
official_response: Airport APBn arrested the two Chinese nationals and Nayan Ali; others fled; evidence seized. The victim's mother filed a case at Airport police station under sections 6(1)/6(2)/7/8/10 of the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act 2012.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Airport APBn SP (operations) Mohammad Mozammel Haque: this is the second recent arrest of Chinese nationals for trafficking at the airport; rings working with local brokers target simple, poor village women and try to traffic them to China with various inducements.
other_practical_details: Marriage to a foreign national was used as the trafficking vehicle rather than a job offer.
key_quote_bn: তারা মূলত গ্রামের সহজ-সরল ও দরিদ্র পরিবারের নারীদের নিশানা করে বিভিন্ন প্রলোভন দেখিয়ে চীনে পাচার করার চেষ্টা করছে।

headline_en: The dominance of broker rings must be stopped
amount_per_person: BDT 32,000 to raise the age on voter ID and passport (as admitted by a broker in the earlier report)
perpetrator_type: passport office brokers; editorial suspects insiders at the office
perpetrator_names: Gazipur Regional Passport Office (no individuals named)
how_victim_met_them: Computer shops in front of and around the passport office
how_it_was_discovered: Prothom Alo report on the Gazipur office
harm: Hours of queueing for ordinary applicants; document forgery for money
official_response: Deputy director claims brokers are not allowed inside; editorial says reality differs.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Prothom Alo editorial: remove the brokers' shops around the office, set up a help desk run by the passport office itself so applicants do not depend on outside shops, and investigate and punish insiders helping the ring.
other_practical_details: Editorial on the Gazipur passport office report; about passport issuance, not a migration case.
key_quote_bn: যে সেবা নাগরিক অধিকার হিসেবে সহজে পাওয়ার কথা, সেখানে তা আজও দালালদের হাতে জিম্মি।

headline_en: Pay the brokers and the work is fast, otherwise hardship
amount_per_person: BDT 1,000-1,500 extra to brokers to skip the queue; BDT 32,000 quoted to raise the age on both the voter ID and the passport (half in advance, passport within a month), BDT 2,000 more for delivery in 15 days
payment_method: half in advance (for the age-change offer)
perpetrator_type: passport office brokers working from computer shops outside the office
perpetrator_names: Broker Masum; Md Jony at 'Bismillah Computer' shop opposite the Gazipur Regional Passport Office (Paler Math, Joydebpur-Dhaka road)
how_victim_met_them: Brokers stand around the passport office every day and approach applicants; 25-30 small shops (the article also says over fifty computer shops nearby) fill in forms and pay the bank fee for applicants
trust_devices: computer shops right outside the office; brokers' clients visibly sent straight to the fingerprint and photo room in 10-15 minutes
timeline: Self-applicants: arrived 9am, finished 1:30pm; one could not even submit the file by 1:30pm and returned the next day (over 2 hours). Fingerprint and photo step alone 2-2.5 hours.
how_it_was_discovered: Reporter posed as an applicant wanting his age raised by one year
harm: Hours-long queues for those who do not pay; extra payments; forged age on NID and passport offered for money
official_response: Deputy director Nasrin Parvin said pressure of applicants had risen, that it should not take 2-3 hours, and that she does not allow brokers inside since she took charge.
other_practical_details: The article concerns passport issuance, not a migration case; it does not say the applicants were going abroad for work. An applicant, Riyad Mia, refused a BDT 1,000 demand and still got the work done without paying. Raising the age legally needs an NID correction that takes months; brokers offer it in 7 days to a month.
key_quote_bn: ভোটার আইডি কার্ডের বয়স ও পাসপোর্টে বয়স বাড়িয়ে দিতে ৩২ হাজার টাকা লাগবে।

headline_en: Demand to open the Malaysian labour market to all legal agencies
amount_per_person: BDT 152,000 per worker had to be paid to the syndicate last time (allegation in BAIRA members' memorandum)
amount_total: Agencies paid BDT 5 crore each to become syndicate members last time; BDT 14 crore each allegedly being collected this time
perpetrator_type: syndicate of selected recruiting agencies
perpetrator_names: Named in the memorandum as syndicate ringleaders: Amin Nur (Malaysian citizen of Bangladeshi origin), fugitive Ruhul Amin alias Swapan, and their Awami League associates
harm: Extra cost per worker passed through the syndicate
official_response: BAIRA members gave a memorandum to the Chief Adviser's Office (5 May 2025) and formed a human chain outside the expatriates' welfare ministry; an earlier memorandum signed by owners of 453 agencies was submitted to the ministry on 21 April.
other_practical_details: Memorandum's claims: Malaysia takes workers from 14 countries but selects specific agencies only for Bangladesh; the MoU signed under the previous government let the Malaysian government pick Bangladeshi agencies, which seeded the syndicate. Proposed alternative: BMET builds a database of interested workers, agencies recruit from it, workers deposit the government-fixed cost through a bank, BMET supervises. They also want Malaysia's online recruitment software cancelled. A linked headline says the Malaysia ring embezzled USD 200 crore (2 billion).
key_quote_bn: সিন্ডিকেটকে গতবার কর্মীপ্রতি ১ লাখ ৫২ হাজার টাকা করে দিতে হয়েছে। গতবার ৫ কোটি টাকা করে চাঁদা নিয়ে এজেন্সিকে সিন্ডিকেটের সদস্য করা হয়েছে। এবার ১৪ কোটি টাকা করে আদায় করা হচ্ছে।

headline_en: Brokers take young Bangladeshis to the Russia-Ukraine war with promises of jobs
destination_promised: North Macedonia (unnamed 20-year-old, sent to Russia instead); Russia for electrician and welding jobs (others)
route_and_actual_destination: Bangladesh -> Russia (all worked at the same company) -> dismissed -> picked up by Russian brokers at the airport or in Moscow -> Russian army camps -> front in Ukraine (Luhansk, Donetsk)
promised_job_and_wage: Electrician at 40,000-45,000 roubles a month (unnamed youth); welding at BDT 70,000 a month (Afzal Hossain Meraj). Second-stage lure by Russian brokers: Russian citizenship plus BDT 310,800 a month (Afzal); cleaner job at 200,000 roubles (Ayon Mondal); 'work' and visa renewal (unnamed youth).
amount_per_person: BDT 800,000 to the broker (unnamed youth); BDT 650,000 (Ayon Mondal)
perpetrator_type: local brokers in Bangladesh; Russian brokers approaching jobless workers at the airport and in Moscow
how_victim_met_them: Went to Russia through local brokers; after losing the job, a Russian broker approached them at the airport when they tried to fly home (or during 1.5 jobless months in Moscow, for Afzal)
trust_devices: a real job in Russia for the first 2-6 months; offer of Russian citizenship and a high salary; taken to a hotel with talk of work; passports and papers taken 'for visa renewal'; contract signed in front of 3-4 Russians; first put to cutting trees in a forest before weapons appeared
timeline: Unnamed youth: arrived Russia 8 August 2024; company expelled 15-20 workers after 2-3 months; went to the airport late February 2025; 5 days of weapons training after 20 March, to Ukraine on the sixth day; second operation in Luhansk about 7-8 April. Afzal: went 8-9 months earlier, worked 6 months, jobless 1.5 months, 3-4 days of training. Ayon: went 5 months earlier, stuck for one month.
how_it_was_discovered: After signing the contract they were taken to a forest to cut trees; a few days later guns and ammunition arrived and the four recruiters left. 'We understood they had sold us.'
what_happened_abroad: Minimal training (3-5 days loading and firing a gun), then sent to operations in Ukraine; missile and drone attacks; of 10-12 on one operation six returned and the rest are missing. Afzal has received no pay so far and now carries food and ammunition between camps. Ayon says those who refuse training are tortured; they use phones in secret and send voice recordings. Mohammad Akram Mia (22) was killed.
victims_count: Three interviewed; Afzal estimates 40-50 Bangladeshis have fought for Russia in Ukraine; 15-20 workers (mostly Bangladeshi, plus two Nepalis and two Indians) were expelled from the company together
victim_home_districts: Brahmanbaria (Ashuganj), Mymensingh (Trishal, Gouripur), Gazipur, Dhaka (Old Dhaka), Rangamati
harm: Deaths: Mohammad Akram Mia (22, Ashuganj, Brahmanbaria) and Yasin Mia Sheikh (22, Gouripur, Mymensingh, 27 March). Forced combat, unpaid, passports taken, several missing, no way back.
advice_or_warning_in_article: The three recruits blame the brokers for knowingly sending people to their deaths and ask young people not to fall for offers to come to Russia; they appeal to the Bangladesh government to bring them home.
other_practical_details: Destination switch: promised North Macedonia, sent to Russia. All three worked at the same company in Russia and were dismissed. Named Bangladeshis in the camps: Sohag Mia (Old Dhaka), Amit Barua (Rangamati), Ayon Mondal (Gazipur), Rubel (29), Imran Hossain (31), Md Mohsin Mia (26), Faisal Ahmed, Diganta Biswas. Family of Akram Mia learned of his death from a Bangladeshi fellow fighter by phone.
key_quote_bn: একপর্যায়ে ওই চারজন আমাদের রেখে চলে যান। বুঝতে পারি তাঁরা আমাদের বিক্রি করে দিয়েছেন

headline_en: Bangladeshi families search for sons who went to Russia and got caught up in the Ukraine war
destination_promised: Cyprus (job promised to Mohammad Akram Hossain and his brother-in-law, later switched to Russia); Russia, electrician at a Chinese company (Mohammad Yasin Sheikh)
route_and_actual_destination: Akram's group of 10: Bangladesh -> Saudi Arabia on Hajj visas (kept there several weeks) -> flown to Russia -> St Petersburg -> by bus to an army camp. Yasin: Russia, then Russian army, killed in the Ukraine war.
promised_job_and_wage: Job in Cyprus (unspecified); electrician at a Chinese company in Russia (Yasin). No wage stated.
visa_type_claimed: Hajj visa to Saudi Arabia as the first leg; told only a Russian work visa could be obtained
how_money_was_raised: Yasin took money from home to pay the broker; family says they spent 'a lot of money'
perpetrator_type: overseas recruitment firm (unnamed) and brokers; trafficking ring
how_victim_met_them: Akram and his brother-in-law registered with a firm that supplies workers abroad; Yasin went through a broker
trust_devices: registration with an overseas recruitment firm; claim that only a Russian work visa was available; contract written in Russian handed over on arrival, signed without understanding it
timeline: Yasin left Bangladesh September 2024, had to join the Russian army in December 2024, reported killed 27 March 2025. Akram's group taken to Saudi Arabia in September 2024, held several weeks, then flown to Russia; taken to an army camp, given uniforms the next morning.
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Russia: given a Russian-language contract, bused from St Petersburg to an army camp, handed a military uniform the next morning and sent to training
what_happened_abroad: Enlisted in the Russian army and sent to training for the Ukraine war. Akram escaped the camp with several Senegalese men before being sent to fight and flew home. His brother-in-law remains in the Russian army and phones home asking to be brought back. Yasin Sheikh (22) died in combat.
victims_count: A dozen families have contacted the Bangladesh embassy in Moscow; Akram's group was 10; a Bangladeshi newspaper citing security sources put the number fighting at over 100
harm: One death (Mohammad Yasin Sheikh, 22); forced military service; Akram spent several thousand dollars to get home
official_response: CID (SP Mustafizur Rahman): one Bangladeshi woman arrested for human trafficking; proceedings begun in six more cases; raids for other accused. Bangladesh embassy in Moscow (charge d'affaires Farhad Hossain) contacted Russian authorities and replied to about a dozen family requests. Russian authorities claim all who fought signed contracts and are paid.
other_practical_details: AFP report. Family learned of Yasin's death from a Bangladeshi friend also fighting for Russia, then from a Russian commander by phone; they are waiting for the body. India, Nepal and Sri Lanka nationals were recruited the same way with job promises.
key_quote_bn: তাই আমরা যেতে রাজি হয়েছিলাম। কিন্তু আমরা কখনো কল্পনা করিনি যে এভাবে আমাদের (যুদ্ধক্ষেত্রে) ফেলে যাওয়া হবে।

headline_en: First married over the phone, then put on a boat to be taken to the husband
destination_promised: Malaysia; good jobs for men and women, and marriage to a 'suitable' man for women
route_and_actual_destination: Rohingya camps in Ukhiya -> by vehicle to Kachchhapia hill, Baharchhara, Teknaf (held in a house) -> fishing trawler FB Kulsuma from Shaplapur/Kachchhapia beach -> was to pass St Martin's and Myanmar waters to Thailand, then be handed over onward to Malaysia. Actually intercepted by navy ship 'Durjoy' 44 nautical miles south-west of St Martin's Island and brought back to Teknaf.
promised_job_and_wage: 'Good job' in Malaysia (no wage stated); marriage to a man living in Malaysia
amount_per_person: BDT 30,000-50,000 taken from most passengers (police SI); the young woman's family had spent about BDT 50,000 up to boarding
perpetrator_type: trafficking brokers (several broker rings working in relay: taking people out of the camp, driving them to Teknaf, loading the trawler); a man in Malaysia presented as husband
how_victim_met_them: A broker proposed a 'suitable' groom in Malaysia to the parents in Balukhali camp (Camp-9), Ukhiya; one Bangladeshi driver was abducted at gunpoint by two men who hired his auto-rickshaw at Kotbazar
trust_devices: marriage conducted over mobile phone to a man in Malaysia the woman had never met; the supposed husband himself advising her to board; promise of good jobs
timeline: Phone marriage 3 April 2025; handed to broker morning of 5 April; trawler left about 2am on the night of 7 April; intercepted Tuesday afternoon (8 April); handed to Teknaf police 9 April. The abducted driver was taken 2 April, held 4 days, forced aboard 7 April.
how_it_was_discovered: Navy seized the trawler in the deep Bay of Bengal; the woman said she understood it was a mistake only after being caught
victims_count: 214 passengers (118 men, 68 women, 28 children), mostly Rohingya; at least one Bangladeshi
victim_home_districts: Cox's Bazar (Ukhiya camps; the abducted driver is from Kotbazar, Ukhiya)
harm: Money lost (BDT 30,000-50,000 each); confinement in hill huts; one man abducted at gunpoint and forced aboard; trawler had no life-saving gear and inadequate food and water
official_response: Navy seized trawler FB Kulsuma and handed passengers to Coast Guard, then Teknaf police. RRRC commissioner Mizanur Rahman: legal action against 12 of the rescued Rohingya involved in various crimes; the rest returned to camps.
other_practical_details: Staging point: huts on Kachchhapia hill, Baharchhara union, Teknaf, where 20-25 men and women were already being held. Many girls were 'married' by phone to men in Malaysia as the lure (SI Helal Uddin, Shah Porir Dwip police outpost). Second case in the article: an auto-rickshaw driver from Kotbazar, Ukhiya was hired by two passengers toward Marine Drive, held at gunpoint in a deserted spot, kept four days in the hill hut and forced onto the trawler.
key_quote_bn: অধিকাংশ নারী-পুরুষ থেকে দালাল চক্র হাতিয়ে নিয়েছে ৩০-৫০ হাজার টাকা করে।

headline_en: Expatriates returning empty-handed (editorial)
destination_promised: Abroad generally (attractive jobs promised by brokers)
promised_job_and_wage: 'Attractive job' once they arrive; nothing specific
visa_type_claimed: Many go on a visit (travel) visa and become irregular
amount_per_person: Average BDT 4,61,220 spent to migrate by people from Mathbaria, Pirojpur (OKUP/IIED study)
how_money_was_raised: Selling land or taking large loans; in the study 25% from land sales and 18% from high-interest loans
perpetrator_type: brokers
trust_devices: promise that an attractive job is waiting on arrival
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival: no job; on a visit visa they become irregular
what_happened_abroad: No work, or hidden work that barely covers their own costs; low or withheld pay, physical and mental abuse, restricted movement; arrested by police without passports and sent home empty-handed
victims_count: About 89,000 workers returned this way last year, over 80,000 the year before
harm: Debt, land lost, return with nothing
official_response: Editorial: no effective government initiative; no strong action against broker rings; cases are filed but the accused are not punished.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Prothom Alo editorial: unless the web of fraud is broken no welfare measure will work; calls for effective and lasting steps.
other_practical_details: BRAC Migration Programme: 250-300 workers return empty-handed each day and receive BDT 1,000 each for the trip home. 99% of surveyed workers faced at least one modern-slavery indicator, 81% more than five.
key_quote_bn: অনেকেই ভ্রমণ ভিসায় সেখানে গিয়ে ‘অবৈধ’ হয়ে যান।

headline_en: Went abroad to change their fortune, returning even poorer
route_and_actual_destination: Brunei, 2019; found no job; returned after 9 months
amount_per_person: BDT 5 lakh
how_money_was_raised: Mortgaged the family's shrimp farm for a loan; borrowed again to buy the return ticket
timeline: Went 2019; 9 months without paid work; shrimp farm still not redeemed in 2025
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival: there was no job
what_happened_abroad: Did all the household work in a Bangladeshi's home in exchange for food and lodging only, with no wages
victims_count: 1 main (Abdullah Rubel); a second individual case below
harm: BDT 5 lakh lost; shrimp farm still mortgaged; debt
official_response: No action on these cases. Article notes there are few programmes for returnees and none specifically for climate-displaced people cheated abroad.
advice_or_warning_in_article: OKUP chairperson Shakirul Islam: many forced abroad by climate damage are cheated and return poorer; developed countries and the Bangladesh government must take responsibility. OKUP/IIED study: people who borrow to migrate are forced to accept any work; 99% of workers faced at least one indicator of modern slavery (low or withheld pay, physical or mental abuse, restricted movement) and 81% more than five.
other_practical_details: Second case: Hasan Gazi of Shyamnagar went to Kuwait via India in 2018 on BDT 5.5 lakh borrowed from relatives, worked four years at various jobs, was arrested by police and sent home; now drives an auto-rickshaw in Keraniganj. Study: Mathbaria (Pirojpur) migrants spent on average BDT 4,61,220 to go abroad, 25% of it from selling land and 18% from high-interest loans. About 89,000 workers returned on out-passes last year after arrest (80,000+ the year before). BRAC Migration Programme: 250-300 workers return empty-handed each day and get BDT 1,000 each for travel home.
key_quote_bn: সেখানে গিয়ে কোনো কাজ পাননি। এক বাংলাদেশির বাড়িতে গৃহস্থালি সব কাজের বিনিময়ে থাকা-খাওয়ার সুযোগ পেয়েছিলেন। কোনো বেতন পেতেন না।

headline_en: Climate migrants falling into slavery
destination_promised: Mostly internal (Dhaka, Savar, Ashulia, Chattogram EPZ); overseas mainly Gulf countries, including Qatar construction
amount_per_person: IIED study: a household spends BDT 461,220 (Pirojpur) or BDT 413,667 (Sylhet) to send a member abroad
how_money_was_raised: Selling land or high-interest loans (IIED study)
perpetrator_type: Employers in Bangladesh and abroad (research finding; no individual perpetrator named)
timeline: Out-migration from the surveyed areas rose between 2011 and 2024
what_happened_abroad: The IIED study lists, for migrants abroad: confiscation of visa and passport, forced work, withheld wages, threats and beatings, excessive and unpaid work. One third of the overseas migrants in the study work as construction labourers in risky conditions; it calls Bangladeshi workers who built infrastructure for the 2022 Qatar World Cup victims of modern slavery.
victims_count: Survey of 648 households in 33 villages (10 unions of Mathbaria, Pirojpur and 9 unions of Gowainghat, Sylhet); 70.06% had a migrant
harm: Debt bondage: overseas migrants borrow to go and cannot realistically return before repaying; withheld wages, abuse, passport confiscation
advice_or_warning_in_article: IIED study: migrants are not aware of their rights and so are easily cheated; six recommendations including preventing abuse of migrants and creating safe migration routes. Ritu Bharadwaj (lead researcher, IIED): the government should start an advice helpline for migrants and a separate job registration system for them so they do not disappear into exploitative and unsafe work. Prof. Sharmind Neelormi (Economics, Jahangirnagar University): disaster-displaced people migrate without skills; construction workers who go abroad have little choice but to accept abuse and unbearable conditions. Shakirul Islam (chairman, Ovibashi Karmi Unnayan Program (OKUP)): there is no protection system for these migrants.
other_practical_details: The article is mainly about internal climate migrants (garment, brick kiln, construction, domestic work) based on the IIED study 'Exposed and Exploited: Climate Change, Migration and Modern Slavery in Bangladesh' (18 February 2025); the overseas part is a research pattern, not an individual case. The study says climate risk raised the likelihood of a household migrating abroad by 214% and internally by 161%, and that at least 92% of internal climate migrants end up in some form of modern slavery. Internal cases: Afzal Hossain (40) from Gowainghat, garment worker in Savar at BDT 7,500 a month, factory closed with wages unpaid; fisherman Bellal Khandaker (35) of Mathbaria left for a Chattogram EPZ garment factory with about BDT 500,000 of debt to a fish trader (advance) and NGOs.
key_quote_bn: টাকার জোগাড় হচ্ছে জমি বিক্রি বা চড়া সুদের ঋণের মাধ্যমে। আবার অভিবাসীরা তাদের অধিকার সম্পর্কেও সচেতন নয়, ফলে সহজে প্রতারিতও হচ্ছে।

headline_en: BDT 1,128 crore embezzled in the name of sending workers to Malaysia
route_and_actual_destination: Malaysia
amount_per_person: Government-fixed cost BDT 78,990; agencies allegedly took five times that in addition
amount_total: BDT 1,128 crore from 67,380 workers
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency (12 agencies owned by former ministers, MPs and their families)
perpetrator_names: M/s Orbitals Enterprise (owner Kashmiri Kamal, wife of former finance minister A H M Mustafa Kamal alias Lotus Kamal): 6,029 workers, BDT 100.99 crore. M/s Orbitals International (Nafisa Kamal): 2,995, BDT 50.17 crore. Snigdha Overseas Limited (former MP Nizam Uddin Hazari and wife Nurjahan Begum): 6,657, BDT 111.50 crore. Binimoy International (Abdus Sobhan Bhuiyan and wife Taslima Akter): 5,458, BDT 91.42 crore. Five M International (Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury): 7,124, BDT 119.33 crore. M/s Unique Eastern Private Limited (Mohd Noor Ali, wife Selina Ali, daughter Nabila Ali, former secretary Khondaker Shawkat Hossain): 3,788, BDT 63.45 crore. Catharsis International Limited (Mohammad Ruhul Amin and wife Lutfur Nesa Shelly): 7,787, BDT 130.43 crore. M/s Ahmed International (former MP Benzir Ahmed): 8,592, BDT 143.92 crore. BM Travels Limited (Shafiqul Islam and wife Mousumi Akter): 8,093, BDT 135.56 crore. BNS Overseas Limited (Ishtiaq Ahmed Saikat and wife Nasrun Nesa): 4,215, BDT 70.60 crore. Rubel Bangladesh Limited (Muhammad Mojibul Haque Rubel and wife Kamrun Nahar Hiramoni): 2,845, BDT 47.65 crore. The Ifti Overseas (Md Rubel and Borhan Uddin Panna): 3,797, BDT 63.60 crore.
victims_count: 67,380 workers
harm: Overcharged about five times the official cost
official_response: Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) filed cases on 11 March 2025 against 32 owners and officials of 12 recruiting agencies; announced by ACC director general Md Akhter Hossain.
verification_mentioned: The government-fixed cost for Malaysia was BDT 78,990 per worker (ACC)
other_practical_details: The agency names (spellings transliterated from Bangla: ওরবিটাল, স্নিগ্ধা, বিনিময়, ফাইভএম, ইউনিক ইস্টার্ন, ক্যাথারসিস, আহমদ, বিএম ট্রাভেলস, বিএনএস, রুবেল বাংলাদেশ, দি ইফতী) are licensed agencies that were part of the Malaysia syndicate; no RL numbers given in the article.
key_quote_bn: তাঁদের বিরুদ্ধে সরকার নির্ধারিত ৭৮ হাজার ৯৯০ টাকার স্থলে অতিরিক্ত পাঁচ গুণ অর্থ গ্রহণ করে ৬৭ হাজার ৩৮০ প্রবাসীর কাছ থেকে ওই অর্থ আত্মসাতের অভিযোগ আনা হয়েছে।

headline_en: Dream of going to Italy left Khurshed of Bhairab disabled; he has lost his homestead and everything
destination_promised: Italy, via Libya (broker to find him work in Libya until the crossing)
route_and_actual_destination: Libya from 14 June 2023; one year and eight months there; never reached Italy; returned to Bangladesh 13 Feb 2025
promised_job_and_wage: Work in Libya until the Italy crossing; got work as a painter. Later a shopping mall job promised at 1,400 dinar a month (paid half) and an oil company job at 1,200 dinar a month.
amount_per_person: BDT 4 lakh to reach Libya; BDT 9 lakh agreed with another broker for the sea crossing to Italy, of which BDT 6 lakh paid in two instalments
amount_total: BDT 19 lakh in all for the Italy attempt, plus several lakh on treatment
payment_method: Instalments
how_money_was_raised: Sold the land of his homestead
perpetrator_type: brokers (in Bangladesh and in Libya)
timeline: Left 14 June 2023; raid on 10 July 2024; a month jobless; four months at an oil company; three and a half months in hospital; home 13 Feb 2025
how_it_was_discovered: Paid BDT 6 lakh in two instalments for the sea crossing but was never sent; instead kept in holding houses that were raided
what_happened_abroad: Hid for two hours on a fourth-floor window ledge during a security raid; cheated of half his pay at a shopping mall after paying 500 dinar to get the job; held with 210 others at a holding site, where 160 were arrested in a raid while he hid four hours in a tree; jumped from a second floor when a mafia gang attacked the building the broker had moved him to, injuring arm and leg; untreated for five days, infection, five operations in a government hospital
victims_count: 1 (Khurshed Mia, 35)
victim_home_districts: Narsingdi (Ibrahimpur village, Belabo upazila); living in Bhairab, Kishoreganj
harm: Permanent disability (cannot walk, uses a wheelchair); BDT 19 lakh plus treatment costs lost; homestead sold; wife now works as a domestic help
other_practical_details: In Libya a job itself had to be bought (500 dinar for the mall job) and wages were then halved. Broker's men moved him from a private to a government hospital because they could not bear the cost. Returned with help from an individual.
key_quote_bn: দুই দফায় ছয় লাখ টাকা দিয়েও ইতালিতে পৌঁছাতে পারেননি তিনি।

headline_en: Trafficking of women across the Bangladesh-India border continues despite tighter controls
destination_promised: India (work; in one case 'learning dance' at BDT 50,000 a month; in another, work plus cheaper medical treatment; in another, domestic work)
route_and_actual_destination: Across the land border (around Benapole: Putkhali, Daulatpur, Gatipara, Sadipur, Rudrapur in Jashore; Maheshpur in Jhenaidah; Satkhira) into India; sold to brothels in Hyderabad, Maharashtra and Bengaluru
promised_job_and_wage: Dance training job at BDT 50,000 a month (three schoolgirls); unspecified work; domestic work
visa_type_claimed: None (irregular border crossing)
amount_per_person: Traffickers now take BDT 15,000-20,000 per person just to get someone across the border (Rights Jashore); women in brothels were told they had been bought for BDT 2-3 lakh
perpetrator_type: online contact; relative or neighbour; chain of handlers (bus conductor, house owner, auto-rickshaw driver, border guide)
perpetrator_names: Facebook ID 'Nil Pakhi' (belonging to a girl known to one victim and used by the girl's mother). Saudi case: Lamim Visa Care, Satkhira, owner Monirul Islam (arrested); M/s Siam Trade International, Dhaka, owner Md Rafiqul Islam (denies).
how_victim_met_them: Facebook message from an acquaintance's account; a neighbour woman; a cousin said to be working in Maharashtra; boyfriends or husbands in other cases
trust_devices: message came from a known person's Facebook ID; the acquaintance's mother helped arrange the trip; a cousin already working in India; love affair or marriage
timeline: Main case: trafficked two years ago, rescued by Indian police after two years. Schoolgirls: contacted January 2025, intercepted 10 Feb 2025. Cancer patient: trafficked 10 Oct 2024, rescued 21 Nov 2024. 15-year-old: trafficked 11 Feb 2025, rescued 23 Feb 2025.
how_it_was_discovered: Sold to a brothel on arrival in India; the three schoolgirls were stopped when BGB chased them at the Maheshpur border
what_happened_abroad: Sold into brothels and forced into sex work; one woman's six-month-old child was dangled from a balcony to force her compliance
victims_count: Several individual cases; Justice and Care: 186 women and children brought back and 133 rescued at the border between Jan 2024 and Feb 2025 (Jhenaidah, Chuadanga and Jashore only)
harm: Forced sex work, sexual violence, up to two years in captivity
official_response: One of the three girls filed a case at Maheshpur Police Station on 24 Feb 2025 under the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act 2012; no arrest. Home Ministry: 1,135 trafficking cases in 2024; about a third of accused arrested; in 2024 5 life sentences, 55 other sentences and 1,250 acquittals.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Under the trafficking law, sending someone inside or outside the country by deception in the name of work is human trafficking. Justice and Care country director Tariqul Islam: criminal rings always exploit instability. BGB Lt Col Saifullah Siddiqui: each person in the chain has a separate role, so victims cannot say who took them from where.
other_practical_details: Other case (Saudi Arabia): a Satkhira woman went on 21 Nov 2024 for a promised cleaning job, was instead placed as a domestic worker in a house and sexually abused; returned January 2025; filed a case in Satkhira court on 16 Feb 2025. Chain for the schoolgirls: Dhaka bus to Jhenaidah, conductor hands over to a man, a woman's house, battery auto-rickshaw to Maheshpur, a masked guide at the border. Rescued victims are handed over at the Benapole 'zero line'; BNWLA, Rights Jashore and Justice and Care assist survivors.
key_quote_bn: কাজ দেওয়ার কথা বলে তাঁকে ভারতে নিয়ে যাওয়া হয়েছিল। সেখানে যৌনপল্লিতে বিক্রি করে দেওয়া হয়।

headline_en: Cumilla Shibir leader calls the allegation of taking BDT 45 lakh baseless
route_and_actual_destination: Nepal (Kathmandu), where several people were held hostage; returned to Bangladesh
amount_per_person: BDT 45 lakh alleged by Tarek Aziz; Ashek Elahi says his own father paid BDT 40 lakh
payment_method: Ashek Elahi's account: his father paid BDT 40 lakh in cash and through the bank to Jobayer
perpetrator_type: disputed: complainant blames a neighbour and politician; the accused blames an individual who 'sends people to America' and a Nepali mafia ring
perpetrator_names: Accused by Tarek Aziz: Ashek Elahi (denies). Named by Ashek Elahi: Jobayer Hossain of Chhatarpaiya, Senbag, Noakhali, and Masud of Kishoreganj (both absconding).
how_victim_met_them: Disputed. Ashek Elahi says Tarek's father knew Jobayer and introduced him; Tarek says they never knew any Jobayer and the contract was with Ashek Elahi.
timeline: Group travelled to Nepal on 7 Dec 2023
how_it_was_discovered: Held hostage in Nepal; phones, passports and papers taken
what_happened_abroad: Several people held hostage in Nepal until families paid; released by the 'Nepali mafia ring' after payment (accused's account)
victims_count: Several (Tarek Aziz, and by his own account Ashek Elahi and others)
harm: BDT 40-45 lakh lost per family as claimed by each side
ransom_details: BDT 40 lakh paid by Ashek Elahi's father to Jobayer in cash and via bank, by his account
official_response: Human trafficking case by Tarek Aziz; all accused on bail. Ashek Elahi says complaints against Jobayer were lodged with Nepal police, the Bangladesh mission in Nepal and Motijheel Police Station, and that he has a court case to recover blank cheques and stamp papers taken from his family by force.
other_practical_details: Follow-up to the 1 March 2025 story (counter press conference on 3 March 2025). Shows how hard it is to establish who the contract was with when the deal is oral and made through neighbours.
key_quote_bn: টাকা পেয়ে জোবায়েরের নেপালি মাফিয়া চক্র আমাদের ছেড়ে দেয়। আমি নিজে তারেকের মতোই একজন ভুক্তভোগী।

headline_en: Allegation of taking BDT 45 lakh by holding a man hostage in Nepal on promise of sending him to the United States
route_and_actual_destination: Promised: legally to Nepal, visa from there, Brazil, then across the Mexico border into the US. Actual: flown to Nepal on 7 Dec 2023 and locked in a godown in Kathmandu; dumped on a Kathmandu road after payment; returned to Bangladesh on an out-pass on 23 Dec 2023.
visa_type_claimed: Visa to be obtained in Nepal for Brazil (no US visa; entry via the Mexico border)
amount_per_person: BDT 45 lakh
amount_total: BDT 45 lakh
payment_method: BDT 2 lakh up front with passport and papers; BDT 40 lakh to the bank account of the intermediary Rezaul Karim Ratan and BDT 3 lakh in cash, to be paid once the traveller confirmed he was in Mexico
perpetrator_type: relative or neighbour (next-door neighbour and politician) with a travel agency
perpetrator_names: Ashek Elahi of Taherpur village, Monoharganj, Cumilla (former president, Cumilla South district Chhatra Shibir; denies the allegation); Tourism Aid Limited, Farmgate, Dhaka; intermediary Rezaul Karim Ratan, businessman of Angaria, Laksam
how_victim_met_them: Neighbour approached the victim's father on 11 Nov 2023 saying he could send the son to America through a known agent
trust_devices: neighbour and known politician; taken to an agency office in Farmgate where the contract was made; balance payable only after arrival in Mexico was confirmed; money held through a local intermediary's bank account; first leg (Nepal) was a legal trip
timeline: Offer 11 Nov 2023; flew to Nepal 7 Dec 2023; home 23 Dec 2023 (16 days); case filed 9 May 2024
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Kathmandu he was locked in a godown and his phone, passport and papers were taken
what_happened_abroad: Held at gunpoint and forced to send his father a WhatsApp voice message saying he was in Mexico, which triggered the balance payment; then blindfolded and dumped on a road in Kathmandu
victims_count: 1 (Tarek Aziz); the accused says several people including himself were held
victim_home_districts: Cumilla (Khanatua village, Moishatua union, Monoharganj upazila)
harm: BDT 45 lakh lost; detention at gunpoint; threats to withdraw the case
ransom_details: The BDT 43 lakh balance was released on a coerced voice message; BDT 40 lakh to Rezaul Karim Ratan's bank account and BDT 3 lakh cash
official_response: Case filed 9 May 2024 against four people at the Dhaka Human Trafficking Offences Suppression Tribunal; arrest warrant issued for Ashek Elahi (he says he is on bail); investigation report submitted within a month and a half; case under trial. Returned from Nepal with help of Nepal police.
money_recovered: None. In arbitration Ashek Elahi signed a stamp paper to pay BDT 45 lakh plus BDT 1 lakh compensation but paid nothing, the victim says.
other_practical_details: The 'pay the balance only on arrival' safeguard was defeated by forcing the traveller to send a false arrival message. Accused says the real culprits are Jobayer Hossain of Senbag, Noakhali and Masud of Kishoreganj and that he was himself a victim.
key_quote_bn: পরে আমার মাথায় অস্ত্র ঠেকিয়ে ভয়ভীতি দেখিয়ে আমার বাবার হোয়াটসঅ্যাপে ভয়েস রেকর্ড পাঠাতে বাধ্য করে—আমি মেক্সিকো অবস্থান করছি।

headline_en: Youth dies of torture in Libya; body sent to Italy by boat
route_and_actual_destination: Dhaka direct to Dubai, a few days there, then Libya; taken hostage at the Libyan airport; died in a detention house in Libya on 14 Feb 2025; body put on a trawler to Italy with other migrants on 15 Feb
amount_per_person: BDT 16 lakh 'body contract' to reach Italy, after BDT 20 lakh ransom
amount_total: BDT 40 lakh taken in stages according to the father
payment_method: Cash in several instalments, collected in person by the broker Shipon Khan
how_money_was_raised: Sold the homestead and everything they had; borrowed from people and at high interest
perpetrator_type: village broker; Libyan 'mafia'; a Bangladeshi broker in Libya
perpetrator_names: Shipon Khan, son of Lalu Khan, Adityapur village, Madaripur Sadar
how_victim_met_them: Local broker lured him
trust_devices: 'body contract' guaranteeing delivery to Italy however long it takes, with food, lodging and air fare covered; broker kept telling the family he was alive
timeline: Left early August 2024; held and tortured about a week on arrival, then ransomed; died 14 Feb 2025; family learned on the night of 26 Feb 2025 from other migrants
how_it_was_discovered: Unable to reach him by phone, the family contacted other migrants from Bangladesh and learned on 26 Feb that he had died before reaching Italy and his body had been sent on the boat
what_happened_abroad: Taken hostage by mafia straight from the Libyan airport, tortured in a detention house, released after ransom, then held again and died of torture; not fed three meals
victims_count: 1 (Saidul Bepari, 23)
victim_home_districts: Madaripur (Khatopara village, Kunia union, Sadar upazila)
harm: Death; body not located; BDT 40 lakh lost; family destitute

official_response: Madaripur Sadar OC Md Moksedur Rahman: family told to file a written complaint, then investigation. Family says local elders are pressing them to settle for money. Broker claims the matter is settled and the death was an accident.
other_practical_details: 'Body contract': brokers take a fixed sum on a promise to deliver the migrant to Italy alive however long it takes, bearing food, lodging and air fare. Family alleges the broker takes youths to Libya, sells them to mafia for ransom, and sent the body by boat to disguise the death.
