key_quote_bn: এত দিন খালি সাইদুল বাঁইচা আছে, বাঁইচা আছে বলত।

headline_en: This Madaripur youth returned to his family after 104 days by paying ransom
destination_promised: Morocco on a work permit, then onward to Spain or Italy
route_and_actual_destination: Dhaka (14 Oct 2024) to Chennai (16-hour transit), Sri Lanka (one day), Dubai, Egypt (23 hours at the airport, passports taken and returned with Libyan visas), Benghazi, Tripoli (19 Oct). Sold to police on the way to the 'Algerian border', then handed to Libyan mafia. Returned to Bangladesh 26 Jan 2025.
promised_job_and_wage: Morocco work permit; no job or wage stated
visa_type_claimed: Morocco work permit; actually given a Libyan visa at Cairo airport
amount_per_person: BDT 17 lakh contract to reach Spain or Italy; BDT 4.5 lakh taken in cash up front
amount_total: BDT 33 lakh in all spent by his family in stages
payment_method: Cash BDT 4.5 lakh first; brokers collected the balance from the family while the victims were already in police custody, saying they were on the way to Morocco without phones
how_money_was_raised: Family sold land, gold, cattle and goats, mortgaged the house for an interest loan, and borrowed from relatives and neighbours
perpetrator_type: village broker (via a relative)
perpetrator_names: Broker 'Bombai' Ripon (Sardar); later broker Farhad in Libya
how_victim_met_them: Through a maternal uncle, after failing to obtain a work permit himself
trust_devices: introduced by his own uncle; air tickets and some dollars handed over in Dhaka; claim that the broker has people at every airport; told the Libyan visa was only for transit to Morocco via Algeria; family told he had no phone because he was travelling to Morocco
timeline: Left 14 Oct 2024; Tripoli 19 Oct; 5-6 days in a room; sold to police; five days with the mafia before the ransom demand; with broker Farhad from 18-19 Nov; home 26 Jan 2025; 104 days in total
how_it_was_discovered: At the airport in Egypt: after 23 hours the passports came back with Libyan visas, a country they were never supposed to go to. Confirmed when the driver stopped after 4-5 hours, got out and police seized them.
what_happened_abroad: Sold to police, phones taken; USD 1,000 paid to the broker ring to get out of police custody, after which police handed them to Libyan mafia. Held in a jail-like place with over 60 Bangladeshis; stripped, blindfolded and beaten on video sent home; fed a little noodles at noon and one piece of bread at night. Freed through another broker; later offered a sea crossing to Italy, refused, and returned via the embassy.
victims_count: 2 (Md Habibullah and Azad Hossain), joined by 2 more from Madaripur; 40-50 other Bangladeshis seen at the Egypt airport; 60+ in the mafia prison
harm: Torture, 104 days away, BDT 33 lakh lost, house mortgaged, heavy debt
ransom_details: USD 1,000 paid via the broker ring to be released by police; mafia demanded USD 5,000 per person; released after the family paid BDT 8 lakh per person through another broker (Farhad)
official_response: GD filed at the local police station; Bangladesh embassy contacted; returned after formalities. No arrest reported.
other_practical_details: Victim holds a master's degree and had tried for a legal work permit. Passports were collected at the Egypt airport and came back with a different country's visa. Brokers told the family the travellers had no phone so the balance could be collected. After release, the second broker offered the Mediterranean crossing to Italy.
key_quote_bn: ২৩ ঘণ্টা পর পাসপোর্ট হাতে পেয়েই বুঝতে পারলাম, প্রতারণার শিকার হয়েছি। কারণ, আমাদের লিবিয়ার ভিসা দেওয়া হয়েছে।

headline_en: Death from torture by broker ring in Libya; Russell never reached Italy
route_and_actual_destination: Libya; sold to a local broker ring on arrival; died there on 21 Feb 2025
amount_per_person: BDT 15 lakh paid to the broker for the journey
amount_total: About BDT 50 lakh in all according to the father and the union chairman
payment_method: Several instalments
how_money_was_raised: Sold the ancestral homestead and farmland; loans from relatives
perpetrator_type: village broker from the same village; Libyan 'mafia' ring
perpetrator_names: Lilu Mia of Dharmandal village, Dharmandal union, Nasirnagar
how_victim_met_them: Broker is from the victim's own village
timeline: Went to Libya early 2024; died 21 Feb 2025 (about a year)
how_it_was_discovered: After arrival in Libya he was sold to a local ring and torture videos were sent to the family; family learned of the death through an expatriate on 22 Feb 2025
what_happened_abroad: Sold to a local ring, tortured on video to extract money; when a further BDT 10 lakh could not be paid he was tortured and died. Father alleges he was killed with a poisonous injection.
victims_count: 1 (Md Russell Mia, 25)
harm: Death; about BDT 50 lakh lost; homestead and farmland sold
ransom_details: BDT 30 lakh extracted in several rounds using torture videos; a further BDT 10 lakh demanded a few days before the death
official_response: Nasirnagar OC Md Khairul Alam: legal action will be taken if the family files a written complaint. Broker has fled with his family.
other_practical_details: The article gives the father's name inconsistently (Laus Mia in one place, Awal Mia in another).
key_quote_bn: কিন্তু লিবিয়ায় পৌঁছানোর পর তাঁকে স্থানীয় দালাল চক্রের কাছে বিক্রি করে দেওয়া হয়। এরপর শুরু হয় নির্যাতন।

headline_en: One son on Russia's battlefield, another in a Malaysian jail; parents at a loss
destination_promised: Cyprus first; then a job in Russia
route_and_actual_destination: Left home 17 Aug 2024; taken to Saudi Arabia; after two months taken on via Dubai, Libya or Turkey (as the article puts it) to Russia; forced to the Ukraine battlefield to fight for Russia
promised_job_and_wage: Job in Russia (unspecified); originally Cyprus
visa_type_claimed: Cyprus visa applied for at the embassy; none issued in two years
amount_per_person: BDT 8 lakh paid to the agency
how_money_was_raised: BDT 4 lakh loan from an NGO, sale of his mother's and wife's jewellery, and money borrowed at interest; the father also mentions bank loan and selling cattle
perpetrator_type: agency or travel office (travel agency called a recruiting agency in the article; licence status not stated) (licence status not stated in article)
perpetrator_names: Dream Home Travels, Dhaka
trust_devices: agency submitted his papers to the Cyprus embassy for a visa; agency office in Dhaka
timeline: Waited about two years for a Cyprus visa; left 17 Aug 2024; about two months in Saudi Arabia; on the battlefield by Feb 2025
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Russia: kept in a military barracks, hair cut army-style and given combat training; messaged his wife 'bring me home at any cost'
what_happened_abroad: The broker took 10 Bangladeshis; one (Akram of Narsingdi) escaped and returned home; the other nine were forced to fight for Russia in Ukraine; one of them was killed and one shot
victims_count: 10 taken together; 9 sent to the front
victim_home_districts: Jashore (Boro Meghla village, Sadar upazila); also Narsingdi
harm: Forced into combat; one of the group dead and one wounded; family in debt and has sold livestock; BDT 8 lakh lost
official_response: Families of the nine held human chains in Dhaka, went several times to the Russian embassy and the Foreign Ministry, wrote to the Expatriates' Welfare Ministry and to the Chief Adviser's Office. No official action reported.
other_practical_details: Second case in the same family: younger brother Bazlur Rahman Sardar (30) was sent to Malaysia by brokers; after two years he came home sick, went back two months ago, and was arrested at work with over 100 others because of a fault in his papers. Nobody from his recruiting agency appeared, so his passport was red-stamped; held about a month and a half and to be deported.
key_quote_bn: বাকি নয়জনকে জোর করে রাশিয়ার পক্ষে যুদ্ধ করার জন্য পাঠানো হয় ইউক্রেনের যুদ্ধক্ষেত্রে।

headline_en: 24 missing in Libya on the way to Italy; relatives on hunger strike in Shariatpur seeking their whereabouts
route_and_actual_destination: Bangladesh to UAE, then Egypt, then Libya; to be sent by sea from Libya to Italy; missing in Libya since 21-22 March 2024
amount_per_person: BDT 12-20 lakh taken from each family (examples: BDT 18 lakh, BDT 20 lakh)
payment_method: Taken at various times in several payments
how_money_was_raised: One family sold land and a cattle farm; another is under heavy debt
perpetrator_type: unlicensed agency or travel office / village broker (runs a firm; licence status not stated)
perpetrator_names: Rashed Khan of Charjadabpur village, Angaria union, Shariatpur Sadar; his firm Lamisa Enterprise; several unnamed associates
how_victim_met_them: Rashed Khan and associates collected people from villages in Shariatpur and Madaripur; one victim left home in his company
trust_devices: has a firm (Lamisa Enterprise) and sends people to various countries; broker personally accompanied a victim from home
timeline: People taken from home in 2022 and 2023 (one left 3 Feb 2024); last contact 21-22 March 2024; still missing 15 Feb 2025 (about 11 months)
how_it_was_discovered: One victim phoned a few days after leaving to say they would be sent illegally by sea from Libya; contact stopped on the night of 22 March 2024 and the broker gives no information
what_happened_abroad: Some were arrested twice by police in Libya and jailed; some were held hostage and tortured; families paid to free them from captivity and jail; then all 24 went silent
victim_home_districts: Shariatpur (Sadar upazila), Madaripur (Sadar and Kalkini upazilas)
harm: 24 missing; BDT 12-20 lakh lost per family; debt; land and farm sold
ransom_details: Money taken from families to free some from hostage-taking and from jail in Libya; amounts not stated
official_response: 11 cases filed against Rashed Khan and associates in Shariatpur court and Palong Model Police Station, under the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act. CID arrested Rashed Khan in Jatrabari, Dhaka on 14 Feb 2025; sent to jail by Shariatpur Chief Judicial Magistrate court on 15 Feb; remand and bail hearing set for the following Monday.
other_practical_details: Victims named: Saiful (Suryamoni, Kalkini), Shahin Sikdar (26), Didar Hossain. Villages: Dakshin Madhyapara, Dakshin Bhashanchar, Natun Hat, Char Neyamatpur, Char Bhashanchar, Chapatali, Charchatang (Shariatpur Sadar); Jagir, Jafarabad, Tribhagadi (Madaripur Sadar); Suryamoni (Kalkini).
key_quote_bn: দালাল রাশেদ বিভিন্ন সময় আমদের কাছ থেকে ১৮ লাখ টাকা নিয়েছে।

headline_en: Allegation of embezzling BDT 60 lakh on promise of UK 'work permit visas'
route_and_actual_destination: Never left Bangladesh
visa_type_claimed: UK work permit visa (six visas)
amount_per_person: BDT 10 lakh per visa (BDT 2 lakh advance each)
amount_total: BDT 60 lakh for six visas (accused says the dealings were only BDT 16 lakh)
payment_method: BDT 12 lakh advance, then BDT 48 lakh in cash; the victim offered to pay by bank but the accused insisted on cash in hand
perpetrator_type: individual visa broker (neighbour from the same upazila)
perpetrator_names: Syed Ubaidur Rahman, of Dakshin Tajpur village, Osmaninagar, now living in Kuarpar, Sylhet city
trust_devices: photo of the visas sent on WhatsApp; has sent his own two sisters to England; part payment by cheque after arbitration
timeline: Agreement early 2022; visa photos sent a few months later; cheques given 21 July 2024; dishonoured again 10 Dec 2024; legal notice 12 Dec 2024; two cases filed 14 Jan 2025
how_it_was_discovered: After the full cash payment the passports were sent back by courier instead of being handed over in person, and there was no visa in them
victims_count: 1 complainant (S K Azad Amin) paying for six visas
harm: BDT 60 lakh lost (as alleged)
official_response: Two separate cases filed on 14 Jan 2025 in the Senior Judicial Magistrate Amoli Court No. 1, Sylhet; a further case for visa forgery in preparation. No arrest reported.
money_recovered: Through local mediation the accused gave six cheques of BDT 2 lakh each (BDT 12 lakh), which were dishonoured for insufficient funds. Accused claims he returned BDT 4 lakh through arbitration.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Victim: the accused has cheated many others the same way; called for his arrest to protect other would-be migrants.
other_practical_details: Red flags in this case: refusing a bank transfer and insisting on cash; showing the visa only as a WhatsApp photo; returning passports by courier rather than in person.
key_quote_bn: কিন্তু পাসপোর্টে কোনো ভিসা ছিল না। তখন তাঁরা প্রতারিত হওয়ার বিষয়টি বুঝতে পারেন।

headline_en: This death journey of the young must be stopped (editorial)
route_and_actual_destination: Libya, then by boat towards Italy; boat with 56 aboard sank in the Mediterranean on 25 Jan 2025, 23 bodies washed ashore
amount_per_person: BDT 15 lakh contract with the broker (Sujon Faraji took BDT 16 lakh from his aunt). Analyst Asif Munir: BDT 16-20 lakh per person.
how_money_was_raised: Sujon Faraji took BDT 16 lakh from his paternal aunt without telling his father, who had not agreed
perpetrator_type: village broker; domestic and international rings; editorial says some licensed recruiting agencies stand behind the brokers
perpetrator_names: Monir Sheikh of Majumdarkandi, Rajoir upazila, Madaripur
trust_devices: told they would be taken to Italy by ship
how_it_was_discovered: On the night of 24 Jan they were to be taken by ship but were put on a small boat instead
what_happened_abroad: According to Mintu Howlader (father of Hridoy Howlader, Kamarkhali, Faridpur), those who refused to board the small boat were shot dead and those who boarded drowned. Editorial also describes rings holding Italy-bound youths in detention camps in Libya and torturing them until relatives pay.
victims_count: 23 bodies from a boat of 56; at least 12 of the dead from Madaripur and Faridpur according to relatives
harm: Deaths by drowning and reportedly by shooting
ransom_details: Pattern only: families in Bangladesh pay large sums before captives in Libya are released; no amount
official_response: Embassy in Tripoli: 4,200 Bangladeshis freed from Libyan detention centres and sent home in a year and a half; more than a thousand irregular Bangladeshis still held. Editorial says past cases against agencies led to no action.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Migration analyst Asif Munir (to Deutsche Welle): domestic and international rings are involved; each person spends BDT 16-20 lakh and many then end up in danger, dead, imprisoned or held in camps. Editorial calls for zero tolerance towards the rings.
other_practical_details: Also mentions Humayun Kabir of Natore killed by a drone strike on the Russia-Ukraine battlefield. Figures cited: 84,000 Bangladeshis reached Europe by sea 2009-2024; on average at least 100 Bangladeshis drown each year.
key_quote_bn: যাঁরা উঠতে চাননি, তাঁদের গুলি করে হত্যা করেছে। যাঁরা উঠেছেন, তাঁরা ডুবে মারা গেছেন।

headline_en: Ministry's warning for those wishing to go abroad for employment
destination_promised: Middle Eastern countries, Russia, Greece, Libya, Lebanon, Egypt, Cambodia, Malaysia and others (well-paid work)
promised_job_and_wage: Good salary and work (unspecified)
visa_type_claimed: Tourist or visit visa used for work
perpetrator_type: fraudsters and broker rings; fake job adverts on social media
trust_devices: promise of high pay; job adverts on Facebook and YouTube
harm: Financial and mental loss, security risk, and deaths on irregular routes (as stated by the ministry)
official_response: Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment issued a public warning notice (reported 6 Feb 2025)
verification_mentioned: Ministry: confirm the job and the recruiting agency with BMET; check agency or employer information on the BMET website or through the Probashbondhu call centre; do not travel for work without BMET emigration clearance
advice_or_warning_in_article: Ministry notice: (1) do not go abroad for work on a tourist or visit visa on a broker's promise; (2) do not go for work without BMET emigration clearance; (3) confirm the job and the recruiting agency with BMET; (4) do not go through any person or organisation other than a valid recruiting agency; (5) under the Bangladesh-Malaysia MoU there is no scope for women workers to be employed in Malaysia; (6) verify agency or employer details from the BMET website or Probashbondhu call centre to avoid fake job adverts on Facebook, YouTube etc.
other_practical_details: There is no legal right to work on a tourist or visit visa. Any offer of a job in Malaysia for a woman worker is outside the MoU.
key_quote_bn: দালালের প্রলোভনে ট্যুরিস্ট বা ভিজিট ভিসায় কাজের উদ্দেশ্যে বিদেশ গমন না করা।

headline_en: 'Is this that game! I have neither my son nor my brother'
destination_promised: Italy (first on an agricultural visa, then by sea from Libya)
route_and_actual_destination: Left home 1 Jan 2025; Dhaka to Dubai to Libya; taken to the coast; boarded an engine boat from the Libyan coast on 24 Jan; boat with 56 aboard sank in the Mediterranean on 25 Jan 2025
visa_type_claimed: Agricultural visa for Italy (first broker, who failed to deliver)
amount_per_person: BDT 14 lakh contract with the first broker for the Italy agricultural visa (not stated whether per person). Police and locals: the ring takes BDT 18-25 lakh from each person.
perpetrator_type: village broker
perpetrator_names: Swapan 'dalal' of Mahendradi (police: Swapan Matubbar of Haridasdi village, Rajoir); Monir Hossain (police: Monir Howlader of Majumdarkandi village, Rajoir); Rafiq of Alipur, Bhanga upazila, Faridpur
trust_devices: promise of a legal agricultural visa first; broker's assurance they would reach Italy with no problem; victims phoned home saying all was fine and the 'game' would happen soon
timeline: Contract with first broker about a year and a half before Feb 2025; when he failed, new contract with a second broker for the Libya route; left 1 Jan 2025; boat left 24 Jan; sank 25 Jan; 23 bodies washed ashore 28-31 Jan
how_it_was_discovered: Family first heard of the nephew's death from the broker; then news came that the uncle was also dead; broker then became unreachable
what_happened_abroad: Boat sank before reaching Italy; 23 decomposed bodies washed up on the Libyan coast, almost all believed Bangladeshi according to the embassy in Libya
victims_count: 2 in the main case (Abul Basar Akon 32 and nephew Titu Howlader 19); boat carried 56; 23 bodies recovered; 8 more from Rajoir reported missing
victim_home_districts: Madaripur (Rajoir upazila: Gobindapur and Paschim Swarmangal)
harm: Two deaths in one family; bodies not located
ransom_details: None in this case; police and locals say that if caught by Libyan police or held by Libyan mafia, families have to pay several times more
official_response: Madaripur police investigating the broker ring; brokers in hiding. District administration working through the embassy to bring bodies home.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Article explains that the sea crossing from Libya in small overloaded boats is called the 'game' and many die every year.
other_practical_details: Pattern: a broker first sells a legal visa (agricultural visa for Italy), fails, and the family is then pushed to the Libya sea route through another broker. Related headlines in the text: Sumon of Bhairab died under broker torture in Libya; family claims two Faridpur youths were killed by brokers.
key_quote_bn: দালাল বলেছিল, কোনো সমস্যা ছাড়াই তারা ইতালি পৌঁছাবে। দালালকে এখন আর কোনোভাবেই খুঁজে পাচ্ছি না।

headline_en: Why kidnappings have risen in Teknaf
destination_promised: Malaysia (good jobs; marriage to suitable grooms), by sea
route_and_actual_destination: By sea from the Teknaf coast towards Malaysia; held at the Thailand or Myanmar border before reaching Malaysia while ransom is demanded from relatives in the Bangladesh camps
promised_job_and_wage: 'Good job' in Malaysia or marriage; no wage stated
perpetrator_type: trafficking brokers working in Rohingya camps; armed Rohingya groups with some local Teknaf residents
how_victim_met_them: Brokers recruit inside the Rohingya camps of Ukhiya and Teknaf
timeline: Sea trafficking rose again from January 2024 after six or seven years of near-stoppage
how_it_was_discovered: Ransom call to relatives in the camps once the person is held at the Thailand or Myanmar border
what_happened_abroad: Held at the Thailand or Myanmar border for ransom; if the family cannot pay, attempts are made to kidnap the family's members in Bangladesh
victims_count: At least 600 people (mostly Rohingya men, women and children) rescued during trafficking from the Teknaf coast in one year, along with 45 traffickers, in 8-9 operations. Over 500 young people sent to Malaysia from Lambashia camp in a year, of whom over 300 were caught and returned (camp leader Rafiq Ullah). Separately 193 people kidnapped for ransom in Teknaf in just over a year (86 Rohingya), at least 98 freed after paying.
victim_home_districts: Cox's Bazar (Rohingya camps in Ukhiya and Teknaf; Teknaf Sadar, Whykong, Hnila and Baharchhara unions)
harm: Captivity, ransom, kidnapping of relatives
ransom_details: For trafficking victims the amount is not stated. In a local kidnapping case BDT 7 lakh was demanded for a 6-year-old Rohingya boy; his father left BDT 50,000 and then BDT 1,60,000 in cash at places the kidnappers pointed out; the boy was dumped bound outside a hospital in Kutupalong camp.
official_response: 20 kidnapping cases at Teknaf Police Station in a year; 138 kidnapped people rescued; police preparing a combing operation in the hills; RAB-15 increasing surveillance.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Additional SP Md Jasim Uddin (district police spokesman): kidnapping for ransom in Teknaf revolves around human trafficking and drug smuggling. Balukhali camp leader Kamal Hossain: Rohingya are held at the Thailand or Myanmar border and ransom is demanded from relatives in the camps.
other_practical_details: Article is mainly about kidnapping for ransom inside Teknaf (drug trade, armed groups in the hills). Trafficking increases when the Bay of Bengal is calm. Victims who pay ransom usually do not report to police.
key_quote_bn: মালয়েশিয়া পৌঁছার আগে থাইল্যান্ড কিংবা মিয়ানমার সীমান্তে রোহিঙ্গাদের আটকে রেখে বাংলাদেশের আশ্রয়শিবিরে থাকা তাঁদের আত্মীয়স্বজনের কাছে মুক্তিপণ চাওয়া হয়।

headline_en: Three young men from Mathbaria tortured in Libya, ransom demanded
route_and_actual_destination: Bangladesh to Dubai (UAE), then Libya; held and tortured in Libya
promised_job_and_wage: Not stated; one father says the plan was to send money home and return after 4 years to buy his own vehicle
amount_per_person: BDT 300,000 contract when leaving home (article does not say whether per person or for all three)
amount_total: Yunus's family alone has paid BDT 15 lakh since he left, plus BDT 5,000 recently for food
how_money_was_raised: Lokman's wife sold 15 katha of land to raise the ransom
perpetrator_type: village broker and trafficking ring (families believe someone known to the brokers lives near their homes)
perpetrator_names: Not named; families refuse to name the brokers for fear of more torture
timeline: Left July 2023; contact lost after reaching Dubai; some time later called from Libya on imo saying they were being tortured; still held in Jan 2025 (about 18 months)
how_it_was_discovered: imo call from Libya telling the families they were being tortured and asking to come home, followed by ransom demands
what_happened_abroad: Held by the broker and fraud ring in Libya, tortured, threatened with death; given a little water and one piece of bread in 24 hours; appear skeletal on video calls
victims_count: 3 (Lokman Hossain 35, Md Yunus 34, Jasim 34)
victim_home_districts: Pirojpur (Noli Joynagar village, Sapleza union, Mathbaria upazila)
harm: Prolonged captivity and torture, starvation; land sold; BDT 15 lakh already paid by one family
ransom_details: BDT 12 lakh demanded per person; how and to whom paid not stated
official_response: Lokman's wife Rima Akter filed a case at Mathbaria Police Station in 2024 under the human trafficking law; investigation with the district Detective Branch. Pirojpur DC Mohammad Ashraful Alam Khan said the administration can do little but can write to the Foreign Ministry if the families complain.
other_practical_details: Families are afraid to speak or name brokers because the brokers have contacts near their homes and the captives may be tortured more. Money keeps being demanded after the first payment: one family has paid five times the original contract.
key_quote_bn: দালাল ও প্রতারক চক্রটি জনপ্রতি ১২ লাখ টাকা মুক্তিপণ দাবি করেছে।

headline_en: Travel agency accused of taking over BDT 1 crore
destination_promised: Europe (a European country of the candidate's choice); job not stated
route_and_actual_destination: Seven of them were taken to India and Nepal on 12 March 2024 for 'visa processing'; sent back to Bangladesh from India on 28 June 2024. Nobody reached Europe.
amount_per_person: Not given per person; BDT 80 lakh from 7 people, BDT 38 lakh from 4 people, BDT 9 lakh from 4 more
amount_total: BDT 1 crore 27 lakh from 15 people
perpetrator_type: agency or travel office (described as a travel agency / visa application centre; licence status not stated) (licence status not stated in article)
perpetrator_names: Agency not named in the article (called a visa application centre with its office in Gulshan, Dhaka). Owner M S Azizul Haque of Khuniapalong union, Ramu upazila, Cox's Bazar; his wife Safrin Haque is involved; manager Md Yunus.
trust_devices: office premises in Gulshan, Dhaka; taking candidates to India and Nepal for 'visa processing'; promise of a fixed deadline
timeline: Money paid about two years before Jan 2025. 12 March 2024: seven taken to India and Nepal. 28 June 2024: sent home from India. A few days before 8 Jan 2025 victims found the Gulshan office locked.
how_it_was_discovered: Complications arose in India/Nepal because of visa forgery and the group was sent home; later victims went to the Gulshan office and found it padlocked, and nobody answered the phone
what_happened_abroad: Seven spent about three and a half months in India and Nepal waiting for visas, then were sent back from India
victim_home_districts: Kishoreganj (Srinagar village and union, Bhairab upazila)
harm: BDT 1.27 crore lost; relatives who went to the owner's village home in Cox's Bazar were threatened with death
official_response: Victim Mamunur Rahman filed a case in the Dhaka Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court under the Overseas Employment and Migrants Act; under investigation by CID Dhaka (SI Farid Ahmed), report promised soon.
money_recovered: None; owner not refunding or answering calls. His wife Safrin Haque said they are trying to resolve it by sending people abroad or refunding.
other_practical_details: Victims named: Rustam Ali, Md Ibrahim Mia, Tarek Mia, Antor Mia (two of that name), Mobarak Mia, Usman Mia, Mamunur Rahman. Victims held a press conference at Natunbazar, Srinagar union, on 8 Jan 2025.
key_quote_bn: দুই বছর আগে এজেন্সির চাহিদামতো ভৈরবের ১৫ জন টাকা পরিশোধ করেন; কিন্তু তাঁদের কাউকে ইউরোপের কোনো দেশে পাঠাতে পারেননি।

headline_en: The story of stateless Faridul, 'imprisoned in the open jail' of Paris
destination_promised: Greece (Europe); broker contracted to get him as far as Greece
route_and_actual_destination: Dubai (worked there from 2003) to Oman by taxi with no passport or visa, boat with about 30 men to Bandar Abbas (Iran), taxi and bus to Turkey, Istanbul, sealed lorry to Greece (late 2010 to 2011); four years in Athens; late 2014 by bus to Macedonia, Serbia, Hungary, then Austria, Czech Republic, Germany (Bonn camp 2015-2018); Paris from 2018, where he remains undocumented
visa_type_claimed: None; travelled without passport or visa
amount_per_person: BDT 500,000 by verbal contract: BDT 50,000 advance, BDT 150,000 on reaching Iran, BDT 300,000 in Turkey
payment_method: Instalments by stage; the Iran instalment was deposited from Dubai by a cousin-type relative into an Iranian bank account given by the brokers; the balance was paid into a bank account given by the smugglers while he was held in Istanbul
perpetrator_type: Bangladeshi brokers abroad (smuggling network)
perpetrator_names: Nur Islam, broker from Noakhali (contracted in Dubai); Masum, Bengali broker who received the group at Bandar Abbas; an unnamed Bengali receiver in Istanbul
how_victim_met_them: Found the broker himself in Dubai after much asking around
trust_devices: pay-by-stage verbal contract; border guards and officials already paid off so crossings were smooth; good food and lodging for seven days in Iran; smugglers gave each person 60 euros when loading the lorry in Istanbul
timeline: Left Dubai late 2010; 7 days in Iran; caught and sent back six times on the way to Istanbul, succeeded the seventh time; over a month locked in a room in Istanbul; about 10 days in a Greek refugee camp; 4 years in Athens; 2015-2018 in Bonn; in Paris since 2018, asylum process 2018-2021 ended in refusal
how_it_was_discovered: Trouble began inside Turkey, where police took the group off buses six times; in Greece soldiers or border guards jailed them on arrival; years of refused asylum claims followed
what_happened_abroad: Faridul Alam (about 50, Gachhbaria village, Chandanaish, Chattogram) earned only BDT 10,000-20,000 a month as a day labourer in Dubai, so paid a broker to reach Europe. In Istanbul many people were packed in one room and not allowed out. About 100 people were put in a closed lorry meant for 25-30. In Greece he was jailed, then moved by UNHCR to a refugee camp and given a 'stay paper'. On the brokers' advice he claimed to be Rohingya in all Greek asylum applications; they were refused. He lived on one-month papers and a 'red card', hawking, with repeated police detention and seizure of goods, and could send nothing home. In 2014 he joined the Syrian refugee flow; Czech police took his money and papers and did not return them. German and French asylum claims were refused. He now cooks for a Bengali mess in La Courneuve, Paris, and sells caps and prayer beads outside a mosque on Fridays.
victims_count: 1 (travelled with about 30 others on the boat and about 100 in the lorry)
harm: BDT 500,000 paid; over 14 years undocumented in Europe with no savings and nothing sent home; never married; cannot return home because he has no passport
official_response: The Bangladesh embassy in Paris took his application and fingerprints, then after a long delay said it cannot issue a new passport unless he submits his old Bangladeshi passport, which he threw away when he left Dubai
advice_or_warning_in_article: The columnist (Dr Muhammad Muhsin, professor of English, University of Barishal) gives no formal advice; he appeals to the Paris embassy and passport officials to issue Faridul a passport so he can return home to die, and gives a French phone number for contacting him.
other_practical_details: Throwing away the passport to claim asylum left him unable to prove he is Bangladeshi years later; the embassy requires the old passport for a new one. Brokers coach migrants to claim Rohingya identity for asylum; it did not work in Greece, Germany or France. The Greek 'red card' avoided deportation but not police harassment. He discarded the Greek red card on entering Hungary. Twice he fell asleep on trains without a ticket and was taken off by police. The German camp gave 350 euros a month. The Dubai-Oman, Oman-Iran and Iran-Turkey crossings went smoothly because smugglers had arrangements with border staff. Published December 2024.
key_quote_bn: সেটি তো তাঁকে ফেলে দিতে হয়েছে দুবাই থেকে তাঁর যাত্রা শুরুর সঙ্গেই।

headline_en: Malaysia syndicate embezzled USD 2 billion
route_and_actual_destination: Malaysia
amount_total: USD 2 billion (BDT 24,000 crore) taken from about 550,000 workers, per RMMRU report
perpetrator_type: syndicate of recruiting agencies; foreign software owner; politicians (four MPs facing legal process)
perpetrator_names: Dato Amin (owner of Malaysia's foreign-worker recruitment software) and his Bangladeshi associate Ruhul Amin; four Bangladeshi MPs (not named in this article)
what_happened_abroad: Many workers found no job after arriving in Malaysia and lived destitute or were forced to return home
victims_count: about 550,000 workers sent through the syndicate
harm: Overcharged; many jobless and destitute in Malaysia or forced to return
official_response: Bangladesh government began legal proceedings against four MPs for links to the syndicate and wrote to Malaysia asking for the two ringleaders to be handed over.
advice_or_warning_in_article: RMMRU (founding chair Tasneem Siddiqui) recommended quick legal action against the chief organiser of the Bangladesh part of the Malaysia syndicate and the closely associated recruiting agencies; said a nexus of policymakers, senior bureaucrats and private actors has prevented good governance in migration.
other_practical_details: Source: RMMRU report 'Trends of labour migration from Bangladesh 2024', presented 28 Dec 2024 at the National Press Club. Report says no labour migration took place in 2024 to Oman, Bahrain, UAE, Maldives and some other countries; Italy stalled because of forged documents and Serbia because the application server was down. Jan-Nov 2024: 906,355 workers went abroad (2023: 1,305,453); 54,696 women.
key_quote_bn: সাড়ে পাঁচ লাখ কর্মী পাঠিয়ে ওই চক্র অভিবাসীদের কাছ থেকে ২০০ কোটি মার্কিন ডলার (২৪ হাজার কোটি টাকা) আত্মসাৎ করেছে।

headline_en: Attempt to extract ransom from hostages; 30 Rohingya rescued
route_and_actual_destination: Never left Bangladesh: gathered from Ukhiya and Teknaf Rohingya camps and held in the house of Saiful Islam, Dakshin Lombori Para, Teknaf Sadar union, Cox's Bazar. Intended route was by sea to Malaysia.
promised_job_and_wage: 'Good job' in Malaysia, or marriage; no wage stated
perpetrator_type: village broker / trafficking ring
perpetrator_names: Ring members not named; victims were held in the house of Saiful Islam, Dakshin Lombori Para, Teknaf Sadar union
how_victim_met_them: Brokers approached residents of the Rohingya camps in Ukhiya and Teknaf with offers of good jobs and marriage in Malaysia
how_it_was_discovered: Police raided the house on a tip-off on Saturday 14 Dec 2024 afternoon while ransom was being collected
victims_count: 30 (15 men, 3 women, 12 children)
victim_home_districts: Rohingya camp residents, Ukhiya and Teknaf, Cox's Bazar
harm: Held hostage for ransom
ransom_details: Ransom was being collected from the hostages' side; amount not stated
official_response: Teknaf Model Police Station rescued the 30; traffickers fled, no arrests. Refugee Relief and Repatriation Commissioner informed; rescued people in police custody pending his decision.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Teknaf OC Muhammad Gias Uddin: every winter brokers take Rohingya hostage for ransom in the name of sending them to Malaysia by sea; sometimes they put people on a big trawler, sail around for a few days, drop them somewhere on the Cox's Bazar coast and flee with the money.
other_practical_details: Typical trick described by police: victims are put on a trawler, kept at sea for several days, then landed back in Cox's Bazar while the traffickers disappear with the money. Season: winter (calm sea).
key_quote_bn: দালাল চক্রের লোকজন ভালো চাকরি ও বিয়ের প্রলোভন দেখিয়ে মালয়েশিয়া পাচারের উদ্দ্যেশে তাদের জড়ো করেছিল। পরে তাদের জিম্মি করে মুক্তিপণ আদায় করা হচ্ছিল।

headline_en: Young man allegedly trafficked to Libya in the name of Spain; case against 12
route_and_actual_destination: Libya; still there, out of contact
amount_per_person: BDT 1,500,000 contract, then about BDT 1,000,000 more; about BDT 2,500,000 in total
payment_method: Verbal contract; three instalments (29 August 2018, 20 November 2018, 10 January 2019), then further payments at various times
perpetrator_type: broker ring based in Sylhet city with agents at home and abroad
perpetrator_names: Faysal Mia (45) of Akhalia, Sylhet city, labour affairs secretary of Kalkalia Union Awami League, Jagannathpur; his brother Mokbul Mia (50); Hasan Nur, Saiful Islam, Salatur Rahman, Sirajul Islam, Samsul Islam and Jilu Mia of Sridharpasha, Jagannathpur; Enam of Asampur; Nazrul Islam of Tapoban, Sylhet city; Saleh of Daulatpur, Derai; Shahin of Parargaon, Jagannathpur
trust_devices: verbal agreement with a known local political figure
timeline: Verbal contract 15 August 2018; paid by 10 January 2019; court petition 27 November 2024; no contact with the son for three and a half months before the case
how_it_was_discovered: He was sent to Libya instead of Spain; ring members there tortured him and threatened to kill him unless more money came; videos and audio of the torture reached the family
what_happened_abroad: Held and tortured in Libya by ring members; death threats; the accused said he could not be brought home without more money
victims_count: 1 (Ali Hossain, 28)
harm: About BDT 2,500,000 lost; torture; missing for three and a half months
ransom_details: About BDT 1,000,000 paid to the accused at various times on the claim that he could not be brought home otherwise
official_response: Father Abul Haque petitioned the Sylhet Human Trafficking Tribunal on 27 November; Judge Md Saifur Rahman ordered Kotwali Model Police Station to record it as an FIR under the Prevention and Suppression of Human Trafficking Act and report by 2 March; case recorded 4 December 2024 against 12
money_recovered: None reported
other_practical_details: The father says he delayed filing a case for years out of concern for his son's safety.
key_quote_bn: প্রায় ২৫ লাখ টাকা আসামিদের দিয়েছি।

headline_en: Australia's work visa is getting easier
visa_type_claimed: Subclass 482 Temporary Skill Shortage visa, to be replaced by a 'Skills in Demand' visa
amount_per_person: 'Lakhs of taka' taken in the name of sponsorship (no figure)
perpetrator_type: fraud rings posing as arrangers of Australian sponsorship (not named)
trust_devices: misreading of real changes in Australian immigration law; eye-catching news of easier visas
verification_mentioned: Only an 'approved sponsor' authorised by Australia's immigration department can nominate someone for a work visa; proof of English is a mandatory condition (writer Kawsar Khan, immigration lawyer, Sydney)
advice_or_warning_in_article: Kawsar Khan, immigration lawyer in Sydney: there are precedents of lakhs of taka being taken in the name of sponsorship, so be very careful; do not think 'pay money and you can go to Australia'; anyone who says an Australian work visa is possible without proof of English should be treated as a fraud ring
other_practical_details: Explainer, no specific case. Proposed changes: one year of work experience instead of two, experience from any period, casual work counted. Proposed streams: Specialist Skills (about AUD 135,000 a year), Core Skills (about AUD 74,000), Essential Skills (lower-paid, possibly farm and construction workers). The writer says getting a sponsor from Bangladesh is very hard in practice and the changes mainly help students already in Australia.
key_quote_bn: আবার স্পন্সরের নাম করে লাখ লাখ টাকা হাতিয়ে নেওয়ার নজিরও রয়েছে।

headline_en: Protest and warning at Rajshahi passport office over broker files being processed first
perpetrator_type: passport brokers with passport office officials
perpetrator_names: Rajshahi Divisional Passport and Visa Office, Shalbagan, Rajshahi; Deputy Director Rozy Khandaker (denies all allegations), described by complainants as a member of the passport department's 'G-25' syndicate
how_it_was_discovered: Applicants in the queue saw broker files go straight upstairs and come back quickly
harm: Hours in the queue for people who apply on their own; extra payment to brokers
official_response: Human chain on 20 November 2024 under the banner 'suffering ordinary people of Rajshahi'; citizens' representatives gave the deputy director one month to fix it. Background: the Anti-Corruption Commission questioned 'G-25' members in 2021 and filed cases against some.
other_practical_details: Article is about passport issuance, not a migration case. Broker files are taken to the deputy director's room on the first floor, signed, entered on the computer by the assistant director there, then sent down for the photo. Applicants without a broker wait downstairs, where the entry desk is often unattended, and officers only look for mistakes in their files. 'G-25': 24 officials said in an intelligence report to collect at least BDT 2,500,000 in bribes a day.
key_quote_bn: দালাল না ধরে ফাইল আনলে শুধু ভুলই খোঁজেন কর্মকর্তারা।

headline_en: Promised Malaysia, held in the hills; 31 rescued including 27 Rohingya
destination_promised: Malaysia by sea (well-paid job for men, marriage to a good groom for women)
route_and_actual_destination: Never left Bangladesh; held in a hideout on a hilltop at Kachchhapia, Baharchhara union, Teknaf, Cox's Bazar
promised_job_and_wage: Well-paid job and better life (no figure)
amount_per_person: BDT 20,000 each
perpetrator_type: sea-route trafficking ring (local people of Ukhiya-Teknaf)
perpetrator_names: Arrested: Md Anwar (44) of Pankhali, ward 4, Hnila, Teknaf; Atikur Rahman (32) of Uttar Lambari, ward 2, Teknaf Sadar union
trust_devices: promise of job or marriage in Malaysia
timeline: One person held 8 days, another over 13 days; rescued on the night of Sunday 17 November 2024; boat departure had been planned for Monday 18 November
how_it_was_discovered: A local man, Ekhlas Mia, abducted on 12 November while visiting Kachchhapia on Marine Drive, escaped on 16 November when being taken to the beach for a trawler and went to RAB
victims_count: 31 (27 Rohingya, 4 Bangladeshi), including women and children
victim_home_districts: Rohingya camps in Ukhiya and Teknaf; Cox's Bazar (Ukhiya)
harm: Confinement, torture, little food, money extorted from relatives
ransom_details: Captives were tortured and made to phone relatives for money and to say they were already in Myanmar; money was taken from many this way (amounts not stated)
official_response: RAB-15 rescued the 31 and arrested two; case filed at Teknaf Model Police Station under the human trafficking law; police to seek five days' remand each
other_practical_details: The ring also abducted passers-by (Ekhlas Mia and his cousin) to add to the group. RAB: traffickers have been active since the Bay of Bengal calmed in September.
key_quote_bn: স্বজনদের বলতে বলা হয়, তাঁরা মিয়ানমারে আছেন।

headline_en: Case against four including a woman in Barishal for trafficking abroad and embezzlement
route_and_actual_destination: Dubai on a 7-day tourist visa, held by a local broker ring, handed to Dubai police and sent back; second attempt: taken to Teknaf for an irregular route, from where he escaped
promised_job_and_wage: Well-paid job in Dubai (wage not stated)
visa_type_claimed: Work visa promised; actually a 7-day tourist visa
amount_per_person: BDT 350,000 contract for Dubai, BDT 200,000 paid with the balance due after the visa; then BDT 400,000 demanded for Kyrgyzstan, BDT 200,000 more paid. Case alleges BDT 550,000 embezzled.
payment_method: Instalments
perpetrator_type: relative or neighbour (with associates in Dhaka)
perpetrator_names: Helal Uddin and Mokched Ali Akon of Guabaria union, Hizla, Barishal; Nilufa Begum of Ashulia, Dhaka; Md Saif Uddin of Demra, Dhaka
how_victim_met_them: Helal Uddin is the victim's neighbour
trust_devices: neighbour; agreement to pay the balance only after the visa; offer of a second country instead of a refund
timeline: Paid in 2021; sent to Dubai February 2021; case filed 13 November 2024
how_it_was_discovered: In Dubai, when a local broker ring held him and demanded money; the second time at Teknaf, when he understood he would be sent by an illegal route
what_happened_abroad: Held by a broker ring in Dubai who demanded BDT 100,000; when he could not pay they handed him to Dubai police, who sent him back to Bangladesh
victims_count: 1 (Abul Hossain)
harm: BDT 550,000 lost (as alleged); confinement; deportation from Dubai
ransom_details: BDT 100,000 demanded by the broker ring in Dubai; not paid
official_response: Case filed at Barishal Human Trafficking Tribunal; Judge Sohel Ahmed ordered the Hizla police OC to record the case, investigate and report
money_recovered: None; when he asked for a refund he was asked for more money for Kyrgyzstan
other_practical_details: When the victim asked for his money back the brokers offered a different country for an added payment, which led to a second loss.
key_quote_bn: হেলাল ও তাঁর সহযোগীরা আবুল হোসেনকে প্রতারণা করে সাত দিনের ট্যুরিস্ট ভিসায় দুবাই পাঠান।

headline_en: Two expatriate brothers and a sister-in-law jailed in Barishal human trafficking case
route_and_actual_destination: Kolkata, Delhi, Singapore and Fiji to Vanuatu; confined there; later offered onward travel to Australia, which never happened
promised_job_and_wage: Job in Cuba at BDT 80,000 a month
amount_total: BDT 2,100,000 paid jointly by the two men, then BDT 700,000 more for the Australia offer
payment_method: Paid in Bangladesh to the brother and sister-in-law of the man abroad; second payment to his brother and relatives
perpetrator_type: Bangladeshi already abroad, with family members in Bangladesh collecting the money
perpetrator_names: Palash Howlader (in Vanuatu, presented as living in Cuba); his elder brother Jasim Uddin Howlader (Qatar-based) and Jasim's wife Jannatur Rahman, of Rahutkathi, Babuganj, Barishal; co-accused Harun Or Rashid and Enamul Haque (trial stayed)
how_victim_met_them: Through a business acquaintance, Sajal Jamaddar, whose cousin Palash was said to live in Cuba and who was going himself
trust_devices: relative said to be living in the destination country; an acquaintance going at the same time; talked to the man abroad directly
timeline: Left 11 November 2017; case filed 18 November 2019; verdict 12 November 2024
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Vanuatu, when they were locked in an isolated house with others
what_happened_abroad: 10 people held in an isolated house, half-starved; some went to the police; Vanuatu police arrested Palash and rescued 103 more Bangladeshis from various districts; the two returned with IOM's help
victims_count: 2 in this case (Mofazzel Hossain and Sajal Jamaddar); 10 held together; 103 others rescued by Vanuatu police
harm: BDT 2,800,000 lost; confinement and hunger; death threats when they asked for the money back
ransom_details: BDT 700,000 taken while they were confined in Vanuatu, for a promised move to Australia
official_response: Barishal Human Trafficking Tribunal (Judge Md Sohel Ahmed): Jasim and Palash sentenced to life plus 14 years under two sections and fined BDT 4,500,000 (one more year in default); Jannatur sentenced to 17 years under two sections and fined BDT 1,000,000 (six months in default). The two brothers are fugitives. Defence will appeal.
money_recovered: None; the accused refused to refund and threatened to kill the victims
key_quote_bn: দেশে ফিরে টাকা ফেরত চাইলে আসামিরা টাকা ফেরত দিতে অস্বীকার করেন।

headline_en: Returned migrants tell their stories of hardship
route_and_actual_destination: Saudi Arabia; put to work at a petrol pump, then a date orchard
promised_job_and_wage: Cleaner at a bank in Saudi Arabia (wage not stated)
how_money_was_raised: Father's bank loan and borrowing from relatives
perpetrator_type: broker (not named)
timeline: Went in 2020; fell ill within two years; returned mid-2023
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Saudi Arabia: a different job
what_happened_abroad: Different work from what was promised, promised monthly wage not paid, earnings not enough to live on, fell ill from overwork, returned by more or less escaping
victims_count: 2 named: Md Shanto Khan (Saudi Arabia) and Islam Hossain (Oman)
harm: Loans still unpaid; illness; social and mental humiliation after return
advice_or_warning_in_article: Speakers at a BRAC Migration Programme workshop in Khulna: verify information before going; those who go through brokers are cheated most; many keep no proof of what they paid, so keep proof of every transaction
other_practical_details: Second case: Islam Hossain of Dumuria went to Oman, did not get the promised wage or job, was made to work 12 to 15 hours a day, stayed five years and returned in 2020 during Covid.
key_quote_bn: অনেকে বিদেশে যাওয়ার সময় যে টাকার লেনদেন করেন, তার প্রমাণও রাখেন না।

headline_en: Promised Malaysia, brokers left them on Inani beach
route_and_actual_destination: Fishing trawler from Teknaf; turned back on meeting the Myanmar navy south of St Martin's; 10 days at sea; put ashore at Inani beach, Ukhiya, Cox's Bazar
promised_job_and_wage: 'Good job' in Malaysia; women told they would be married there
amount_per_person: BDT 20,000 to 30,000 per head before boarding (Khurshida Begum paid BDT 30,000)
payment_method: Paid to the broker before boarding
perpetrator_type: sea-route brokers / trafficking ring
perpetrator_names: Not named for this boat. Arrested in a separate boat seizure at Shikalbaha, Karnaphuli: Fazal Karim alias Futu Majhi (47) of Kalamarchhara, Maheshkhali; Enamul Karim (37) of Jaliapalong, Ukhiya; Golam Hossain (40) of Cox's Bazar Sadar
timeline: 10 days at sea; landed about 4 am on 14 October 2024
how_it_was_discovered: Put ashore on Inani beach at dawn; the brokers then disappeared
victims_count: 110 to 120 Rohingya men and women; 26 detained, 80 to 90 fled
victim_home_districts: Rohingya from Ukhiya camps, Cox's Bazar (including Camp 17, Moynarghona)
harm: Money lost; 10 days adrift; detention
official_response: 26 detained and held by the Coast Guard; search for brokers and the others. 2016-2023: 1,134 people rescued from Malaysia-bound sea trafficking (95% Rohingya), 85 cases at Ukhiya and Teknaf police stations, 1,200 accused, 508 arrested.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Advocate Abdus Shukkur, Human Rights Defenders Forum Cox's Bazar: brokers target Rohingya, especially girls; over 20 trawler sinkings on the Malaysia route in recent years killed at least 300. Detained woman Khurshida Begum: trying to go to Malaysia by sea this way was a mistake.
other_practical_details: Traffickers are active from October-November to March when the Bay of Bengal is calm. Departure points named: Teknaf, Ukhiya, Ramu, Cox's Bazar Sadar, Maheshkhali, Anwara and Banshkhali coasts of Chattogram, and the Karnaphuli river. A separate trawler with 17 Rohingya from Teknaf's Mouchoni camp was seized at Shikalbaha, Karnaphuli.
key_quote_bn: আজ ভোরে দালালেরা সবাইকে ইনানী সৈকতে নামিয়ে দেন। এরপর দালালেরাও লাপাত্তা হয়ে যান।

headline_en: The imprisoned and missing young men must be brought back (editorial)
route_and_actual_destination: Libya; 9 returned, the rest held or missing
amount_per_person: BDT 1,100,000 each
how_money_was_raised: Savings and sale of land
perpetrator_type: broker ring (not named in the editorial)
what_happened_abroad: Taken to Libya and sold; held in a camp for a month and a half; beaten daily; fed once in 24 hours; given urine when they asked for water
victims_count: 26 men from 25 families
harm: Families destitute; torture; several imprisoned or missing in Libya
official_response: Editorial calls on the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare to trace and bring back those held or missing and act against brokers; says trafficking rings have stayed out of reach
advice_or_warning_in_article: Prothom Alo editorial: awareness must be raised so young people are not cheated when going abroad
other_practical_details: Editorial on the case reported on 21 September 2024 (26 men from Nasirnagar and Austagram); the 9 who returned did so after being detained by Libyan law enforcement.
key_quote_bn: ইতালি নেওয়ার কথা বলে তাঁদের লিবিয়া নিয়ে গিয়ে বিক্রি করে দেওয়া হয়।

headline_en: 26 young men sent to Libya in the name of Italy; 25 families ruined by a broker ring
route_and_actual_destination: Libya (Benghazi); none reported reaching Italy; 9 returned to Bangladesh from Libyan prisons, the rest held or missing
amount_per_person: BDT 1,100,000 each, paid in stages: BDT 400,000 before leaving, BDT 450,000 while held in a camp in Libya, BDT 250,000 for the boat 'game', plus BDT 120,000 each for air ticket and costs to come home
amount_total: Enamul Haque paid BDT 2,200,000 for two sons
payment_method: Instalments, the later ones demanded from families while the men were held in Libya
how_money_was_raised: Sale of farmland (BDT 700,000), loans (BDT 1,200,000) and savings
perpetrator_type: village broker (ring)
perpetrator_names: Farhad Mia (head), Mamun Mia and Arman Mia of Goalnagar village, and Sayedul Islam (Saidul Mia) of Simerkandi village, Goalnagar union, Nasirnagar, Brahmanbaria. Sayedul, Farhad's cousin, denies taking money.
trust_devices: broker from the same union; promise to reach Italy within a week
timeline: Went to Libya in 2022-23; held in a camp for a month and a half; sold two and a half to three months after the last payment; three months in prison; 9 returned between 7 August and 14 September 2024; two brothers out of contact for a year
how_it_was_discovered: An hour into the boat trip from Benghazi with 60 people on board they realised they had all been sold
what_happened_abroad: Held in a camp for a month and a half; beaten daily; one meal in 24 hours; two litres of salt water for washing and toilet; forced to clean a man named Ahammad's house from morning to evening, beaten with a pistol by his son; made to stand in the sun, given urine to drink; caught by the authorities after being put on a boat and jailed; Farhad got them out, took more money, then sold them. One man was sold four times.
victims_count: 26 men from 25 families; 9 returned; 7 named as missing
victim_home_districts: Brahmanbaria (Nasirnagar: Laluartuk, Dakshindia, Goalnagar villages), Kishoreganj (Austagram: Ratani village)
harm: BDT 1.1 million each lost; torture, forced labour, prison in Libya; several missing; families destitute and in debt
ransom_details: BDT 450,000 each taken by Farhad while the men were confined in the Libyan camp; BDT 250,000 more for the boat; BDT 120,000 each to get home
official_response: No complaint had been filed; Nasirnagar UNO Mohammad Imranul Haque Bhuiyan said he learnt of it from journalists and would act on a complaint. Families held a human chain demanding trial and compensation.
money_recovered: None reported
other_practical_details: 'Game' is the brokers' word for the boat crossing. Returnees contacted home from prison through a Pakistani man and a man from Bhairab.
key_quote_bn: নৌকাটি এক ঘণ্টা চলার পর তাঁরা বুঝতে পারেন, তাঁদের সবাইকে বিক্রি করে দেওয়া হয়েছে।

headline_en: Two brothers' dream of Italy ends in the Mediterranean
route_and_actual_destination: Bangladesh to Dubai on a visit visa, then Libya (confined in a room by Bangladeshi brokers), then an engine boat from the Libyan coast; the boat sank near the Tunisian coast
visa_type_claimed: Visit visa to Dubai
amount_total: BDT 3,000,000 contract for the two brothers
payment_method: Full contract amount collected after they reached Libya
how_money_was_raised: Borrowing (father speaks of debts)
perpetrator_type: village broker who is the local union parishad chairman
perpetrator_names: Md Farhad Matubbar, chairman of Gopalpur Union Parishad, Dasar upazila, Madaripur (alleged head of the broker ring; he denies it)
how_victim_met_them: Local union chairman persuaded the family
trust_devices: elected union chairman's word; promise to reach Italy within 15 days
timeline: Left 4 March 2024; boat left Libya 27 April with 70 migrants; family learnt of the deaths on 3 September, about four months later
how_it_was_discovered: A relative in Italy, Md Israfil, told the parents. Brokers had kept saying the brothers were alive and avoided every request to let the family speak to them by phone.
what_happened_abroad: Confined in a room in Libya, given dry food instead of rice; boat engine exploded near Tunisia and the boat sank; some swam to safety, the brothers and several other Bangladeshis went missing
victims_count: 2 brothers: Milon Munshi (35) and Al-Amin Munshi (33); 70 people on the boat
harm: Both brothers dead; BDT 3,000,000 lost; family in debt
official_response: Dasar police visited the home and asked the family to file a complaint, on which a case would be recorded. OC S M Shafiqul Islam said the chairman faced earlier trafficking allegations, is influential, has three sons in Italy and is said to run a large channel.
money_recovered: None reported
other_practical_details: The chairman says earlier trafficking cases against him were withdrawn by the complainants themselves. A video of him counting bundles of BDT 1,000 notes from young men for Italy went viral two years earlier.
key_quote_bn: কিন্তু এখন দেখি ট্যাকাও গেল, আমার দুই ছেলেও গেল।

headline_en: 24 Bangladeshis hostage in Libya after trying to reach Italy through a broker
route_and_actual_destination: Libya; none reached Italy; some held by kidnappers, some in Libyan prisons
amount_per_person: BDT 2,200,000 to 2,400,000 (Faruk Mia BDT 2,400,000; Shafiqul Islam BDT 2,300,000; Tofayel Ahmed and Sabuj Mia BDT 2,200,000 each)
amount_total: Several crore taka from 24 people (police)
payment_method: Handed over by the family to the broker
perpetrator_type: village broker (ring)
perpetrator_names: Rasel Mia, of Jagannathpur, Bhairab municipality, Kishoreganj, and associates (the 'Rasel ring')
trust_devices: broker rings in Bhairab have sent people to Italy via Libya for about 10 years and many earlier clients arrived
timeline: Faruk's father paid about a year before the report; Faruk set off about six months before; one family had no news of their son's location for three months
how_it_was_discovered: Calls from the captives to their families describing torture and asking for ransom; the broker and his associates then cut off contact
what_happened_abroad: Held hostage by kidnappers or jailed in Libya; beaten, denied food daily, large ransoms demanded
victims_count: At least 24
harm: BDT 2.2 to 2.4 million each lost; captivity and torture in Libya; none reached Italy
ransom_details: BDT 1,000,000 demanded to free Shafiqul Islam; large sums demanded for others; families say nobody can guarantee release after payment
official_response: On 5 July victims' families surrounded and beat Rasel at his home and handed him to police; a case under the human trafficking law was filed by victim's father Ebadullah and Rasel was sent to Kishoreganj district jail. Rasel admitted to police that he took the money.
money_recovered: None reported; appeals to local community leaders gave no result
other_practical_details: Rasel's explanation: new problems on the sea route meant he could not send everyone and people became impatient.
key_quote_bn: ইতালি পাঠানোর কথা বলে রাসেল ২৩ লাখ টাকা নিয়েছে। এখন ছেলেকে মুক্ত করতে চাচ্ছে ১০ লাখ টাকা।

headline_en: Worker numbers falling in the country that sends the most remittance (UAE)
route_and_actual_destination: Travelled to the UAE on visit visas; many found no job there
visa_type_claimed: Visit (travel) visa, to be converted to an employment visa through an employer after arrival
perpetrator_type: a 'ring' exploiting the visit-visa route, and brokers (not named)
trust_devices: a real UAE rule after Covid that let workers enter on a visit visa and convert to an employment visa
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival: no job
what_happened_abroad: Many workers found no work and lived on streets and in parks; converting the visa meant paying a broker again
harm: No job, homelessness, extra payments, irregular status
official_response: State Minister Shafiqur Rahman Chowdhury visited the UAE on 24 May and met employers on 25 May about sending more motorbike riders and drivers
advice_or_warning_in_article: BAIRA Secretary General Ali Haider Chowdhury: the UAE does not issue visas for unskilled work; it wants professionals, for which workers lack certificates. BAIRA Joint Secretary General Tipu Sultan: many who went on visit visas for work found none. OKUP Chairperson Shakirul Islam: those who went on visit visas had to pay brokers again for an employment visa; fraud at every step.
other_practical_details: A UAE employer linked to a worker who has become irregular is fined 50,000 dirhams, which makes employers reluctant to hire Bangladeshis. Monthly departures to the UAE: about 8,500 in 2022, 8,200 in 2023, 6,500 in the first four months of 2024. The UAE market was closed to Bangladeshis in 2012 after complaints.
key_quote_bn: ভ্রমণ ভিসায় গিয়ে কর্মসংস্থান ভিসা নিতে দালালকে নতুন করে টাকা দিতে হয়েছে।

headline_en: Benazir, the MPs' syndicate and the new landlords' hunger for wealth (column)
route_and_actual_destination: About 17,000 gathered at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport but could not fly to Malaysia
amount_per_person: BDT 544,000 actual cost against a government-set BDT 79,000; many paid BDT 550,000
amount_total: About BDT 20,000 crore taken illegally from 450,000 workers in a year and a half by the Malaysian and Bangladeshi syndicates
how_money_was_raised: Sale of homestead, gold and land; high-interest loans
perpetrator_type: recruiting agency syndicate in both countries, including four MPs
perpetrator_names: Not named
how_it_was_discovered: At Dhaka airport, when they could not board before the deadline
victims_count: About 17,000 who could not travel; 450,000 overcharged
harm: Families ruined; Tanvir (22) drowned in the Meghna on the way home
official_response: State Minister Shafiqur Rahman Chowdhury promised an inquiry and action against those responsible
other_practical_details: Opinion column mainly about corruption among the elite (former police chief Benazir Ahmed, MP Anwarul Azim); the Malaysia syndicate is one example. Only Bangladesh, among 15 source countries, had a selected-agency arrangement.
key_quote_bn: মালয়েশিয়া যেতে যেখানে সরকারের নির্ধারিত ব্যয় ৭৯ হাজার টাকা, সেখানে এই চক্রের কারণে সে ব্যয় বেড়ে হয়েছিল ৫ লাখ ৪৪ হাজার টাকা।

headline_en: Applications rejected for 'errors', all fine once you use a broker (Mymensingh passport office)
amount_per_person: BDT 2,500 above the government fee per 'channel file'; BDT 1,200 of it goes to the passport office, the rest to the broker
amount_total: At least BDT 500,000 a day taken at the Mymensingh passport office
perpetrator_type: passport brokers working from computer shops, with passport office staff
perpetrator_names: About 30 computer/photocopy shops in front of the Mymensingh Regional Passport Office, Maskanda, Mymensingh city (shops and staff not named)
how_victim_met_them: Applicants turned away at the counter go to the shops outside the office
trust_devices: fake 'nationality and character certificate' in the name of Mymensingh City Corporation carrying a handwritten broker code (three capital letters plus a number) that counter staff recognise
timeline: Azharul Islam was refused on two days from 24 April with new 'errors' each time; after going to the deputy assistant director on 28 April his application was accepted and he got the passport on 16 May
how_it_was_discovered: Complaint by applicant Azharul Islam to Prothom Alo, followed by five days of reporting at the office and shops
harm: Extra cost and repeated visits; correct applications refused without a broker
official_response: Deputy Assistant Director Bachir Ahmed said he would look into it; Deputy Director Morad Chowdhury said he did not know of the code system or of staff taking money and would inquire
verification_mentioned: An applicant who refused a broker went directly to the deputy assistant director and asked why a complete application was refused; it was then accepted
advice_or_warning_in_article: Deputy Director Morad Chowdhury: applicants are told to be careful of brokers outside the office. Ali Yusuf of SHUJAN Mymensingh: nothing gets done at the passport office without a broker; the administration should act.
other_practical_details: Article is about passport issuance, not a migration case. Brokers no longer roam outside the office; every shop offers the 'channel file'. The office keeps a daily count of coded applications and an office employee collects the money each Wednesday.
key_quote_bn: পাসপোর্ট অফিসে দালাল ছাড়া কাজ হয় না, এটি সবাই জানেন।

headline_en: In Libya one gang sold them to another gang
route_and_actual_destination: Dhaka to Dubai (held 2 days in a small house with 30-35 people), flight to Egypt (24 hours in a warehouse-like place near the airport), flight to Libya; never reached Italy; returned to Bangladesh
promised_job_and_wage: Job in Italy paying BDT 50,000 a month
amount_per_person: Azmir Hossain: BDT 600,000 (BDT 150,000 taken in advance, the rest he carried with him; the article also says BDT 600,000 was extracted from home by phone in stages). Abdullah Al Zobayer: BDT 400,000 taken from his family
payment_method: Instalments: advance handed to the broker, the rest carried by the migrant, then payments demanded from the family by phone
how_money_was_raised: Loans from relatives and sale of the family's cow
perpetrator_type: Bangladeshi already abroad (Libya-based) with relatives and friends at home
perpetrator_names: Sahadat (Shahadat) Hossain, Libya-based, from the same area; his brother Azad Hossain; Sajib; Azim; Nurul Karim; Bibi Zohura
how_victim_met_them: Sahadat, from the same locality, persuaded Azmir's mother; Zobayer was drawn in by his friend Azad Hossain, Sahadat's younger brother
trust_devices: broker from the same village; friend's word; promise of high wage
timeline: Azmir left on 21 March and reached home on 5 May (2024), 41 days after leaving; 8 days without food in a locked room
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Libya: passports seized, Sahadat's behaviour changed, beatings whenever a job was mentioned
what_happened_abroad: Passports taken; moved from place to place; beaten; family phoned for money; after the money was collected Azmir was sold to another group and left in the desert for handover, rescued by a Libyan and sheltered by a Bangladeshi acquaintance, then taken back by Sahadat; locked up and beaten after trying to escape; escaped through a broken window
victims_count: 2 named (Azmir Hossain, 24, and Abdullah Al Zobayer, 24); 30-35 people were held together in Dubai
victim_home_districts: Chattogram (Mirsarai upazila: Karerhat and Hinguli unions)
harm: BDT 600,000 and BDT 400,000 lost; BDT 600,000 debt; head injury and mental illness (Azmir), severe weight loss; Azmir's father had two strokes
ransom_details: Money demanded from families by phone while the men were confined and beaten: BDT 600,000 from Azmir's family in stages, BDT 400,000 from Zobayer's family
official_response: Azmir filed a criminal case in a Chattogram court against six people; the court took cognisance and ordered an investigation. Zobayer was preparing a case.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Victim Abdullah Al Zobayer: nobody should go to Libya through these traffickers; the gang targets people in Bangladesh and Bangladeshi workers in the Middle East, promising good jobs or Europe, then holds them hostage in Libya for money
other_practical_details: A union parishad member saw Azmir's injuries on a video call and phoned Sahadat several times to get him returned.
key_quote_bn: বাড়ি থেকে ছয় লাখ টাকা আদায়ের পর সাহাদাত আমাকে চড়া দামে আরেক পক্ষের কাছে বিক্রি করে দেন।

headline_en: Will the tears of Kalim, Belal and Tanvir melt stone (column)
route_and_actual_destination: Did not leave Bangladesh; turned back from Dhaka airport after the 31 May 2024 deadline
amount_per_person: BDT 550,000 to 700,000 paid to recruiting agencies; government-set cost is no more than BDT 79,000
how_money_was_raised: Interest-bearing loans (including from local 'samity' lenders), mortgaging the homestead, selling paddy land, cattle, goats and poultry, money from father and uncles
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agencies in Bangladesh and Malaysia (syndicate); at least four MPs said to have grown their business through the syndicate
perpetrator_names: No agency or MP named in this article
trust_devices: final BMET clearance; visa and approval
how_it_was_discovered: At Dhaka airport on the deadline day, when they could not get on a flight even after buying tickets at three to four times the price
victims_count: 16,970 with final clearance could not go (ministry and BMET); 31,304 in total held up by visa and approval problems (BMET source); about 40,000 (BAIRA officials); field sources say possibly over 100,000
victim_home_districts: Barishal (Mohammad Kalim), Cox's Bazar (Belal Hossain), Brahmanbaria - Akhaura (Tanvir Mia, 22)
harm: All money lost; debt on interest. Tanvir Mia fell from the door of the Upakul Express train into the Meghna at the Bhairab rail bridge on his way home from the airport and went missing. Kalim spoke of suicide.
official_response: State Minister for Expatriates' Welfare Shafiqur Rahman Chowdhury said an inquiry committee would investigate and action would be taken if anyone was found responsible
other_practical_details: Air tickets were sold at three to four times the normal price in the last days. Malaysia's market previously closed in 2009, 2016 and 2018 for the same syndicate reason.
key_quote_bn: সুদের ওপর ঋণ নিয়ে টাকা দিয়েছিলাম। এখন মালয়েশিয়া যেতে পারলাম না।

headline_en: Human Rights Commission orders on the Malaysia labour market situation
route_and_actual_destination: Workers with visas and clearance could not fly before Malaysia closed entry on 1 June 2024; thousands gathered without tickets at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Dhaka, on the last day
amount_per_person: An extra BDT 50,000 per passenger in the name of air fare (allegation)
amount_total: About BDT 150 crore from about 30,000 passengers in the last 10 days of May, in the name of air tickets (allegation)
perpetrator_type: recruiting agencies / vested-interest group (not named)
how_it_was_discovered: At Dhaka airport on the deadline day (Friday 31 May), when people without tickets could not board
what_happened_abroad: Allegation that workers were sent to name-only companies and found no work on reaching Malaysia
victims_count: About 30,000 passengers overcharged for tickets (allegation); a large number with visas and clearance could not travel
harm: Extra money lost; many could not travel despite visa and clearance
official_response: National Human Rights Commission took up the matter suo motu and ordered the Secretary of the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment to investigate, act against those responsible, arrange travel for workers with visas, and report by 10 July
other_practical_details: A related headline cited in the article says 17,000 workers with final clearance could not go to Malaysia.
key_quote_bn: প্রত্যেক যাত্রীর কাছ থেকে বিমানভাড়ার নামে অতিরিক্ত ৫০ হাজার টাকা নেওয়ার অভিযোগ উঠেছে

headline_en: To go to Malaysia some mortgaged land, some sold cattle
route_and_actual_destination: Stuck at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport, Dhaka; some who flew were held at the airport in Malaysia for lack of proper papers
visa_type_claimed: Worker visa
amount_per_person: BDT 500,000-600,000 paid to the 'company' (agency); Habibur Rahman paid BDT 550,000; average cost BDT 544,000
payment_method: Paid to agencies or brokers, often in parts and without money receipts
how_money_was_raised: Land mortgaged (Habibur: 16 decimals for BDT 100,000), cattle sold (four cows for BDT 450,000), bank loans, borrowing from relatives
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency; broker
perpetrator_names: An unnamed agency in Paltan, Dhaka (Habibur Rahman's); 101 agencies took approvals in all, none named
trust_devices: BMET clearance and visa obtained for many; assurance of being sent to Malaysia 'through another country'
timeline: Habibur mortgaged land a year earlier; came to the airport four days before the 31 May 2024 deadline
how_it_was_discovered: At Dhaka airport on and after 31 May 2024: no air ticket, or no work permit paper from the Malaysian company even after buying tickets at three times the price
what_happened_abroad: Some who reached Malaysia were held at the airport there for lack of proper documents
victims_count: 31,304 workers stuck over visa and approval problems (ministry and BMET sources); about 40,000 affected in all (BAIRA joint secretary general's estimate); several thousand turned back from the airport on 1 June
harm: Several lakh taka each paid and not travelled; land and cattle gone; debt
official_response: State Minister Shafiqur Rahman Chowdhury: those responsible will not be spared; an inquiry committee will be formed. BAIRA secretary general: trying to work out how many could not go, then discuss with the ministry.
money_recovered: None reported; many agencies cannot be reached by phone and some offices are shut
advice_or_warning_in_article: Shakirul Islam, chairperson, OKUP: recruiting agencies must take responsibility and return the principal with compensation, and the government must ensure it. Fakhrul Islam, BAIRA joint secretary general: agencies should refund 100% of deposits and the government can act to recover money paid to brokers.
other_practical_details: Of 524,946 workers approved by the ministry, BMET clearance was given for 493,642. Those without clearance had already paid the agency everything except the air fare. Ticket prices rose several-fold near the deadline. Many others had only begun (passport handed to the agency, medical done) and paid part amounts with no receipt.
key_quote_bn: তাঁরা অন্য দেশ দিয়ে মালয়েশিয়ায় পাঠাবেন বলে আশ্বাস দিচ্ছেন। কিন্তু সেখানে তো আর লোক নেবে না।

headline_en: The price of the government's wrong decision (editorial)
route_and_actual_destination: Several thousand workers with visas and job letters could not fly before Malaysia's 31 May 2024 entry deadline and stayed in Bangladesh
amount_per_person: BDT 500,000 to 550,000 taken from each Malaysia-bound worker by recruiting agencies of the two countries
how_money_was_raised: Sale of property and assets, borrowing
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agencies in Bangladesh and Malaysia (selected-agency syndicate)
perpetrator_names: No agency named. Bestinet, owner of the Migram software of Malaysia's Foreign Workers Central Management System (FWCMS), is said to play the main role; Bangladeshi agencies had to satisfy it to send workers
trust_devices: real visa; job letter / demand letter; fake appointment letters shown by Malaysian agencies
how_it_was_discovered: Workers holding visas and job letters could not travel by the 31 May deadline; others found on arrival that the appointment letters were fake
what_happened_abroad: Those recruited on fake appointment letters by Malaysian agencies are living in misery in Malaysia
victims_count: Several thousand who could not travel (no exact figure in this article)
harm: Money paid to agencies lost; families who sold assets or borrowed left ruined
official_response: Editorial says Bangladesh has taken no action; UN and EU have voiced concern; Malaysian High Commissioner in Dhaka said agencies of both countries are outside government control
money_recovered: None reported; editorial says agencies will not refund voluntarily and the government must take legal steps to force refunds
other_practical_details: Malaysia takes workers from 15 countries; for 14 it sets no condition of selected agencies, only for Bangladesh were a limited set of agencies selected, and Bangladesh agreed. Malaysia's market for Bangladeshis previously closed in 2009, 2016 and 2018.
key_quote_bn: দুই দেশের রিক্রুটিং এজেন্সিগুলো মালয়েশিয়াগামী প্রত্যেক তরুণের কাছ থেকে পাঁচ থেকে সাড়ে পাঁচ লাখ টাকা হাতিয়ে নিয়েছে

headline_en: Syndicate again and again, Malaysia labour market closed again and again
destination_promised: Malaysia, worker (Nayem Uddin was promised work in a tiles factory)
route_and_actual_destination: Malaysia
promised_job_and_wage: Tiles factory job promised; given construction labour for another company
amount_per_person: BDT 520,000 (Nayem Uddin, through a broker); government maximum BDT 78,990; study average BDT 544,000; listed agencies charge BDT 152,000-165,000 per worker just for use of their name
payment_method: Cash without receipts in all cases; part allegedly moved to Malaysia by hundi
how_money_was_raised: Loan on interest, repaid in instalments (Nayem Uddin)
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency (syndicate); broker
perpetrator_names: Aminul Islam bin Abdul Nur ('Amin Nur'), Bangladeshi-origin Malaysian citizen, owner of Bestinet, which owns the Migrams software of Malaysia's Foreign Workers Central Management System (FWCMS); Ruhul Amin alias Swapan, former BAIRA secretary general, alleged to be his representative in Bangladesh (denies everything). Agencies quoted: Five M International (MD Masud Uddin Chowdhury MP) and Sarkar International (owner Mohammad Ali Sarkar; 7,745 workers) - both say they took only the government fee.
timeline: Nayem went November 2023; work stopped after 15 days; kept two and a half more months in an office; then suddenly sent home
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival: different job, then no job
what_happened_abroad: Nayem Uddin of Narsingdi worked 15 days as a construction labourer, then the company stopped his work, kept him two and a half months in an office and sent him home
harm: BDT 520,000 lost, unable to pay loan instalments
official_response: Ministry is not running a separate inquiry; wants to raise it at the joint technical committee with Malaysia. A 2017 complaint to Bangladesh's ACC went nowhere because the accused were private-sector; a complaint to Malaysia's MACC was allegedly stopped by Amin Nur's influence. Malaysian High Commissioner Haznah Md Hashim: 'there may be a syndicate here beyond the control of both governments.'
verification_mentioned: Government-fixed maximum cost for Malaysia: BDT 78,990. Demand letters are allocated to listed agencies through the FWCMS software; the worker must go through the agency in whose name the demand arrives.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Tasneem Siddiqui (RMMRU): if Malaysia would not take workers outside the syndicate there was no need to send them.
other_practical_details: Listed agencies take written undertakings from the 'sub-agent' agencies that actually recruit, making them responsible if the worker gets no job, although the sub-agent appears in no government record - so the agency on a worker's papers may disclaim responsibility. State-owned BOESL sent workers at zero cost (employer pays) but got only 1,467 clearances by 24 April against demand for over 10,000, because its demand letters were diverted to other agencies. Earlier closures: 2009, 2018 (10-agency syndicate).
key_quote_bn: টাইলস কারখানায় কাজ দেওয়ার কথা ছিল, দিয়েছে এক কোম্পানির নির্মাণশ্রমিকের কাজ। ১৫ দিন পর তাঁর কাজ বন্ধ করে দেয় কোম্পানি।

headline_en: Malaysia labour market: four MPs' businesses boom after joining the 'syndicate'
destination_promised: Malaysia (worker visas; Selim's case: a promised job that is not specified)
route_and_actual_destination: Direct to Malaysia. Many arrived to no job; Selim was put on construction piling work instead of the promised job and came home after about six months.
visa_type_claimed: Regular work visa with BMET clearance, sent under the name of a syndicate agency
amount_per_person: Government-fixed cost BDT 79,000; actual average BDT 544,000 per worker (survey of 357 migrants in Malaysia, May to mid-Oct 2023, by Verite Inc. and four other organisations).
