'Syndicate fee' of at least BDT 150,000 per worker; three non-syndicate agency owners said they paid BDT 152,000 to 165,000 per worker to the syndicate agency.
amount_total: People in the sector estimate BDT 24,000 crore of business from about 450,000 workers in 18 months; about BDT 20,000 crore above the government fee; more than BDT 6,500 crore of that as syndicate fee
how_money_was_raised: Selim sold his own autorickshaw and his wife's jewellery and borrowed from people. Survey: 96% of workers took a loan from at least one source.
perpetrator_type: Licensed recruiting agencies in a 100-agency syndicate, owned by MPs, ruling-party leaders and a city councillor; alleged involvement of senior officials of both governments (UN experts)
perpetrator_names: Snigdha Overseas Ltd (MP Nizam Uddin Hazari, Feni; licence Dec 2018; about 8,000 workers in 18 months, 4th highest; executive director Shahela Parvin); Five M International (MP Lt Gen (retd) Masud Uddin Chowdhury, Feni-3; top sender, 8,592 clearances); Ahmed International (MP Benzir Ahmed, Dhaka-20, BAIRA president when the syndicate was formed; 7,849 workers, 5th); Orbitals Enterprise (Kashmeri Kamal, wife of former finance minister A H M Mustafa Kamal) and Orbitals International (daughter Nafisa Kamal), 9,861 together; Catharsis International (Ruhul Amin alias Swapan, former BAIRA secretary general, alleged leader who picked 69 of the 100 agencies and through whom money moved to Malaysia; 7,102 workers); Oishi International (2nd) and New Age International (3rd), said by sources to be active syndicate members; BNS Overseas Ltd (Ishtiaq Ahmed, son of BAIRA president Mohammad Abul Bashar); PR Overseas (son-in-law Golam Rakib; licence Oct 2021; over 4,000 workers); Sadia International (Shamim Ahmed Chowdhury); BM Travels Ltd (Md Shafiqul Islam, councillor of Dhaka North ward 39, Bhatara; 7,225 clearances); Ananya Apurba Recruiting Agency (Mohiuddin Ahmed, joint general secretary of Dhaka South city Awami League; licence July 2022; 2,600 clearances); Imperial Overseas (MD Mohammad Mahbubur Rahman; licence March 2021; over 7,000 in 18 months). No RL numbers printed.
trust_devices: licensed agencies selected by the Malaysian side; valid visa and BMET clearance; agencies owned by MPs and politically connected people
timeline: Market reopened July 2022 after about four years closed; about 450,000 BMET clearances in 18 months; Malaysia suspended intake and visa holders had to enter by Friday 31 May 2024. Selim went March 2023, was sick for about one and a half months, returned September 2023.
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Malaysia: no job, or not the promised job
what_happened_abroad: Many workers got no work. Selim (Narayanganj) was given piling work as a construction labourer, fell and injured his head, the company gave no treatment, he lay sick about a month and a half and bought his own ticket home. Long-term Bangladeshi residents say thousands are jobless: some sell goods on the footpath, some buy umbrellas from shops and resell them when it rains, some survive on odd jobs.
victims_count: Ministry count: 5,000 workers found no job; residents say thousands. 453 workers returned empty-handed between January and 24 March 2024, without passports, on travel permits.
harm: Debt and loss of assets, unemployment, untreated workplace injury, return with nothing and without passport
official_response: State minister for expatriates' welfare Shafiqur Rahman Chowdhury (11 May): Malaysia fixed the agency list; complaints are being looked into and those found guilty will face action. The article says the ministry never acted despite repeated syndicate and overcharging allegations and allowed a syndicate again in 2022. The ministry says work is being arranged for the 5,000. OHCHR statement of 19 April by UN experts. Malaysia suspended recruitment of foreign workers.
verification_mentioned: The official cost is BDT 79,000 per person; anything above that is over the government rate. Snigdha Overseas' executive director claimed they took nothing above the government-fixed cost.
advice_or_warning_in_article: UN experts (OHCHR, 19 April): many Bangladeshi workers in Malaysia are in miserable, inhuman and undignified conditions; large sums are taken with false job promises; senior officials of both governments are involved. Tasneem Siddiqui (founding chair, RMMRU): the risk that workers would end up in misery was known in advance, government offices knew, and the government should not have agreed to send workers through a syndicate.
other_practical_details: How the syndicate works: only selected agencies may send workers (25 at first, then 100 in three steps, chosen by Malaysia from a ministry list of 1,520 with no stated criteria). Agencies outside the syndicate that receive demand letters must send their workers under a syndicate agency's name and pay it BDT 152,000 to 165,000 per worker; part of that goes to the controllers in Malaysia. Two agencies confirmed sending through Imperial Overseas by paying the fee. Malaysia takes workers from 14 countries; only Bangladesh has a syndicate. Several syndicate agencies had almost no earlier record: Snigdha sent 100 workers in 3.5 years before joining, Ahmed International 238, Imperial 344 up to July 2022.

timeline: Taken 20 June 2014; arrested by Malaysian police as an illegal migrant in June 2017; one year in prison; brought home October 2018

victims_count: 2 (Nurul Islam and Helal Uddin)

headline_en: Maldives labour market closed again for Bangladeshis
route_and_actual_destination: Not sent; waiting for visas that are no longer being issued
amount_per_person: BDT 260,000 paid with another 200,000 due on visa (Monir Hossain, Chattogram); BDT 35,000 paid (Sheikh Alamin, Chandpur)
how_money_was_raised: Monir borrowed BDT 100,000 on monthly interest
perpetrator_type: broker; acquaintance
how_victim_met_them: Through an acquaintance / a known broker
timeline: Market opened Dec 2023, unskilled workers sent from Jan 2024, no new visas since April 2024; Monir was promised a visa in March
how_it_was_discovered: Visa never came; Bangladesh High Commission in Maldives issued a notice on 22 May 2024 that Maldives has suspended visas for Bangladeshi workers
victims_count: Not known; 6,436 people took BMET clearance for Maldives up to 22 May and a large share are stuck without visas
harm: Money tied up with brokers, interest on loans, uncertainty; broker still giving assurances
official_response: Maldives law caps workers from any single country at 100,000 and Bangladesh has filled the quota; the High Commission is trying to get the quota raised. Some unskilled workers were deported for working outside their approved employer.
verification_mentioned: High Commission notice: there is no scope to work for anyone other than the approved employer. Some workers went without the mission's attestation; they are being identified.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Bangladesh High Commission in Maldives (22 May notice): working outside the approved employer is illegal and has led to deportations. First Secretary (Labour) Md Sohel Parvez: no new visas since April because of the legal quota.
other_practical_details: Trick noted: Maldives gives Bangladeshi tourists a visa on arrival at the airport, and brokers use this to send workers without embassy attestation. About 100,000 regular and at least 30,000 irregular Bangladeshi workers are there; 96% went through relatives or brokers (RMMRU). Irregular workers earn less. 16,000 undocumented workers were forced home between March and December 2021.
key_quote_bn: বাংলাদেশের পর্যটকদের জন্য বিমানবন্দর থেকেই ভিসা দেয় মালদ্বীপ। এটির সুযোগ নিয়ে দালালেরা কর্মীদের সঙ্গে প্রতারণা করেন।

headline_en: Thousands of Bangladeshis helpless after coming to Canada on visit visas without understanding
destination_promised: Canada (hope of an LMIA-approved job after arriving on a visit visa)

visa_type_claimed: Visit visa

payment_method: Money brought from Bangladesh to Canada by hundi (for legal costs)
perpetrator_type: document-fixing rings in Bangladesh; smuggling ring inside Canada
trust_devices: fabricated financial and other supporting documents; fake invitation letters
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival: no LMIA-approved job found; documents re-checked at Canadian airports and those with fake invitation letters or documents sent straight back; some turned back at airports before reaching Canada

headline_en: Malaysia labour market closed again because of the syndicate
route_and_actual_destination: Malaysia
amount_per_person: BDT 400,000-500,000 on average; BAIRA joint secretary general says nobody went for less than BDT 450,000, against a normal cost of no more than BDT 80,000. BDT 150,000 per worker went to the syndicate.
amount_total: Syndicate took over BDT 6,000 crore from 400,000-plus workers; BDT 18,000 crore of business in a year and a half (BAIRA members)
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency (syndicate of 100 selected agencies) with a counterpart ring of private agencies in Malaysia
perpetrator_names: Dato Seri Abdul bin Amin Nur ('Dato Amin'), Bangladeshi-origin Malaysian citizen, owner of Synerflux [সিনারফ্ল্যাক্স], which got the online recruitment system contract in 2016; said to have helped form the syndicate both times. The 100 agencies are not named in this article.
timeline: Market reopened Aug 2022 after closing Sept 2018; no new approvals; visa applications accepted until 31 March 2024; last entry date 31 May 2024. Some workers jobless for months (one post says four months).
how_it_was_discovered: On arrival in Malaysia: many found no job
what_happened_abroad: Many workers got no job after arriving and have lived in misery for months; two Bangladesh High Commission officials (unnamed) say 150,000-200,000 Bangladeshi workers are jobless there and many come to the mission for help, which can do little
victims_count: 150,000-200,000 jobless in Malaysia (embassy officials' estimate)
harm: Unemployment and destitution abroad after paying four to five times the proper cost
official_response: Malaysia stopped approving new foreign worker applications (all source countries, from 1 June). State Minister Shafiqur Rahman Chowdhury says relations are good and problems will be solved gradually; ministry additional secretary says the syndicate issue is under consideration. Malaysian High Commissioner Haznah Md Hashim: one cause of the problem is the syndicate active in both countries.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Tasneem Siddiqui (RMMRU): agencies involved in earlier irregularities should have been held to account; this time those involved must be punished. BCSM (alliance of 23 migrant organisations): agencies, the Malaysian government and companies must be held accountable.
other_practical_details: Workers also paid for medical tests run under the same syndicate. In 2016-18 a 10-agency syndicate charged BDT 200,000-350,000 against an official cost of BDT 33,375 and took about BDT 5,500 crore in two years. 1,520 agencies were registered for Malaysia but only 25, later 100, were allowed; the MoU left the choice of agencies to Malaysia. Jobless workers post in the Facebook group 'Malaysia Probashi Bangladeshi' asking for work.
key_quote_bn: একজন কর্মী ৮০ হাজার টাকায় মালয়েশিয়ায় যাওয়ার কথা থাকলেও সাড়ে চার লাখের কমে কেউ যেতে পারেননি।

headline_en: Body of 'frustrated' youth who could not go abroad found cut by train
route_and_actual_destination: Never left Bangladesh
amount_per_person: BDT 600,000 lost to a broker for Romania; then engaged another broker for Italy at BDT 1.3 million
perpetrator_type: broker (not described further)
timeline: Lost the BDT 600,000 'a few months' before his death; had returned from Saudi Arabia about three years earlier
victim_home_districts: Sunamganj (Hargram, Jagannathpur); died at Kulaura, Moulvibazar
harm: BDT 600,000 lost; mental distress; Sajal Baidya (35) died under a train at Kulaura Junction station on 6 March 2024 - relatives and railway police believe it was suicide
official_response: Kulaura railway police handled the death; no action against the brokers mentioned
other_practical_details: A returnee from Saudi Arabia who tried twice through brokers to reach Europe and failed both times. The article does not say whether the Italy money was actually paid or lost.
key_quote_bn: কয়েক মাস আগে দালালের মাধ্যমে রুমানিয়া যেতে ছয় লাখ টাকা খোয়ান। এরপর ১৩ লাখ টাকায় ইতালি যেতে আরেক দালাল ধরেন।

headline_en: Bring every offender to justice (editorial)
destination_promised: Europe (lucrative jobs), per the Libya cases cited
route_and_actual_destination: Libya; some then by sea towards Italy
perpetrator_type: trafficking ring; Bangladeshi already abroad (Libya-based trafficker); official (airport immigration officer)
perpetrator_names: Mofizur Rahman and Ashraful Alam Bhuiyan (US embassy case); an unnamed Libya-based trafficker identified by CTTC
what_happened_abroad: Citing a Daily Star report (23 Feb 2024): many young Bangladeshis who went for work were brutally tortured by trafficking rings in Libya and freed only after relatives sent large sums from home. On 15 Feb a boat with 52 migrants caught fire and sank in the Mediterranean off Tunisia; 8 Bangladeshis died, 26 others rescued, one badly injured.
victims_count: 629 people rescued and brought back in 2022 by BRAC's migration programme after being taken to Libya on the promise of jobs in Europe; 8 Bangladeshis dead in the 15 Feb boat incident
harm: Torture, ransom, deaths at sea
ransom_details: Released only after relatives sent large sums from Bangladesh; amounts not stated
official_response: US embassy case against five Bangladeshis; Home Ministry figures: all accused acquitted in 316 of 332 trafficking cases disposed Jan-Sep 2023
advice_or_warning_in_article: Editorial: everyone concerned must stay alert so traffickers cannot send people abroad on fake papers, and every person involved must be punished. Salma Ali (BNWLA): ring members are influential and threaten victims into settlements.
other_practical_details: CTTC says one Libya-based trafficker has appointed 40 brokers across Bangladesh whose job is to find young people wanting to go abroad. UNHCR figure cited: 13% of 5,236 refugees and migrants who reached Italy by sea were Bangladeshi. Editorial, no new individual case.
key_quote_bn: দেশ থেকে স্বজনেরা মোটা অঙ্কের টাকা পাঠালেই কেবল তাঁরা ছাড়া পান।

headline_en: Five arrested at Shahjalal airport over sending people to Europe on fake visas
route_and_actual_destination: Planned: fly to Qatar on fake visas, then irregularly to France, Italy and Greece. Stopped in front of Terminal 2, Shahjalal airport, Dhaka, before departure.
visa_type_claimed: Fake visas (for Qatar); work permit and visa papers were among items seized
amount_per_person: BDT 1.6 million to 1.8 million each (16-18 lakh)
perpetrator_type: airport and airline staff ring; broker
perpetrator_names: Mohammad Asaduzzaman (security staff at Shahjalal airport) and Mohammad Kabir Hossain (booking assistant, Qatar Airways), described as the two ringleaders
trust_devices: visas (fake); e-tickets; work permit and visa documents; insiders at the airport and airline with a special airport entry card
how_it_was_discovered: Airport Armed Police Battalion got a tip that a ring was trying to send three people to Europe on fake visas; joint APBn-DB operation in front of Terminal 2 on Wednesday (21 Feb 2024)
harm: The three travellers (Jane Alam, Sabbir Mia, Samrat Saudagar) were themselves arrested for trying to travel on fake visas, after paying BDT 16-18 lakh each
official_response: Case filed for cheating and forgery against the five; court granted one day's remand. Seized: 3 passports, 3 fake visas, special airport entry card, phones, e-tickets, work permit and visa papers.
other_practical_details: DB says low-level staff of agencies working at the airport and private airline staff have long run a ring sending people to the Middle East, Europe and elsewhere on fake visas for lakhs of taka. The passengers carrying the fake visas were arrested along with the organisers.
key_quote_bn: এ জন্য দালালকে ১৬ থেকে ১৮ লাখ করে টাকা দিয়েছেন তাঁরা।

headline_en: US embassy files case against 5 Bangladeshis over human trafficking
route_and_actual_destination: One route stated: Bangladesh to India, then Suriname in South America, then across the Mexico border into the United States. Another: via Paraguay to the United States.
perpetrator_type: brokers; official (airport immigration officer allegedly paid)
perpetrator_names: Mofizur Rahman (54), Ashraful Alam Bhuiyan (33), Mohammad Zaman, Bhasani, and Mohammad Nur Alam (named as head of the ring)
how_it_was_discovered: During their own US visa interviews on 11 February 2024, Mofizur Rahman and Ashraful Alam Bhuiyan admitted working as brokers smuggling people; they had submitted fake documents and described themselves as garment businessmen
official_response: US embassy official Michael Lee [মিকাইল লি] filed a case at Gulshan police station, Dhaka; investigation assigned to DMP's Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit
other_practical_details: Per the case statement, Mofizur sent people to Dubai and, with other brokers, to the US, including his own brother via India, Suriname and the Mexico border. Ashraful said an immigration officer at Shahjalal International Airport helps him in exchange for money. Both took large sums for sending people to various countries (amounts not stated).
key_quote_bn: মানব পাচারে তাঁকে অর্থের বিনিময়ে শাহজালাল আন্তর্জাতিক বিমানবন্দরে একজন অভিবাসন কর্মকর্তা সাহায্য করেন বলে জানান।

headline_en: Expatriate smart card fraud again; BMET sees 'solution' in moving the server
destination_promised: Saudi Arabia (the 24 cards); not stated for the 20 cards
perpetrator_type: licensed recruiting agency; official (unidentified, BMET system access)
perpetrator_names: Cards were issued in the names of Alif Overseas (RL-847; owner Md Monirul Haque) - 24 cards on 31 Dec 2023; Bangladesh Export Corporation (RL-803) - 7 cards on 2 Jan and 1 on 3 Jan 2024; Saad International Limited [সাদ ইন্টারন্যাশনাল লিমিটেড] (RL-1068; MD Shamim Mahmud Patwari) - 7 cards on 1 Jan and 5 on 3 Jan. Alif Overseas and Saad International deny wrongdoing; Alif says it never applied for the 24 cards and that someone inside BMET may be involved. No one was finally held responsible by the inquiry.
timeline: 20 applications rejected in the Ami Probashi app between 27 Dec 2023 and 4 Jan 2024 were later cleared; inquiry committee formed 10 Jan, reported 7 Feb. The 24 cards of 31 Dec were noticed in the third week of January, reported in writing to the DG on 28 Jan.
how_it_was_discovered: BMET officials checking paperwork in the third week of January found no supporting data on the server for the 24 smart cards; the 20 app cards were found to have been approved after being rejected
victims_count: 44 smart cards (24 + 20)
official_response: Six-member BMET inquiry: 19 of the 20 rejected applications were approved from an Android phone via two IP addresses and one from the Additional DG's computer, where his ID and password were saved; the app has no session timeout and no OTP. Committee blamed no one finally and made 8 recommendations (OTP, session timeout, IT audit, store all Ami Probashi data on BMET's server). On 5 Feb the BMET DG wrote to DMP's cyber crime unit saying Alif Overseas took 24 emigration clearances by hacking the system; the DC said the letter had not yet arrived. BMET did not immediately cancel the 24 cards. BMET is moving its server to Bangladesh Computer Council.
verification_mentioned: Every worker going abroad legally must register with BMET and get a smart card (emigration clearance), issued in person by BMET and district manpower offices or online through the private 'Ami Probashi' app; all data sits on BMET's server. A related headline in the article refers to airports turning back workers over alleged fraud in BMET-issued smart cards.
advice_or_warning_in_article: Tasneem Siddiqui, founding chair, RMMRU: workers sent abroad without proper verification can be cheated; agencies in whose names cards were fraudulently issued should be investigated and punished if guilty.
other_practical_details: Rejected smart card applications can lawfully be approved after document checks by BMET's Director (Employment) or Additional DG (Employment). BMET officials say the old server software makes it impossible to stop the fraud or identify those involved.
key_quote_bn: এসব স্মার্ট কার্ডের বিপরীতে সংশ্লিষ্ট তথ্য খুঁজে পাওয়া যায়নি সার্ভারে।

headline_en: Pay attention to the safety of women migrants (editorial)
route_and_actual_destination: Saudi Arabia
perpetrator_type: foreign employer
what_happened_abroad: Editorial restating the pattern: women domestic workers forced to return because of illness, low or no pay, food and language problems and physical, mental and sexual abuse
victims_count: 3,000 women returned cheated and empty-handed in 2023 (citing Prothom Alo's own report)
harm: Abuse, unpaid wages, return empty-handed
official_response: Editorial says there are almost no examples of action against the recruiting agencies accused after women return abused and empty-handed
advice_or_warning_in_article: Editorial: returnees say the roughly one-month pre-departure training is not enough; many cannot read or sign their name and do not know the destination language, which makes going abroad extremely dangerous for them. Farida Yasmin (Supreme Court lawyer): women's protection is not separately covered in the amended migration law.
other_practical_details: Editorial with no individual case; based on the 13 Jan 2024 Prothom Alo report on falling numbers of women workers.
key_quote_bn: প্রায় অদক্ষ এবং প্রায় অশিক্ষিত এই নারীদের জন্য বিদেশবিভুঁইয়ে কাজ করতে যাওয়াটা অত্যন্ত বিপজ্জনক।

headline_en: Number of women workers falls even amid record overseas employment
route_and_actual_destination: Saudi Arabia
promised_job_and_wage: Domestic worker on a two-year contract; wage not stated
perpetrator_type: foreign employer
timeline: Lutfa Begum went in March 2020, worked 1 month 5 days, then about 3 months in a Saudi safe home before returning
what_happened_abroad: Lutfa Begum of Brahmanbaria had to work in two adjacent houses, could not eat the food, and the male household members behaved badly; she asked the person through whom she went for work elsewhere and did not get it; when she asked to go home she was sent to a Saudi government safe home. Pattern described: illness, low or no pay, food and language problems, physical, mental and sexual abuse; some return pregnant; most flee to the embassy safe home and are then moved to the Saudi government safe home.
victims_count: About 3,000 women returned empty-handed in 2023 (2,902 women among 86,621 workers who returned on outpasses without passports, counted by the Wage Earners' Welfare Board's Probashi Kallyan Desk at the airport; 249 women in December alone)
harm: Abuse; no wages paid (Lutfa received nothing for her work); early return empty-handed
official_response: Government officials: return is arranged at Saudi government expense from the safe home; if a worker wants to return within three months of arrival it is arranged through the Saudi recruiting company. Lutfa received BDT 30,000 cash assistance in two instalments after returning.
money_recovered: No wages recovered; BDT 30,000 cash assistance after return
advice_or_warning_in_article: Farida Yasmin, adviser, Bangladesh Obhibashi Mohila Sramik Association and Supreme Court lawyer: the amended migration law does not separately address women's protection; women abroad are still regularly abused. BRAC Migration Programme: abuse by employers of domestic workers in Saudi Arabia is not stopping; women are forced to return almost every month. Sector people: pre-departure training is compulsory for women going to Saudi Arabia but is sometimes skipped and its quality is questioned.
other_practical_details: No government agency counts returnees except those who come back on an outpass (travel permit) after losing their passport; that count is kept by the Probashi Kallyan Desk at the airport. 77,263 women went abroad in 2023 out of 1.3 million-plus workers; most women go to Saudi Arabia as domestic workers. BAIRA joint secretary general Tipu Sultan blames negative publicity and slow processing for the fall.
key_quote_bn: কোনো বেতন পাননি। তবে দেশে ফিরে দুই দফায় ৩০ হাজার টাকার নগদ সহায়তা পেয়েছেন।

headline_en: All accused acquitted in 316 human trafficking cases
route_and_actual_destination: Trafficked to Nadia district, West Bengal, India
perpetrator_type: trafficking ring (not described further)
timeline: Victim held 7 months in an Indian jail before returning; her father later spent 4 months in jail on a counter-case
what_happened_abroad: The 28-year-old woman from Savar was trafficked to Nadia, West Bengal, and spent seven months in a jail there before returning to Bangladesh
victims_count: 1 (main case)
harm: Victim jailed 7 months in India; her father, the complainant, was arrested on a false counter-case filed by the accused at Savar police station and jailed 4 months; family says BDT 500,000-600,000 was spent
official_response: Father filed a trafficking case; all accused acquitted, two of them now back in the area. Father says the investigating officer repeatedly said he would take him to court to testify but never did; the Savar SI says the case went to CID long ago. Home Ministry report (Nov 2023): of 332 Human Trafficking Prevention Act cases disposed Jan-Sep 2023, all accused were acquitted in 316 (95.18%), 12,279 accused acquitted; 56 people convicted in 16 cases, only 2 life sentences; no convictions at all in 2021 and 2022. 683 new cases in the 9 months; about 25,000 cases pending trial and 5,327 under investigation. Ministry issued an instruction on investigating the six stages of trafficking (who recruited, how the victim met the ring, the route used).
advice_or_warning_in_article: Salma Ali, president, Bangladesh National Women Lawyers' Association: trafficking cases are lucrative for police; investigating officers take money from both victim and accused and stall cases; ring members are influential and threaten victims into out-of-court settlements, so accused go unpunished. Experts: acquittals come from poor investigation, failure to produce witnesses, and paid settlements with the rings.
other_practical_details: Other cases in the article: (1) A 34-year-old Narayanganj woman went to Saudi Arabia in July 2022, promised domestic work at BDT 30,000 a month; she was physically and mentally abused; when her husband asked those who sent her to bring her back they demanded BDT 320,000; after she threatened suicide she was put out of the house and returned home. Husband filed a case at Hatirjheel police station on 24 Nov 2022 naming Saiful Islam, Md Rubel and Md Malek; investigation still unfinished (SI says he is waiting for information from several institutions). (2) A ring trafficked women to India using TikTok; one victim escaped back on 7 May 2021 and filed a case on 1 June at Hatirjheel naming 12 people, including Rifadul Islam alias 'TikTok Hridoy' (26); investigation unfinished after three years although accused arrested in India have already been convicted there.
key_quote_bn: ভারতে গিয়ে আমার মেয়ে সাত মাস জেল খাটল। আমি মামলা করার পর আসামিরা উল্টো আমার বিরুদ্ধে সাভার থানায় ভুয়া মামলা করেন।
